source: Written 2026-10-17 by Claude Sonnet and solved blind by Claude Opus (Claude Code agents, not runAi: no ai_runs rows), code-checked by lintQuestion; "checked" questions await a platform admin. Hand-written fixture questions are "approved".

notes.NC26.5.ANR.5: Fractions only in the forms the grade works with: unlike denominators with small common denominators (at most 24), mixed numbers add and subtract (no mixed-number multiplication), fraction x fraction, and division only of a unit fraction by a whole number or a whole number by a unit fraction. Every question is text only. Correct options that are fractions are written in LaTeX with compute left empty (the checker cannot parse LaTeX); each such key was verified exactly in the build script.
notes.NC26.5.ANR.4: Whole-number multipliers and divisors are kept at 4 or below, since the summary says 'within 4'.
notes.NC26.5.SGMR.1: Trapezoid is only ever described as having exactly one pair of parallel sides, so the answers do not depend on whether a trapezoid is defined inclusively or exclusively. Kites are not used. No figures are referred to.
notes.NC26.5.SGMR.2: All points are in the first quadrant with whole-number coordinates. No figure is referred to; every shape is given by its corner coordinates written out.
notes.NC26.5.RD.1: No figures: every line plot, bar graph and line graph is given as its list of data values, as the number of X marks above each value, or as the bar heights or points in words. Categorical data and data over time are covered in S1, planning and collecting in S2, choosing a graph in S3, and the three displays in S4-S7; S8 covers scales, labels and plotting without a picture. Fractions on line plots use denominators 2, 4 and 8 only. Ten skills, 9 questions each (3 at each difficulty). No mean, median or range vocabulary is used (the difference between the greatest and least values is asked in plain words).
notes.NC26.5.ANR.1: All expressions use whole numbers and the four operations. Most have two operations; a few at difficulty 3 have three (parentheses, or one multiplication and one division/addition). Representations (arrays, area models, tape diagrams) are described in words, never drawn. Properties covered: commutative, associative, distributive, identity and zero.
notes.NC26.5.ANR.2: Whole numbers go up to the millions (7 digits) and decimals to the thousandths, with the answers staying within those places. Powers of ten are 10, 100 and 1,000 and 10^2, 10^3. Everything is text only.
notes.NC26.5.ANR.6: Rules use only adding and multiplying (no subtracting or dividing rules), at the grade: whole numbers, with a few decimal steps (0.5, 0.75, 1.5). Every pattern is written out in the question or defined by a rule, so nothing refers to a graph or table. Several keys are checked by an exact expression in "compute"; the two "first position where A is greater" questions were checked by a simulation in the build script. The choice about the 6th number of the multiplying-by-10 pattern writes 100000 with thousands separators in LaTeX, so its compute is empty.
notes.NC26.5.SGMR.3: Text only. Customary and metric conversions within one system; the factor is stated in the question except for the metric prefixes in a few d2/d3 questions (1 km = 1,000 m, 1 m = 100 cm, 1 kg = 1,000 g, 1 L = 1,000 mL, 1 cm = 10 mm). Time is not used. Some answers are decimals (0.4, 2.5, 0.45) because the grade works with decimals to thousandths.
notes.NC26.5.SGMR.4: Text only: every prism is described by its measurements (whole numbers; units centimeters, inches, feet, meters). Volume is always in cubic units. No fractional edges. One question (the 216 cubic inch cube) needs the edge of a cube from its volume, answered by recognising 6 x 6 x 6; its compute is the answer itself.

questions.skill: Order of operations: multiplication before addition
questions.stem: Find the value of $6 + 4 \times 3$.
questions.solution: Multiply first: $4 \times 3 = 12$. Then add: $6 + 12 = 18$.

questions.skill: Order of operations: division before subtraction
questions.stem: What is the value of $30 - 12 \div 3$?
questions.solution: Divide first: $12 \div 3 = 4$. Then subtract: $30 - 4 = 26$. (Subtracting first would give 6, which is a common mistake.)

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: Which expression means "add 5 and 2, then multiply the result by 3"?
questions.solution: The adding happens first, so $5 + 2$ goes inside parentheses and the result is multiplied by 3: $(5 + 2) \times 3$. Without parentheses, the multiplication would be done first.

solve.work: Add 5 and 2 first needs parentheses: (5 + 2), then times 3: (5 + 2) x 3 = 21.

questions.skill: Order of operations without parentheses
questions.stem: What is the value of $5 + 2 \times 8$?
questions.solution: Multiply first: $2 \times 8 = 16$. Then add: $5 + 16 = 21$.

questions.skill: Order of operations without parentheses
questions.stem: Which number is the value of $20 - 3 \times 4$?
questions.solution: Multiply first: $3 \times 4 = 12$. Then subtract: $20 - 12 = 8$. The choice 68 comes from subtracting first ($17 \times 4$), 13 from subtracting 3 and then 4, and 32 from adding 12 instead of subtracting.

questions.skill: Order of operations without parentheses
questions.stem: Evaluate $9 + 18 \div 3$.
questions.solution: Divide first: $18 \div 3 = 6$. Then add: $9 + 6 = 15$.

questions.skill: Order of operations without parentheses
questions.stem: What is $16 + 12 \div 4$?
questions.solution: Divide first: $12 \div 4 = 3$. Then add: $16 + 3 = 19$. The choice 7 comes from adding first ($28 \div 4$), 28 from adding 16 and 12 and skipping the division, and 13 from subtracting 3 instead of adding.

questions.skill: Order of operations without parentheses
questions.stem: Calculate $30 - 4 \times 5$.
questions.solution: Multiply first: $4 \times 5 = 20$. Then subtract: $30 - 20 = 10$.

questions.skill: Order of operations without parentheses
questions.stem: A student works out $2 + 6 \times 5$. Which number should the student get?
questions.solution: Multiply first: $6 \times 5 = 30$. Then add: $2 + 30 = 32$. The choice 40 comes from adding first ($8 \times 5$) and 13 from adding all three numbers.

questions.skill: Order of operations with parentheses
questions.stem: What is $2 \times (3 + 4)$?
questions.solution: Do the parentheses first: $3 + 4 = 7$. Then multiply: $2 \times 7 = 14$.

questions.skill: Order of operations with parentheses
questions.stem: Which is the value of $18 \div (6 + 3)$?
questions.solution: Do the parentheses first: $6 + 3 = 9$. Then divide: $18 \div 9 = 2$. The choice 6 comes from dividing 18 by 6 first, then adding 3.

questions.skill: Order of operations with parentheses
questions.stem: Calculate $10 \times (7 - 2)$.
questions.solution: Do the parentheses first: $7 - 2 = 5$. Then multiply: $10 \times 5 = 50$.

questions.skill: Order of operations with parentheses
questions.solution: Do the parentheses first: $15 + 5 = 20$. Then subtract: $40 - 20 = 20$. The choice 30 comes from working left to right ($40 - 15 + 5$), and 60 from adding 20 to 40.

questions.skill: Compare the values of expressions
questions.stem: Which expression has a value of 20?
questions.solution: Find each value: $(2 + 3) \times 4 = 5 \times 4 = 20$; $2 + 3 \times 4 = 2 + 12 = 14$; $2 \times 3 + 4 = 6 + 4 = 10$; $2 \times 3 \times 4 = 24$. Only the first has a value of 20.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: Which expression shows "multiply 4 by 6, then add 7"?
questions.solution: Multiplying 4 by 6 gives $4 \times 6$, and then adding 7 gives $4 \times 6 + 7$. Because the multiplication comes first anyway, no parentheses are needed.

solve.work: Multiply 4 by 6 gives 4 x 6, then add 7: 4 x 6 + 7 (order of operations does the product first).

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: Which expression means "subtract 3 from 10, then multiply by 2"?
questions.solution: The subtraction $10 - 3$ happens first, so it needs parentheses: $(10 - 3) \times 2$. Without parentheses, $10 - 3 \times 2$ would multiply first.

solve.work: Subtract 3 from 10 is 10 - 3, which must be grouped before multiplying by 2: (10 - 3) x 2.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: Add 8 and 4, then divide the result by 3. What number do you get?
questions.solution: Add first: $8 + 4 = 12$. Then divide by 3: $12 \div 3 = 4$. As an expression this is $(8 + 4) \div 3$.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a story
questions.stem: Sam has 3 bags with 5 apples in each bag. He also has 2 loose apples. Which expression gives the number of apples Sam has?
questions.solution: There are $3 \times 5$ apples in the bags, and 2 more loose ones: $3 \times 5 + 2 = 17$.

solve.work: 3 bags of 5 is 3 x 5, plus 2 loose: 3 x 5 + 2 = 17.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a story
questions.stem: A hall has 4 rows of 6 chairs. Then 5 more chairs are put at the back. How many chairs are in the hall?
questions.solution: The rows hold $4 \times 6 = 24$ chairs. Adding the 5 at the back gives $24 + 5 = 29$.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a story
questions.stem: Lila had 20 stickers. She gave 3 stickers to each of 4 friends. Which expression shows how many stickers she has left?
questions.solution: She gave away $3 \times 4$ stickers, so she has $20 - 3 \times 4$ left.

questions.skill: Interpret an expression without calculating
questions.stem: Which sentence describes $3 \times (4 + 2)$?
questions.solution: The parentheses hold $4 + 2$, so that is done first. The sum is then multiplied by 3.

questions.skill: Interpret an expression without calculating
questions.stem: Which expression is 4 times as large as $7 + 5$?
questions.solution: To make $7 + 5$ four times as large, multiply the whole sum by 4: $4 \times (7 + 5)$. Without parentheses, $4 \times 7 + 5$ would multiply only the 7.

solve.work: 4 times as large as (7 + 5) is 4 x (7 + 5). 4 x 7 + 5 only multiplies the 7.

questions.skill: Commutative property
questions.stem: What number goes in the box to make the equation true? $8 + 5 = 5 + \square$
questions.solution: Numbers can be added in either order. $8 + 5 = 5 + 8$, so the box is 8.

solve.issues: Very easy for Grade 5 (a first-grade addition fact); fine only as a warm-up item.

questions.skill: Commutative property
questions.stem: Which equation shows the commutative property of multiplication?
questions.solution: The commutative property says the order of the numbers does not change a product: $6 \times 9 = 9 \times 6$. The others show the associative property, the identity property and the distributive property.

solve.work: Commutative property of multiplication swaps the order of factors: 6 x 9 = 9 x 6. A is associative, C identity, D distributive.

questions.skill: Commutative property
questions.stem: Mia knows that $17 \times 24$ equals 408. What is the value of $24 \times 17$?
questions.solution: Changing the order of the factors does not change the product. So $24 \times 17 = 17 \times 24 = 408$.

questions.skill: Associative property
questions.stem: What number goes in the box to make the equation true? $(4 + 7) + 3 = 4 + (\square + 3)$
questions.solution: Numbers can be grouped in different ways without changing the sum. On the left the numbers are 4, 7 and 3 in that order, so the box is 7. Both sides equal 14.

questions.skill: Distributive property
questions.stem: What number goes in the box to make the equation true? $4 \times 12 = 4 \times 10 + 4 \times \square$
questions.solution: Split 12 into $10 + 2$. Then $4 \times 12 = 4 \times 10 + 4 \times 2$, so the box is 2. Both sides equal 48.

questions.skill: Distributive property
questions.stem: Lena splits 13 into 10 and 3 to find $6 \times 13$. She calculates $6 \times 10 + 6 \times 3$. What is $6 \times 13$?
questions.solution: $6 \times 10 = 60$ and $6 \times 3 = 18$. Adding gives $60 + 18 = 78$.

questions.skill: Identity and zero properties
questions.stem: What number goes in the box to make the equation true? $47 + \square = 47$
questions.solution: Adding 0 to a number leaves it the same. The box is 0.

questions.skill: Identity and zero properties
questions.stem: What number goes in the box to make the equation true? $\square \times 29 = 29$
questions.solution: Multiplying a number by 1 leaves it the same. The box is 1.

questions.skill: Identity and zero properties
questions.stem: What is the value of $86 \times 0$?
questions.solution: Any number times 0 is 0. So $86 \times 0 = 0$.

questions.skill: Connect an expression to a representation
questions.stem: An array has 4 rows with 6 dots in each row. Which expression gives the number of dots?
questions.solution: Equal rows of dots are multiplied: $4 \times 6 = 24$ dots.

solve.issues: Very easy for Grade 5 (a Grade 3 array item); acceptable only as a warm-up.

questions.skill: Connect an expression to a representation
questions.stem: A tape diagram has 3 equal parts of size 8 and one more part of size 5. Which expression gives the total length?
questions.solution: The three equal parts give $3 \times 8 = 24$, and the extra part adds 5: $3 \times 8 + 5 = 29$.

solve.work: 3 equal parts of 8 = 3 x 8, plus one part of 5: 3 x 8 + 5 = 29.

questions.skill: Parentheses change the order of operations
questions.stem: Find the value of $36 \div (2 + 4)$.
questions.solution: Work inside the parentheses first: $2 + 4 = 6$. Then divide: $36 \div 6 = 6$.

questions.skill: Distributive property
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $7 \times (20 + 4)$?
questions.solution: The 7 multiplies both numbers in the parentheses: $7 \times 20 + 7 \times 4$. Check: $7 \times 24 = 168$ and $140 + 28 = 168$.

solve.work: Distributive property: 7 x (20 + 4) = 7 x 20 + 7 x 4 = 140 + 28 = 168. Others: 144, 560, 112.

questions.skill: Associative property of addition
questions.stem: What number goes in the box to make the equation true? $12 + (8 + 15) = (12 + \square) + 15$
questions.solution: Numbers can be grouped in a different way without changing a sum. On the right, 12 is now added to the first number of the pair, which is 8. So the box is 8.

solve.work: Associative property: 12 + (8 + 15) = (12 + 8) + 15, so the box is 8. Check: 35 = 35.

questions.skill: Order of operations without parentheses
questions.stem: Evaluate $125 - 4 \times 25$.
questions.solution: Multiply first: $4 \times 25 = 100$. Then subtract: $125 - 100 = 25$.

questions.skill: Order of operations without parentheses
questions.stem: Which is the value of $15 + 45 \div 5$?
questions.solution: Divide first: $45 \div 5 = 9$. Then add: $15 + 9 = 24$. The choice 12 comes from adding first ($60 \div 5$), 60 from adding without dividing, and 9 from dropping the 15.

questions.skill: Order of operations without parentheses
questions.stem: Calculate $100 - 8 \times 9$.
questions.solution: Multiply first: $8 \times 9 = 72$. Then subtract: $100 - 72 = 28$.

questions.skill: Order of operations with parentheses
questions.stem: Work out $60 \div (2 \times 5)$.
questions.solution: Do the parentheses first: $2 \times 5 = 10$. Then divide: $60 \div 10 = 6$.

questions.skill: Order of operations with parentheses
questions.stem: Which number is the value of $7 \times (15 - 9)$?
questions.solution: Do the parentheses first: $15 - 9 = 6$. Then multiply: $7 \times 6 = 42$. The choice 96 comes from doing $7 \times 15$ first and then subtracting 9.

questions.skill: Order of operations with parentheses
questions.stem: Tomas wrote $90 - (24 + 36)$ on the board. What is its value?
questions.solution: Do the parentheses first: $24 + 36 = 60$. Then subtract: $90 - 60 = 30$.

questions.skill: Order of operations with parentheses
questions.stem: What is the value of $96 \div (4 + 4)$?
questions.solution: Do the parentheses first: $4 + 4 = 8$. Then divide: $96 \div 8 = 12$. The choice 28 comes from dividing by 4 first and then adding 4, and 24 from dividing by only one 4.

questions.skill: Compare the values of expressions
questions.stem: Four expressions use the numbers 6, 2 and 3. Which one has the least value?
questions.solution: Find each value: $6 + 2 \times 3 = 12$; $(6 + 2) \times 3 = 24$; $6 \times 2 + 3 = 15$; $6 \times (2 + 3) = 30$. The least value is 12.

questions.skill: Compare the values of expressions
questions.stem: Which pair of expressions has the same value?
questions.solution: $2 + 3 \times 4 = 2 + 12 = 14$ and $4 \times 3 + 2 = 12 + 2 = 14$. In every other pair, the parentheses change the order of the steps and so change the value: 14 and 20, 10 and 4, 11 and 15.

solve.work: 14 vs 20; 12 - 2 = 10 vs 8/2 = 4; 11 vs 15; 2 + 12 = 14 vs 12 + 2 = 14. Only the last pair match.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: Which expression means "divide 36 by the sum of 5 and 4"?
questions.solution: "The sum of 5 and 4" is $5 + 4$, and it must be worked out before the division, so it goes in parentheses: $36 \div (5 + 4)$.

solve.work: The sum of 5 and 4 is (5 + 4); 36 divided by it is 36 / (5 + 4).

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: Which expression means "6 less than the product of 8 and 5"?
questions.solution: "The product of 8 and 5" is $8 \times 5$, and "6 less than" that is $8 \times 5 - 6$.

solve.work: Product of 8 and 5 is 8 x 5; 6 less than that is 8 x 5 - 6.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: Multiply 7 by the difference between 12 and 5. What is the result?
questions.solution: The difference between 12 and 5 is $12 - 5 = 7$. Then $7 \times 7 = 49$. As an expression this is $7 \times (12 - 5)$.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a story
questions.stem: A shop sells pens in packs of 8. Dev buys 5 packs and then uses 12 pens. Which expression shows how many pens he has left?
questions.solution: Dev buys $5 \times 8$ pens and uses 12 of them, so he has $5 \times 8 - 12$ pens left. That is $40 - 12 = 28$.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a story
questions.stem: Nia buys 3 notebooks that cost 4 dollars each and 2 pens that cost 3 dollars each. How many dollars does she spend in all?
questions.solution: The notebooks cost $3 \times 4 = 12$ dollars and the pens cost $2 \times 3 = 6$ dollars. In all she spends $12 + 6 = 18$ dollars.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a story
questions.stem: Four friends share the cost of a 36 dollar game and a 12 dollar poster equally. Which expression shows how much each friend pays?
questions.solution: The total cost is $36 + 12$, and it is shared among 4 friends, so each pays $(36 + 12) \div 4$. That is $48 \div 4 = 12$ dollars.

questions.skill: Interpret an expression without calculating
questions.stem: Without finding its value, which statement is true about $5 \times (123 + 456)$?
choices: It is 5 times as large as $123 + 456$
questions.answer: It is 5 times as large as $123 + 456$
questions.solution: The sum $123 + 456$ is multiplied by 5, so the expression is 5 times as large as the sum.

solve.answer: It is 5 times as large as $123 + 456$
solve.work: 5 x (123 + 456) is 5 groups of the sum, so 5 times as large as 123 + 456.

questions.skill: Interpret an expression without calculating
questions.stem: Maya uses $4 \times 6 + 2 \times 3$ for the cost of 4 notebooks at 6 dollars each and 2 pens at 3 dollars each. What does $2 \times 3$ stand for?
choices: The cost of all the items
questions.solution: The part $2 \times 3$ is 2 pens at 3 dollars each, so it is the cost of the 2 pens.

solve.work: 2 pens at 3 dollars each: 2 x 3 is the cost of the 2 pens.

questions.skill: Commutative property
questions.stem: Which pair of expressions are equal because of the commutative property?
questions.solution: Only addition and multiplication can be done in either order. $25 \times 4 = 4 \times 25 = 100$. Subtracting and dividing cannot: $25 - 4 = 21$ is not $25 + 4 = 29$, and $25 \div 5 = 5$ is not $5 \div 25$. Also $25 + 4 = 29$ is not $25 \times 4 = 100$.

solve.work: 25 x 4 = 4 x 25 by the commutative property (both 100). The others are not equal.

questions.skill: Commutative property
questions.stem: Which equation is NOT true?
questions.solution: Addition and multiplication can be done in either order. Division cannot: $12 \div 4 = 3$ but $4 \div 12$ is much less than 1.

solve.work: 12 + 0 = 0 + 12 true; 17 = 17 true; 60 = 60 true; 12 / 4 = 3 but 4 / 12 = 1/3, so the division one is not true.

questions.skill: Associative property
questions.stem: Which equation shows the associative property of multiplication?
questions.solution: The associative property says that changing how factors are grouped does not change the product. Both sides keep the order 2, 5, 7 and only move the parentheses.

solve.work: Associative property regroups: (2 x 5) x 7 = 2 x (5 x 7). A is distributive, B commutative, C reorders (commutative).

questions.skill: Associative property
questions.stem: To find $4 \times (7 \times 25)$ in her head, Mina first groups $4 \times 25$. What is the value of the whole expression?
questions.solution: Regroup the factors: $4 \times 25 = 100$ and $100 \times 7 = 700$. So the value is 700.

questions.skill: Distributive property
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $9 \times (10 - 2)$?
questions.solution: The 9 multiplies both numbers in the parentheses: $9 \times 10 - 9 \times 2 = 90 - 18 = 72$, the same as $9 \times 8$.

questions.skill: Distributive property
questions.stem: Sara finds $8 \times 49$ by thinking of it as $8 \times 50 - 8 \times 1$. What is the value?
questions.solution: $8 \times 50 = 400$ and $8 \times 1 = 8$. Subtracting gives $400 - 8 = 392$.

questions.skill: Distributive property
questions.stem: Which equation shows the distributive property?
questions.solution: The distributive property multiplies a number by each part of a sum: $4 \times (6 + 3) = 4 \times 6 + 4 \times 3$. The others show the associative, commutative and identity properties.

solve.work: Distributive: 4 x (6 + 3) = 4 x 6 + 4 x 3 (36 = 24 + 12). B associative, C commutative, D identity.

questions.skill: Identity and zero properties
questions.stem: Which equation shows the identity property of multiplication?
questions.solution: The identity property of multiplication says that a number times 1 stays the same: $9 \times 1 = 9$. The equation $9 + 0 = 9$ is the identity property of addition, $9 \times 0 = 0$ is the zero property and $9 \times 3 = 3 \times 9$ is the commutative property.

solve.work: Identity property of multiplication: times 1 leaves the number unchanged, 9 x 1 = 9. 9 x 0 is the zero property, 9 + 0 additive identity, last commutative.

questions.skill: Connect an expression to a representation
questions.stem: A rectangle is 9 units long and 6 units wide. It is cut into a rectangle that is 9 by 4 and a rectangle that is 9 by 2. Which expression gives the area of the large rectangle?
questions.solution: The area is the sum of the two parts: $9 \times 4 + 9 \times 2 = 36 + 18 = 54$. That is the same as $9 \times 6$.

questions.skill: Connect an expression to a representation
questions.stem: An area model for 7 times 24 is split into a rectangle that is 7 by 20 and a rectangle that is 7 by 4. What is the total area?
questions.solution: The parts have areas $7 \times 20 = 140$ and $7 \times 4 = 28$. The total is $140 + 28 = 168$.

questions.skill: Find the missing number or sign
questions.stem: What number makes the equation true? $5 + 3 \times \square = 29$
questions.solution: Multiplication comes first, so $3 \times \square$ must be $29 - 5 = 24$. Then the box is $24 \div 3 = 8$. Check: $5 + 3 \times 8 = 5 + 24 = 29$.

solve.work: 5 + 3 x box = 29, so 3 x box = 24, box = 8. Check 5 + 24 = 29.

questions.skill: Find the missing number or sign
questions.stem: Which sign goes in the box to make the equation true? $20 \ \square \ 4 \times 2 = 12$
questions.solution: Multiplication comes first: $4 \times 2 = 8$. We need $20 \ \square \ 8 = 12$, and $20 - 8 = 12$. So the sign is minus. The other signs give 28, 160 and 10.

solve.work: 4 x 2 = 8 is done first, so 20 ? 8 = 12 needs minus. Check others: 20 x 4 x 2 = 160, 20 + 8 = 28, 20 / 4 x 2 = 10 (left to right). Only minus.

questions.skill: Find the mistake in an evaluation
questions.stem: Kofi says that $4 + 6 \times 5$ equals 50. What did he do?
choices: He multiplied 4 and 6 first, then added 5
He multiplied 6 and 5 first, then subtracted 4
He added 4 and 6 first, then multiplied by 5
questions.answer: He added 4 and 6 first, then multiplied by 5
questions.solution: Adding first gives $(4 + 6) \times 5 = 50$, which is Kofi's answer. The correct way is to multiply first: $6 \times 5 = 30$, then $4 + 30 = 34$.

solve.answer: He added 4 and 6 first, then multiplied by 5
solve.work: Correct value 4 + 30 = 34. 50 = (4 + 6) x 5, so he added 4 and 6 first. B gives 29, C 26, D 15.

questions.skill: Evaluate an expression with parentheses and two other operations
questions.stem: Find the value of $2 \times (15 - 6) + 4 \times 3$.
questions.solution: Parentheses first: $15 - 6 = 9$. Then multiply: $2 \times 9 = 18$ and $4 \times 3 = 12$. Then add: $18 + 12 = 30$.

questions.skill: Compare the values of expressions
questions.stem: Which expression has the greatest value?

questions.skill: Write an expression for a situation
questions.stem: Each box holds 6 red pens and 4 blue pens. Which expression gives the number of pens in 3 boxes?
questions.solution: One box holds $6 + 4$ pens. Three boxes hold 3 times that: $3 \times (6 + 4) = 30$ pens. The other expressions multiply only one kind of pen by 3, or multiply all three numbers.

solve.work: Each box has 6 + 4 = 10 pens; 3 boxes: 3 x (6 + 4) = 30.

questions.skill: Order of operations without parentheses
questions.stem: What is the value of $3 \times 12 + 40 \div 8$?
questions.solution: Do the multiplication and the division first: $3 \times 12 = 36$ and $40 \div 8 = 5$. Then add: $36 + 5 = 41$.

questions.skill: Order of operations without parentheses
questions.stem: Which is the value of $90 \div 9 - 2 \times 4$?
questions.solution: Do the division and the multiplication first: $90 \div 9 = 10$ and $2 \times 4 = 8$. Then subtract: $10 - 8 = 2$. The choice 32 comes from working left to right ($8 \times 4$), 18 from adding 8 instead of subtracting, and 8 from taking away only 2.

questions.skill: Order of operations without parentheses
questions.stem: Evaluate $7 \times 13 + 480 \div 12$.
questions.solution: Multiply and divide first: $7 \times 13 = 91$ and $480 \div 12 = 40$. Then add: $91 + 40 = 131$.

questions.skill: Order of operations with parentheses
questions.stem: Evaluate $(14 - 6) \times (9 - 3)$.
questions.solution: Do each set of parentheses first: $14 - 6 = 8$ and $9 - 3 = 6$. Then multiply: $8 \times 6 = 48$.

questions.skill: Order of operations with parentheses
questions.stem: Which is the value of $5 \times (24 \div 6 + 2)$?
questions.solution: Inside the parentheses, divide before adding: $24 \div 6 = 4$ and $4 + 2 = 6$. Then multiply: $5 \times 6 = 30$. The choice 22 comes from ignoring the parentheses ($5 \times 4 + 2$), 15 from computing $24 \div (6 + 2)$ first, and 20 from leaving out the $+ 2$.

questions.skill: Order of operations with parentheses
questions.stem: What is the value of $2 \times (50 - 3 \times 8)$?
questions.solution: Inside the parentheses, multiply before subtracting: $3 \times 8 = 24$ and $50 - 24 = 26$. Then multiply: $2 \times 26 = 52$.

questions.skill: Compare the values of expressions
questions.stem: Which statement is true?
questions.solution: $20 - 3 \times 4 = 8$ and $(20 - 3) \times 4 = 68$, and $8 < 68$ is true. The others are false: $7 + 3 \times 5 = 22$ but $(7 + 3) \times 5 = 50$; $36 \div 6 + 3 = 9$ but $36 \div (6 + 3) = 4$, and 9 is not less than 4; $4 \times 5 - 2 = 18$ but $4 \times (5 - 2) = 12$.

questions.skill: Compare the values of expressions
questions.stem: Four expressions are listed: $4 + 5 \times 4$, $(4 + 5) \times 4$, $4 \times 5 + 4$ and $4 \times (5 + 4)$. How many of them have a value of 24?
questions.solution: $4 + 5 \times 4 = 4 + 20 = 24$; $(4 + 5) \times 4 = 36$; $4 \times 5 + 4 = 24$; $4 \times (5 + 4) = 36$. Two of the four have a value of 24.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: Which expression means "subtract 4 from twice the sum of 9 and 6"?
questions.solution: "The sum of 9 and 6" is $(9 + 6)$. "Twice" that is $2 \times (9 + 6)$. "Subtract 4 from" that gives $2 \times (9 + 6) - 4$.

solve.work: Twice the sum of 9 and 6 is 2 x (9 + 6); subtract 4: 2 x (9 + 6) - 4.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: Divide 100 by the product of 5 and 4, then add 12. What number do you get?
questions.solution: The product of 5 and 4 is 20. Dividing gives $100 \div 20 = 5$. Adding 12 gives $5 + 12 = 17$. As an expression this is $100 \div (5 \times 4) + 12$.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a described calculation
questions.stem: Which expression means "add 10 to the quotient of 48 and 6, then multiply by 3"?
questions.solution: The quotient of 48 and 6 is $48 \div 6$. Adding 10 gives $10 + 48 \div 6$, and this whole sum is then multiplied by 3, so it goes in parentheses: $(10 + 48 \div 6) \times 3$.

solve.work: Quotient 48 / 6; add 10: 10 + 48 / 6; then multiply that whole by 3: (10 + 48 / 6) x 3 = 18 x 3 = 54. Option B gives 10 + 24 = 34, so only A.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a story
questions.stem: A baker makes 6 trays of 12 rolls. He sells 45 rolls in the morning and 15 more in the afternoon. How many rolls are left?
questions.solution: He bakes $6 \times 12 = 72$ rolls. He sells $45 + 15 = 60$. So $72 - 60 = 12$ rolls are left.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a story
questions.stem: A class collects 9 cans a day for 5 days. Then 5 cans are thrown away and the rest are divided equally among 4 bins. Which expression gives the number of cans in each bin?
questions.solution: The class collects $9 \times 5$ cans. After throwing 5 away, there are $9 \times 5 - 5$ cans, and this whole amount is divided by 4. So the expression is $(9 \times 5 - 5) \div 4$, which is $40 \div 4 = 10$.

solve.work: Collected 9 x 5 = 45; minus 5 = 40; divided among 4 bins: (9 x 5 - 5) / 4 = 10.

questions.skill: Write an expression for a story
questions.stem: Priya earns 8 dollars each hour and works 5 hours. She spends 14 dollars on lunch and 6 dollars on a bus ticket. How many dollars does she have left?
questions.solution: She earns $8 \times 5 = 40$ dollars. She spends $14 + 6 = 20$ dollars. She has $40 - 20 = 20$ dollars left.

questions.skill: Interpret an expression without calculating
questions.stem: The value of $(23 + 17) \times 6$ is 240. What is the value of $(23 + 17) \times 12$? Do not add 23 and 17 again.
questions.solution: The second expression multiplies the same sum by 12 instead of 6, which is twice as much. So the value is $2 \times 240 = 480$.

questions.skill: Interpret an expression without calculating
questions.stem: Alex knows that $14 \times 6$ equals 84. Using this, what is the value of $14 \times 7$?
questions.solution: $14 \times 7$ is one more group of 14 than $14 \times 6$. So $14 \times 7 = 84 + 14 = 98$.

questions.skill: Associative property
questions.stem: What number goes in the box to make the equation true? $(9 \times 6) \times \square = 9 \times (6 \times 5)$
questions.solution: Both sides are the product of 9, 6 and 5 with different grouping. So the box is 5. Each side equals 270.

solve.work: Associative: (9 x 6) x 5 = 9 x (6 x 5); box = 5. Check 54 x 5 = 270 = 9 x 30.

questions.skill: Associative property
questions.stem: Which expression equals $(13 + 28) + 22$ and is the easiest to work out in your head?
questions.solution: Regroup the addition as $13 + (28 + 22)$. Then $28 + 22 = 50$ and $13 + 50 = 63$, which equals $(13 + 28) + 22 = 41 + 22 = 63$.

questions.skill: Distributive property
questions.stem: What is the value of $6 \times 34 + 6 \times 16$? Hint: both parts have a factor of 6.
questions.solution: Write it as $6 \times (34 + 16) = 6 \times 50 = 300$. Check: $6 \times 34 = 204$ and $6 \times 16 = 96$, and $204 + 96 = 300$.

questions.skill: Distributive property
questions.stem: Which expression is equal to $12 \times 15$ if 12 is split into 10 and 2?
questions.solution: Split 12 into $10 + 2$ and multiply each part by 15: $12 \times 15 = 10 \times 15 + 2 \times 15 = 150 + 30 = 180$.

questions.skill: Distributive property
questions.stem: Which expression is NOT equal to $7 \times 18$?
questions.solution: $7 \times 18 = 126$. Also $7 \times 20 - 7 \times 2 = 140 - 14 = 126$, $7 \times 9 \times 2 = 63 \times 2 = 126$, and $70 + 56 = 126$. But $7 \times 10 + 8 = 78$, because the 7 was not multiplied by the 8.

questions.skill: Distributive property
questions.stem: A garden has 14 rows with 25 plants in each row. Using $14 \times 25$ equals $10 \times 25 + 4 \times 25$, how many plants are in the garden?
questions.solution: $10 \times 25 = 250$ and $4 \times 25 = 100$. Adding gives $250 + 100 = 350$ plants.

questions.skill: Connect an expression to a representation
questions.stem: Which story matches the expression $5 \times (3 + 4)$?
choices: 5 shelves each hold 3 red books, and there are 4 more blue books
3 shelves each hold 5 books, and there are 4 more books
5 shelves each hold 3 red books and 4 blue books
A shelf holds 5 red books, 3 blue books and 4 green books
questions.answer: 5 shelves each hold 3 red books and 4 blue books
questions.solution: $5 \times (3 + 4)$ means 5 equal groups, each with $3 + 4$ items. That matches 5 shelves, each holding 3 red and 4 blue books: $5 \times 7 = 35$ books.

solve.answer: 5 shelves each hold 3 red books and 4 blue books
solve.work: 5 x (3 + 4): 5 groups, each of 3 + 4. 5 shelves each holding 3 red and 4 blue books. A is 3 x 5 + 4, B is 5 x 3 + 4, C is 5 + 3 + 4.

questions.skill: Connect an expression to a representation
questions.stem: An array of dots has 6 rows. The first 5 rows have 8 dots each and the last row has 3 dots. How many dots are in the array?
questions.solution: The first 5 rows have $5 \times 8 = 40$ dots. Adding the last row gives $40 + 3 = 43$ dots.

questions.skill: Connect an expression to a representation
questions.stem: A tape diagram shows a whole bar of 50 units. A part made of 4 equal pieces of 6 units each is removed. Which expression gives the length that remains?
questions.solution: The removed part is $4 \times 6 = 24$ units. What remains is $50 - 4 \times 6 = 50 - 24 = 26$ units.

questions.skill: Find the missing number or sign
questions.stem: What number goes in the box? $4 \times (\square + 6) = 40$
questions.solution: The parentheses must equal $40 \div 4 = 10$. So $\square + 6 = 10$ and the box is 4. Check: $4 \times (4 + 6) = 40$.

questions.skill: Find the missing number or sign
questions.stem: What number goes in the box? $100 - 6 \times \square = 64$
questions.solution: Multiplication comes first, so $6 \times \square$ must be $100 - 64 = 36$. The box is $36 \div 6 = 6$. Check: $100 - 6 \times 6 = 64$.

solve.work: 100 - 6 x box = 64, so 6 x box = 36, box = 6.

questions.skill: Find the missing number or sign
questions.stem: Which number makes the equation true? $(\square + 5) \times 3 = 3 \times 7 + 3 \times 5$
questions.solution: The right side is $21 + 15 = 36$. So $(\square + 5) \times 3 = 36$, which means $\square + 5 = 12$ and the box is 7. The distributive property shows the same thing: $3 \times (7 + 5) = 3 \times 7 + 3 \times 5$.

solve.work: Right side 21 + 15 = 36. (box + 5) x 3 = 36 so box + 5 = 12, box = 7 (distributive: (7 + 5) x 3 = 3 x 7 + 3 x 5). 12 would make 51.

questions.skill: Find the mistake in an evaluation
questions.stem: Dana wrote that $50 - 4 \times 5$ equals 230. What is the correct value of $50 - 4 \times 5$?
questions.solution: Dana subtracted first ($46 \times 5 = 230$). The multiplication must come first: $4 \times 5 = 20$, and then $50 - 20 = 30$.

questions.skill: Find the mistake in an evaluation
questions.stem: Jo worked out $2 \times 5 + 3 \times 4$ like this: $2 \times 5$ is 10, then $10 + 3$ is 13, then $13 \times 4$ is 52. What is the correct value of $2 \times 5 + 3 \times 4$?
questions.solution: Both multiplications must be done before the addition: $2 \times 5 = 10$ and $3 \times 4 = 12$. Then $10 + 12 = 22$.

questions.skill: Value of a digit up to the millions
questions.stem: In the number $3{,}482{,}915$, what is the value of the digit 4?
questions.solution: Reading from the left, the places are millions (3), hundred thousands (4), ten thousands (8), and so on. The 4 is in the hundred thousands place, so its value is $4 \times 100{,}000 = 400{,}000$.

questions.skill: Expanded form of a decimal
questions.stem: Which number is equal to $6 + 0.2 + 0.05$?
questions.solution: The 6 is the ones, 0.2 is 2 tenths, and 0.05 is 5 hundredths. Together they make 6.25.

questions.skill: Multiply a decimal by 10
questions.stem: What is $3.6 \times 10$?
questions.solution: Multiplying by 10 moves every digit one place to the left, so 3.6 becomes 36.

solve.work: Multiplying by 10 moves each digit one place left: 3.6 x 10 = 36.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a whole number up to the millions
questions.stem: In $5{,}207{,}000$, which place is the digit 5 in?
questions.solution: The number has seven digits. The first digit, from the left, is in the millions place, so the 5 is worth 5 millions. The places after it are hundred thousands (2), ten thousands (0) and thousands (7).

solve.work: 5,207,000: 5 millions, 2 hundred thousands, 0 ten thousands, 7 thousands. The 5 is in the millions place.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a whole number up to the millions
questions.stem: Which digit is in the thousands place of $9{,}731{,}204$?
questions.solution: Reading from the right, the places in $9{,}731{,}204$ are ones (4), tens (0), hundreds (2), thousands (1). So the digit in the thousands place is 1. The digit 3 is in the ten thousands place, 7 in the hundred thousands place and 2 in the hundreds place.

solve.work: 9,731,204: 9 M, 7 HTh, 3 TTh, 1 Th, 2 H, 0 T, 4 O. Thousands digit is 1.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a whole number up to the millions
questions.stem: In $2{,}906{,}351$, what digit is in the hundred thousands place?
questions.solution: The digit 2 is in the millions place, and the next place to its right, the hundred thousands place, holds the 9.

solve.work: 2,906,351: 2 M, 9 HTh, 0 TTh, 6 Th. Hundred thousands digit is 9.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a decimal to the thousandths
questions.stem: Which digit is in the tenths place of $3.752$?
questions.solution: The first digit after the decimal point is the tenths place. In $3.752$ it is 7. The 5 is in the hundredths place and the 2 in the thousandths place.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a decimal to the thousandths
questions.stem: What digit is in the hundredths place of $8.614$?
questions.solution: After the decimal point the places are tenths (6), hundredths (1) and thousandths (4). So the digit in the hundredths place is 1.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a decimal to the thousandths
questions.stem: In the number $0.325$, what is the value of the digit 3?
questions.solution: The 3 is the first digit after the decimal point, in the tenths place. Its value is 3 tenths, which is $0.3$.

questions.skill: Compare the values of a digit in different places
questions.stem: The number 66 has two 6s. The value of the left 6 is how many times the value of the right 6?
questions.solution: The left 6 is in the tens place and is worth 60. The right 6 is in the ones place and is worth 6. Since $60 \div 6 = 10$, the left 6 is 10 times as great.

questions.skill: Compare the values of a digit in different places
questions.stem: In $4.44$, the 4 in the ones place is how many times as great as the 4 in the tenths place?
questions.solution: The 4 in the ones place is worth 4 and the 4 in the tenths place is worth $0.4$. Since $4 \div 0.4 = 10$, the first is 10 times as great.

questions.skill: Whole numbers in words and standard form
questions.stem: Which number is "three hundred forty thousand, six hundred twelve"?
questions.solution: Three hundred forty thousand is 340,000 and six hundred twelve is 612. Together they make $340{,}612$.

solve.work: Three hundred forty thousand = 340,000; six hundred twelve = 612. 340,612.

questions.skill: Whole numbers in words and standard form
questions.stem: Write "two million, four hundred thousand" as a number.
questions.solution: Two million is 2,000,000 and four hundred thousand is 400,000. Adding gives $2{,}400{,}000$.

questions.skill: Whole numbers in words and standard form
questions.stem: How is $5{,}060{,}300$ written in words?
choices: five million, six hundred thousand, three hundred
fifty million, sixty thousand, three hundred
five million, sixty thousand, three hundred
questions.answer: five million, sixty thousand, three hundred
questions.solution: The number has 5 millions, then 060 thousands (sixty thousand) and 300 ones (three hundred). So it is five million, sixty thousand, three hundred.

solve.answer: five million, sixty thousand, three hundred
solve.work: 5,060,300 = 5,000,000 + 60,000 + 300: five million, sixty thousand, three hundred.

questions.skill: Decimals in words and standard form
questions.stem: Which decimal is written in words as "six and two tenths"?
questions.solution: The whole number is 6 and the fraction part is 2 tenths, which is $0.2$. Together they make $6.2$.

questions.skill: Decimals in words and standard form
questions.stem: Write "nine and eight hundredths" as a decimal.
questions.solution: The whole part is 9. Eight hundredths is $0.08$, with a 0 in the tenths place. So the decimal is $9.08$.

questions.skill: Expanded form of a number
questions.solution: Each part sits in its own place, with 0 tens: 5 ten thousands, 3 thousands, 4 hundreds, 0 tens and 7 ones. The number is $53{,}407$.

questions.skill: Expanded form of a number
questions.stem: Which is $2{,}561$ in expanded form?
questions.solution: The digit 2 is worth 2,000, the 5 is worth 500, the 6 is worth 60 and the 1 is worth 1. So $2{,}561 = 2{,}000 + 500 + 60 + 1$.

solve.issues: Easy for Grade 5 (four-digit expanded form, earlier-grade work); fine as a warm-up.

questions.skill: Expanded form of a number
questions.stem: Which number is the same as $9 \times 100 + 4 \times 10 + 6 \times 1$?
questions.solution: 9 hundreds, 4 tens and 6 ones make $900 + 40 + 6 = 946$.

solve.issues: Easy for Grade 5 (three-digit expanded form, earlier-grade work); fine as a warm-up.

questions.skill: Equivalent decimals
questions.stem: Which decimal is equal to $0.4$?
questions.solution: Adding a zero at the end of a decimal does not change its value. 4 tenths is the same as 40 hundredths, so $0.4 = 0.40$.

solve.work: 0.4 = 0.40 (adding a zero in the hundredths). 0.14, 4.0, 0.04 differ.

questions.skill: Equivalent decimals
questions.stem: How many hundredths are equal to 7 tenths?
questions.solution: One tenth is 10 hundredths. So 7 tenths is $7 \times 10 = 70$ hundredths.

questions.skill: Multiply by 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: What is $45 \times 100$?
questions.solution: Multiplying by 100 moves each digit two places to the left, so 45 becomes 4,500.

questions.skill: Multiply by 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: Which is the value of $0.7 \times 10$?
questions.solution: Multiplying by 10 moves each digit one place to the left. So $0.7 \times 10 = 7$. The choice $0.07$ moves the digit the wrong way.

questions.skill: Multiply by 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: A tile is 3.4 centimeters long. Ten tiles are placed end to end in a row. How long is the row in centimeters?
questions.solution: The row is 10 times as long as one tile: $3.4 \times 10 = 34$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Divide by 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: What is $85 \div 10$?
questions.solution: Dividing by 10 moves each digit one place to the right, so 85 becomes 8.5.

questions.skill: Divide by 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: Which is the value of $7 \div 100$?
questions.solution: Dividing by 100 moves the digit two places to the right, so 7 becomes $0.07$.

questions.skill: Divide by 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: A rope 340 centimeters long is cut into 100 equal pieces. How long is each piece in centimeters?
questions.solution: Each piece is $340 \div 100 = 3.4$ centimeters long.

questions.skill: Powers of ten with exponents
questions.stem: Which number is equal to $10^3$?
questions.solution: The exponent 3 means 10 is used as a factor 3 times: $10^3 = 10 \times 10 \times 10 = 1{,}000$. The choice 30 is $3 \times 10$.

questions.skill: Compare two decimals
questions.stem: Which decimal is the greatest?
questions.solution: Compare the tenths first: 0.7 has 7 tenths, while the others have 0, 1 and 2 tenths. So 0.7 is the greatest.

solve.work: Tenths: 0.07 has 0, 0.27 has 2, 0.7 has 7, 0.17 has 1. Greatest 0.7.

questions.skill: Compare two decimals
questions.stem: Which is greater, 3.4 or 3.04? Write the greater number.
questions.solution: Both have 3 ones. Then 3.4 has 4 tenths and 3.04 has 0 tenths. So 3.4 is greater.

questions.skill: Compare two decimals
questions.stem: Which of these is a true statement?
questions.solution: $0.2 = 0.20$, which is less than $0.25$. So $0.2 < 0.25$ is true. $0.20 > 0.2$ is false because they are equal.

solve.work: 0.20 = 0.2 so A false; 0.2 = 0.20 < 0.25, so B, C false and D true.

questions.skill: Order decimals
questions.stem: Mia has three decimals: 0.3, 0.03 and 0.33. Which list puts them in order from least to greatest?
questions.solution: In hundredths these are 0.30, 0.03 and 0.33. From least to greatest: 0.03, then 0.3, then 0.33.

questions.skill: Order decimals
questions.stem: The decimals 0.7, 0.07 and 0.77 are put in order from least to greatest. Which decimal is in the middle?
questions.solution: In hundredths these are 0.70, 0.07 and 0.77. In order they are 0.07, 0.7, 0.77, so the middle one is 0.7.

questions.skill: Read a decimal written in words
questions.stem: Which decimal is written in words as "four and thirty-seven thousandths"?
questions.solution: "Four" is the whole number. "Thirty-seven thousandths" needs three places after the decimal point: 037. So the number is 4.037.

questions.skill: Divide a decimal by a power of ten
questions.stem: What is $9.3 \div 100$?
questions.solution: Dividing by 100 moves every digit two places to the right, so 9.3 becomes 0.093.

solve.work: Dividing by 100 moves digits two places right: 9.3 / 100 = 0.093.

questions.skill: Order decimals
questions.stem: Which list shows these decimals in order from least to greatest: 0.45, 0.405, 0.054, 0.5?
questions.solution: Write each with three decimal places: 0.450, 0.405, 0.054, 0.500. From least to greatest: 0.054, 0.405, 0.450, 0.500.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a whole number up to the millions
questions.stem: In which number does the digit 5 have a value of $50{,}000$?
questions.solution: A 5 worth 50,000 is in the ten thousands place. In $350{,}218$ the 5 is in the ten thousands place. In the other numbers the 5 is worth 5,000,000, 500 and 5,000.

solve.work: 50,000 means 5 in the ten thousands place. 5,302,418: 5 M. 350,218: 3 HTh, 5 TTh (yes). 83,501: 5 hundreds. 1,205,006: 5 thousands. Only 350,218.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a whole number up to the millions
questions.stem: A city has $6{,}083{,}417$ people. What is the value of the digit 8 in this number?
questions.solution: The places are 6 millions, 0 hundred thousands, 8 ten thousands. The 8 is in the ten thousands place, so its value is $8 \times 10{,}000 = 80{,}000$.

solve.work: 6,083,417: 6 M, 0 HTh, 8 TTh, 3 Th. The 8 is worth 80,000.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a decimal to the thousandths
questions.stem: What is the value of the digit 9 in $12.093$?
questions.solution: The places after the decimal point are tenths (0), hundredths (9) and thousandths (3). The 9 is in the hundredths place, so its value is 9 hundredths, which is $0.09$.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a decimal to the thousandths
questions.stem: In which number does the digit 4 have a value of $0.004$?
questions.solution: A 4 worth $0.004$ is in the thousandths place. In $6.504$ the last digit is a 4 in the thousandths place. In the other numbers the 4 is worth $0.04$, $4$ and $0.4$.

solve.work: 0.004 means 4 in the thousandths. 6.504: 4 thousandths (yes). 6.045: 4 hundredths. 6.450: 4 tenths. 4.605: 4 ones.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a decimal to the thousandths
questions.stem: How many hundredths are in $0.46$?
questions.solution: The number $0.46$ is 46 hundredths, because 4 tenths is the same as 40 hundredths and $40 + 6 = 46$.

questions.skill: Compare the values of a digit in different places
questions.stem: In $2{,}002$, the value of the left 2 is how many times the value of the right 2?
questions.solution: The left 2 is in the thousands place and is worth 2,000. The right 2 is in the ones place and is worth 2. Since $2{,}000 \div 2 = 1{,}000$, the left 2 is 1,000 times as great.

questions.skill: Compare the values of a digit in different places
questions.stem: In $0.33$, the value of the 3 in the hundredths place is what fraction of the value of the 3 in the tenths place?
questions.solution: The 3 in the tenths place is worth $0.3$ and the 3 in the hundredths place is worth $0.03$. A digit moved one place to the right is worth $\frac{1}{10}$ as much.

questions.skill: Whole numbers in words and standard form
questions.stem: Write "eight million, seven thousand, five hundred" in standard form.
questions.solution: Eight million is 8,000,000, seven thousand is 7,000 and five hundred is 500. The sum is $8{,}007{,}500$. The zeros in the hundred thousands and ten thousands places hold those places.

questions.skill: Whole numbers in words and standard form
questions.stem: Which number is written in words as "nine hundred nine thousand, ninety"?
questions.solution: Nine hundred nine thousand is 909,000 and ninety is 90, so the number is $909{,}090$. The choice $909{,}009$ ends in nine, $990{,}090$ is nine hundred ninety thousand and $909{,}900$ ends in nine hundred.

questions.skill: Decimals in words and standard form
questions.stem: How do you say $0.206$ in words?
questions.solution: The last digit is in the thousandths place, and the digits 206 make two hundred six. So $0.206$ is two hundred six thousandths.

questions.skill: Decimals in words and standard form
questions.stem: Write "twelve and forty-five thousandths" as a decimal.
questions.solution: Forty-five thousandths needs three decimal places, so it is $0.045$. With the whole part 12 the decimal is $12.045$.

questions.skill: Decimals in words and standard form
questions.stem: Which number is "one hundred three thousandths"?
questions.solution: Thousandths means three places after the decimal point. One hundred three is 103, so the number is $0.103$.

questions.skill: Expanded form of a number
questions.stem: What number is $3 \times 10{,}000 + 7 \times 1{,}000 + 2 \times 10 + 9 \times 1$?
questions.solution: That is 3 ten thousands, 7 thousands, 0 hundreds, 2 tens and 9 ones. The number is $37{,}029$.

questions.skill: Expanded form of a number
questions.stem: Which shows $7.034$ in expanded form?
questions.solution: The digits of $7.034$ are 7 ones, 0 tenths, 3 hundredths and 4 thousandths. So $7.034 = 7 + 0.03 + 0.004$.

questions.skill: Expanded form of a number
questions.stem: What decimal is equal to $5 \times 1 + 2 \times \frac{1}{10} + 8 \times \frac{1}{1000}$?
questions.solution: 5 ones, 2 tenths, 0 hundredths and 8 thousandths make $5.208$.

questions.skill: Equivalent decimals
questions.stem: Which decimal is NOT equal to $0.60$?
questions.solution: Zeros at the end of a decimal do not change its value, so $0.60 = 0.6 = 0.600$, and $\frac{60}{100}$ is also 0.6. But $0.06$ is 6 hundredths, which is much less.

solve.issues: Minor: the stem says "Which decimal" but one option is a fraction (60/100).

questions.skill: Multiply by 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: What is $0.047 \times 1{,}000$?
questions.solution: Multiplying by 1,000 moves each digit three places to the left. So $0.047$ becomes $47$.

questions.skill: Multiply by 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: Which product is equal to 52?
questions.solution: Multiplying by 100 moves digits two places left, so $0.52 \times 100 = 52$. The others give 5.2, 520 and 5.2.

questions.skill: Divide by 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: What is $26.4 \div 100$?
questions.solution: Dividing by 100 moves each digit two places to the right, so $26.4$ becomes $0.264$.

questions.skill: Divide by 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: Which expression has the value $0.045$?
questions.solution: Dividing 45 by 1,000 moves the digits three places to the right, giving $0.045$. The others give 0.45, 0.0045 and 4.5.

questions.skill: Divide by 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: A package weighs $2{,}350$ grams. There are $1{,}000$ grams in a kilogram. How many kilograms does the package weigh?
questions.solution: The weight in kilograms is $2{,}350 \div 1{,}000 = 2.35$.

questions.skill: Powers of ten with exponents
questions.stem: What is $5.4 \times 10^2$?
questions.solution: $10^2 = 100$. Multiplying by 100 moves the digits two places to the left, so $5.4 \times 100 = 540$.

questions.skill: Powers of ten with exponents
questions.stem: Which is equal to $10 \times 10 \times 10 \times 10$?
questions.solution: There are four factors of 10, so the product is $10^4 = 10{,}000$.

questions.skill: Find the unknown in a power-of-ten pattern
questions.stem: A number multiplied by 100 gives 470. What is the number?
questions.solution: To undo multiplying by 100, divide by 100: $470 \div 100 = 4.7$.

questions.skill: Compare two decimals
questions.stem: Which decimal is the least: 0.409, 0.49, 0.094 or 0.9?
questions.solution: Compare the tenths first. 0.094 has 0 tenths while the others have 4, 4 and 9 tenths, so 0.094 is the least.

questions.skill: Compare two decimals
questions.stem: How many of the decimals 0.35, 0.305, 0.5 and 0.053 are less than 0.35?
questions.solution: Write each with three places: 0.350, 0.305, 0.500 and 0.053. Only 0.305 and 0.053 are less than 0.350. So the answer is 2.

solve.work: 0.35 is equal, not less; 0.305 < 0.350 yes; 0.5 no; 0.053 yes. Two.

questions.skill: Order decimals
questions.stem: Which list shows 1.2, 1.02, 1.002 and 1.21 in order from greatest to least?
questions.solution: All have 1 one. Write them with three places: 1.200, 1.020, 1.002 and 1.210. From greatest to least: 1.210, 1.200, 1.020, 1.002.

questions.skill: Order decimals
questions.stem: Four runners finished a race in 12.35, 12.305, 12.5 and 12.053 seconds. The winner has the least time. What was the winning time in seconds?
questions.solution: Write the times with three places: 12.350, 12.305, 12.500 and 12.053. The least is 12.053 seconds.

questions.skill: Compare whole numbers up to the millions
questions.stem: Which number is greater than $2{,}345{,}678$?
questions.solution: All the numbers have 2 millions, so compare place by place. $2{,}354{,}000$ and $2{,}345{,}678$ both have 3 hundred thousands, but then 5 ten thousands beats 4 ten thousands. So $2{,}354{,}000$ is greater. The others are less: $2{,}345{,}000$ has fewer hundreds, $2{,}335{,}999$ has only 3 ten thousands and $2{,}099{,}999$ has only 0 hundred thousands.

solve.work: 2,354,000 vs 2,345,678: ten thousands 5 > 4, so greater. The others are smaller (2,099,999; 2,345,000; 2,335,999).

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a whole number up to the millions
questions.stem: In $3{,}508{,}274$, what is the value of the digit 5?
questions.solution: In $3{,}508{,}274$ the 3 is in the millions place, so the 5 is in the hundred thousands place. Its value is 5 x 100,000 = 500,000.

questions.skill: Compare the value of a digit in two numbers
questions.stem: How many times as great is the value of the digit 7 in $7{,}214$ as the value of the digit 7 in $3.072$?
questions.solution: In $7{,}214$ the 7 is in the thousands place, so its value is 7,000. In $3.072$ the 7 is in the hundredths place, so its value is 0.07. Since $7{,}000 \div 0.07 = 100{,}000$, the first is 100,000 times as great.

solve.work: In 7,214 the 7 is worth 7,000. In 3.072 the 7 is in the hundredths place, worth 0.07. 7,000 / 0.07 = 100,000 (five places apart, 10^5).

questions.skill: Reverse a pattern of dividing by ten
questions.stem: A number is divided by 10. The result is 0.38. What is the number?
questions.solution: Dividing by 10 moves each digit one place to the right, so to undo it multiply by 10: $0.38 \times 10 = 3.8$.

questions.skill: Compare decimals
questions.stem: Which comparison is true?
questions.solution: Compare place by place. $0.700 > 0.699$ is true. The others are false: $0.15 < 0.50$, $2.04 < 2.40$, and $3.100 > 3.099$.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a whole number up to the millions
questions.stem: In the number $7{,}370{,}725$, what is the sum of the values of all the 7s?
questions.solution: The 7s are in the millions place (7,000,000), the ten thousands place (70,000) and the hundreds place (700). Their sum is $7{,}000{,}000 + 70{,}000 + 700 = 7{,}070{,}700$.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a whole number up to the millions
questions.stem: Which number has a 6 in the hundred thousands place and a 2 in the thousands place?
questions.solution: In $3{,}642{,}105$ the places are 3 millions, 6 hundred thousands, 4 ten thousands, 2 thousands. Both conditions hold. In $3{,}462{,}105$ the 6 is in the ten thousands place, in $3{,}624{,}105$ the 2 is in the ten thousands place, and in $6{,}342{,}105$ the 6 is in the millions place.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a decimal to the thousandths
questions.stem: In $7.272$, what is the sum of the values of the two 7s?
questions.solution: One 7 is in the ones place and is worth 7. The other 7 is in the hundredths place and is worth $0.07$. Their sum is $7 + 0.07 = 7.07$.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a decimal to the thousandths
questions.stem: Which number has a 5 in the hundredths place and a 3 in the thousandths place?
questions.solution: The hundredths place is the second digit after the point and the thousandths place is the third. In $12.153$ these digits are 5 and 3. The others have 3 and 5, 1 and 3, or 5 and 1.

solve.work: 12.351: 5 hundredths, 1 thousandth. 12.153: 1 tenth, 5 hundredths, 3 thousandths (yes). 12.135: 3 hundredths. 12.513: 1 hundredth.

questions.skill: Value of a digit in a decimal to the thousandths
questions.stem: A decimal has 6 in the ones place, 0 in the tenths place, 4 in the hundredths place and 9 in the thousandths place. What is the decimal?
questions.solution: Write the digits in order: ones 6, then the decimal point, then tenths 0, hundredths 4, thousandths 9. The decimal is $6.049$.

questions.skill: Compare the values of a digit in different places
questions.stem: In $5{,}050.505$, how many times as great is the value of the leftmost 5 as the value of the rightmost 5?
questions.solution: The leftmost 5 is in the thousands place and is worth 5,000. The rightmost 5 is in the thousandths place and is worth $0.005$. Since $5{,}000 \div 0.005 = 1{,}000{,}000$, the leftmost 5 is one million times as great.

solve.issues: Demanding for Grade 5: the two 5s are six places apart, so the answer is a million; fine as a stretch item.
solve.work: 5,050.505: leftmost 5 is 5 thousands = 5,000; rightmost 5 is 5 thousandths = 0.005. They are six places apart, so 10^6: 5,000 / 0.005 = 1,000,000.

questions.skill: Compare the values of a digit in different places
questions.stem: Which statement is true about the two 3s in $3.003$?
choices: The left 3 is $100$ times as great as the right 3
The left 3 is $10$ times as great as the right 3
The left 3 is $1{,}000$ times as great as the right 3
The right 3 is $1{,}000$ times as great as the left 3
questions.answer: The left 3 is $1{,}000$ times as great as the right 3
questions.solution: The left 3 is in the ones place and is worth 3. The right 3 is in the thousandths place and is worth $0.003$. Since $3 \div 0.003 = 1{,}000$, the left 3 is 1,000 times as great.

solve.answer: The left 3 is $1{,}000$ times as great as the right 3
solve.work: 3.003: left 3 = 3, right 3 = 0.003; 3 / 0.003 = 1,000. Left is 1,000 times the right.

questions.skill: Compare the values of a digit in different places
questions.stem: A decimal has a 9 in the tenths place. Another 9 in the decimal has a value that is $\frac{1}{100}$ of the value of the first 9. What is the value of the other 9?
questions.solution: The first 9 is worth $0.9$. One hundredth of $0.9$ is $0.9 \div 100 = 0.009$, which is a 9 in the thousandths place.

questions.skill: Whole numbers in words and standard form
questions.stem: A number is made of 6 millions, 12 thousands and 5 ones. Write the number in standard form.
questions.solution: 6 millions is 6,000,000, 12 thousands is 12,000 and 5 ones is 5. The sum is $6{,}012{,}005$.

questions.skill: Whole numbers in words and standard form
questions.stem: Which is the word form of $3{,}030{,}030$?
choices: three million, three hundred thousand, thirty
questions.solution: Split the number into periods: 3 million, 030 thousand and 030. That reads three million, thirty thousand, thirty. The other choices name $30{,}030{,}030$, $3{,}003{,}030$ and $3{,}300{,}030$.

questions.skill: Decimals in words and standard form
questions.stem: Write "three and four hundred five thousandths" as a decimal.
questions.solution: Four hundred five thousandths is $0.405$. With the whole part 3 the decimal is $3.405$.

questions.skill: Decimals in words and standard form
questions.stem: Which decimal is the same as "twenty-two and twenty-two thousandths"?
questions.solution: Twenty-two thousandths needs three decimal places: $0.022$. So the number is $22.022$. The choice $22.22$ is twenty-two and twenty-two hundredths.

questions.skill: Expanded form of a number
questions.stem: Which shows $24.305$ in expanded form using fractions?
questions.solution: In $24.305$ there are 2 tens, 4 ones, 3 tenths, 0 hundredths and 5 thousandths. So the 3 is multiplied by $\frac{1}{10}$ and the 5 by $\frac{1}{1000}$.

questions.skill: Expanded form of a number
questions.stem: What number is equal to $6 + 14 \times 0.1 + 5 \times 0.001$?

questions.skill: Expanded form of a number
questions.stem: A number is made of 3 millions, 15 hundreds and 8 tens. What is the number?

questions.skill: Equivalent decimals
questions.stem: Which list shows only decimals that are equal to each other?
questions.solution: Only zeros at the END of a decimal can be added or dropped without changing its value. $0.5 = 0.50 = 0.500$. In the other lists a zero sits between the point and a digit, which changes the value.

solve.work: 0.5 = 0.50 = 0.500 all equal. 1.02 differs from 1.2; 0.05, 0.005 differ; 0.03 differs.

questions.skill: Multiply by 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: What is $12.34 \times 1{,}000$?
questions.solution: Moving each digit three places to the left gives 12,340. A zero is needed to hold the ones place.

questions.skill: Multiply by 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: A machine fills each bottle with 0.375 liter of juice. How many liters does it use to fill 1,000 bottles?
questions.solution: The amount is $0.375 \times 1{,}000 = 375$ liters.

questions.skill: Multiply by 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: Which of these statements is true?
questions.solution: $0.06 \times 100 = 6$ is true. The others are false: $4.1 \times 10 = 41$, $3.5 \times 1{,}000 = 3{,}500$ and $0.9 \times 10 = 9$.

questions.skill: Divide by 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: What is $93 \div 1{,}000$?
questions.solution: Dividing by 1,000 moves each digit three places to the right. So 93 becomes $0.093$.

questions.skill: Divide by 10, 100 or 1,000
questions.stem: Which is the value of $4.2 \div 100$?
questions.solution: Dividing by 100 moves each digit two places to the right: $4.2$ becomes $0.042$. A zero holds the tenths place.

questions.skill: Powers of ten with exponents
questions.stem: What is $670 \div 10^2$?
questions.solution: $10^2 = 100$. Dividing 670 by 100 moves the digits two places to the right, so the answer is $6.7$.

questions.skill: Powers of ten with exponents
questions.stem: Which expression is NOT equal to $3.6 \times 10^2$?

questions.skill: Find the unknown in a power-of-ten pattern
questions.stem: What number goes in the box to make the equation true? $\square \times 1{,}000 = 6{,}250$
questions.solution: Undo the multiplication by dividing: $6{,}250 \div 1{,}000 = 6.25$.

questions.skill: Find the unknown in a power-of-ten pattern
questions.stem: What number goes in the box to make the equation true? $0.25 \times \square = 250$
questions.solution: The digits of 0.25 moved three places to the left to become 250. That is multiplying by 1,000. Check: $0.25 \times 1{,}000 = 250$.

questions.skill: Find the unknown in a power-of-ten pattern
questions.stem: Maria multiplied a number by 10 and then divided the result by 1,000. The answer was 0.052. What was her number?
questions.solution: Multiplying by 10 and then dividing by 1,000 is the same as dividing by 100. To undo it, multiply 0.052 by 100: $0.052 \times 100 = 5.2$.

questions.skill: Compare two decimals
questions.stem: Which number is between $2.45$ and $2.46$?
questions.solution: Write 2.45 as 2.450 and 2.46 as 2.460. A number between them is 2.455. The choices 2.5 and 2.46 are not less than 2.46, and 2.4 is less than 2.45.

solve.work: 2.45 = 2.450, 2.46 = 2.460; 2.455 lies between. 2.5 and 2.4 are outside; 2.46 is an endpoint.

questions.skill: Compare two decimals
questions.stem: What is the smallest decimal with three decimal places that is greater than 4.37?
questions.solution: Write 4.37 as 4.370. The next decimal with three places is $4.371$, which is 1 thousandth more.

solve.work: 4.37 = 4.370. The next number with three decimal places is 4.371.

questions.skill: Order decimals
questions.stem: Which list is in order from least to greatest?
questions.solution: Write each with three places: 0.089, 0.098, 0.800 and 0.890. From least to greatest: 0.089, 0.098, 0.800, 0.890.

solve.work: 0.089 < 0.098 < 0.800 < 0.890. First list. Last list puts 0.89 before 0.8 (wrong).

questions.skill: Compare whole numbers up to the millions
questions.stem: What is the least 7-digit number you can make using each of the digits 4, 0, 7, 2, 9, 5 and 1 once?
questions.solution: Put the smallest digits in the highest places, but a number cannot start with 0. So start with 1, then 0, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9: $1{,}024{,}579$.

solve.work: Digits 0,1,2,4,5,7,9. Leading digit cannot be 0, so smallest non-zero 1 first, then 0, then the rest ascending: 1,024,579.

questions.skill: Multiply a three-digit number by a two-digit number
questions.stem: Find $124 \times 12$.

questions.skill: Divide a four-digit number by a one-digit number
questions.stem: What is $1{,}248 \div 4$?
questions.solution: $12 \div 4 = 3$ (hundreds), $4 \div 4 = 1$ (tens), $8 \div 4 = 2$ (ones). The quotient is 312. Check: $312 \times 4 = 1{,}248$.

questions.skill: Multiply by a multiple of ten
questions.stem: A box holds 305 pencils. How many pencils are in 20 boxes?
questions.solution: $305 \times 2 = 610$, and multiplying by 10 more gives $6{,}100$.

questions.skill: Multiply a three-digit number by a two-digit number
questions.stem: A theater has 12 rows of seats, and each row has 110 seats. How many seats are in the theater?
questions.solution: There are 12 rows of 110 seats. $12 \times 110 = 12 \times 100 + 12 \times 10 = 1{,}200 + 120 = 1{,}320$ seats.

questions.skill: Multiply a three-digit number by a two-digit number
questions.stem: Pia multiplies $346 \times 27$ by breaking 27 into $20 + 7$. Her first partial product is $346 \times 7 = 2{,}422$. Which multiplication gives her second partial product?
questions.solution: Breaking 27 into $20 + 7$ gives two partial products: $346 \times 7$ and $346 \times 20$. The second one is $346 \times 20 = 6{,}920$.

solve.work: 27 = 20 + 7; first partial product uses 7, so the second uses 20: 346 x 20 = 6,920.

questions.skill: Multiply a three-digit number by a two-digit number
questions.stem: To find $213 \times 14$, Sam writes $213 \times 4 = 852$ and $213 \times 10 = 2{,}130$. What is $213 \times 14$?
questions.solution: Add the two partial products: $852 + 2{,}130 = 2{,}982$. So $213 \times 14 = 2{,}982$.

questions.skill: Multiply a three-digit number by a two-digit number
questions.stem: A box holds 132 crayons. How many crayons are in 21 boxes?

questions.skill: Multiply a three-digit number by a two-digit number
questions.stem: A bus carries 105 riders on each trip. It makes 15 trips in a day. How many riders does it carry in all?

questions.skill: Multiply a three-digit number by a two-digit number
questions.stem: What is $221 \times 31$?

questions.skill: Multiply by multiples of ten and one hundred
questions.stem: Multiply 600 by 40.
questions.solution: $6 \times 4 = 24$. Then add the 3 zeros that end $600$ and $40$ (two and one): $600 \times 40 = 24{,}000$.

questions.skill: Multiply by multiples of ten and one hundred
questions.stem: A pack holds 250 sheets of paper. How many sheets are in 40 packs?
questions.solution: $25 \times 4 = 100$. Then add the 2 zeros that end $250$ and $40$ (one each): $250 \times 40 = 10{,}000$ sheets.

questions.skill: Multiply by multiples of ten and one hundred
questions.stem: What is $120 \times 30$?
questions.solution: $12 \times 3 = 36$. Then add the 2 zeros that end $120$ and $30$ (one each): $120 \times 30 = 3{,}600$.

questions.skill: Multiply by multiples of ten and one hundred
questions.stem: A truck carries 800 bricks. How many bricks do 60 trucks carry?
questions.solution: $8 \times 6 = 48$. Then add the 3 zeros that end $800$ and $60$ (two and one): $800 \times 60 = 48{,}000$ bricks.

questions.skill: Divide a four-digit number by a one-digit number
questions.stem: A farm collects $2{,}400$ eggs. They are packed 6 to a carton. How many cartons are filled?

questions.skill: Divide a four-digit number by a one-digit number
questions.stem: What is $4{,}800 \div 6$?

questions.skill: Divide a four-digit number by a one-digit number
questions.stem: Find the quotient when $8{,}484$ is divided by 4.
questions.solution: Each digit divides evenly by 4: $8 \div 4 = 2$, then $4 \div 4 = 1$, then $8 \div 4 = 2$, then $4 \div 4 = 1$. The quotient is $2{,}121$. Check: $2{,}121 \times 4 = 8{,}484$.

questions.skill: Divide a four-digit number by a one-digit number
questions.stem: What is $9{,}639 \div 3$?

questions.skill: Divide a four-digit number by a one-digit number
questions.stem: A museum had the same number of visitors on each of 2 days. In all, $6{,}248$ people visited. How many visited on one day?
questions.solution: Share equally between 2 days: $6{,}248 \div 2 = 3{,}124$ visitors a day. Check: $3{,}124 \times 2 = 6{,}248$.

questions.skill: Divide a four-digit number by a one-digit number
questions.stem: Five friends share $5{,}555$ stickers equally. How many stickers does each friend get?
questions.solution: $5{,}555 \div 5 = 1{,}111$. Each friend gets 1,111 stickers.

questions.skill: Find the quotient and remainder
questions.stem: What is the remainder when $2{,}507$ is divided by 5?

questions.skill: Find the quotient and remainder
questions.stem: What is $2{,}403 \div 4$? Give the quotient with its remainder.

questions.skill: Find the quotient and remainder
questions.stem: A teacher has $1{,}608$ stickers and puts them in packs of 5. After making as many full packs as she can, how many stickers are left over?
questions.solution: $5 \times 321 = 1{,}605$, and $1{,}608 - 1{,}605 = 3$. Three stickers are left over.

questions.skill: Find the quotient and remainder
questions.stem: Which of these could be the remainder when a whole number is divided by 7?
questions.solution: A remainder must be less than the divisor. Only 6 is less than 7.

solve.work: A remainder on dividing by 7 must be 0 to 6. Only 6 qualifies.

questions.skill: Interpret a remainder in context
questions.stem: A ribbon is $1{,}001$ centimeters long. Mina cuts it into pieces that are each 3 centimeters long. How many whole pieces can she cut?
questions.solution: $1{,}001 \div 3 = 333$ with remainder 2. The 2 leftover centimeters are too short for another piece, so she can cut 333 whole pieces.

questions.skill: Interpret a remainder in context
questions.stem: Each row in a stadium seats 9 fans. How many rows are needed to seat $1{,}000$ fans?
questions.solution: $1{,}000 \div 9 = 111$ with remainder 1. The last fan needs a seat too, so one more row is needed: $111 + 1 = 112$ rows.

solve.work: 1,000 / 9 = 111 R 1 (9 x 111 = 999). One fan still needs a seat, so 112 rows.

questions.skill: Estimate a product
questions.stem: Which is the best estimate of $398 \times 21$?
questions.solution: Round 398 to 400 and 21 to 20. $400 \times 20 = 8{,}000$. (The exact product is $8{,}358$.)

solve.work: 398 is about 400 and 21 is about 20: 400 x 20 = 8,000 (exact 8,358).

questions.skill: Estimate a product
questions.stem: Round 312 to the nearest hundred and 19 to the nearest ten. Then multiply the two rounded numbers. What is the result?
questions.solution: 312 rounds to 300 and 19 rounds to 20. $300 \times 20 = 6{,}000$.

questions.skill: Estimate a product
questions.stem: Each box holds 98 pencils. About how many pencils are in 41 boxes?
questions.solution: Round 98 to 100 and 41 to 40. $100 \times 40 = 4{,}000$ pencils. (The exact number is $4{,}018$.)

questions.skill: Estimate a quotient
questions.stem: To estimate $4{,}012 \div 8$, Lena uses the compatible numbers $4{,}000 \div 8$. What is $4{,}000 \div 8$?
questions.solution: $40 \div 8 = 5$, so $4{,}000 \div 8 = 500$. The estimate is about 500.

questions.skill: Estimate a quotient
questions.stem: Which is closest to $6{,}312 \div 8$?
questions.solution: $6{,}312$ is close to $6{,}400$. $6{,}400 \div 8 = 800$. (The exact answer is 789.)

solve.work: 6,312 is about 6,400 = 8 x 800, so about 800 (exact 789). 800 is 11 away; 700 is 89 away.

questions.skill: Check and connect multiplication and division
questions.solution: Division undoes multiplication. Since $7 \times 1{,}250 = 8{,}750$, we get $8{,}750 \div 7 = 1{,}250$.

questions.skill: Check and connect multiplication and division
questions.stem: Which multiplication can be used to check that $5{,}196 \div 6 = 866$?
questions.solution: To check a division, multiply the quotient by the divisor: $866 \times 6 = 5{,}196$, which is the number that was divided.

solve.work: Quotient x divisor should equal the dividend: 866 x 6 = 5,196.

questions.skill: Estimate a quotient
questions.stem: A grower picked $1{,}792$ pears and packed about the same number into each of 9 boxes. About how many pears are in each box?
questions.solution: Round 1,792 to the nearby number 1,800, which is easy to divide by 9. $1800 \div 9 = 200$. So there are about 200 pears in each box. A box cannot hold about 20 or 2,000, because $9 \times 20$ is only 180 and $9 \times 2000$ is 18,000.

questions.skill: Multiply a three-digit number by a two-digit number
questions.stem: Find $467 \times 38$.

questions.skill: Interpret a remainder in a division problem
questions.stem: Pencils are packed 8 to a box. A school has $1{,}250$ pencils. How many boxes are needed to pack all of the pencils?
questions.solution: $1{,}250 \div 8 = 156$ with a remainder of 2. The 156 full boxes hold $1{,}248$ pencils, and the 2 pencils left over need one more box. So 157 boxes are needed.

solve.work: 1,250 / 8 = 156 R 2 (8 x 156 = 1,248). The 2 leftover pencils need one more box, so 157 boxes.

questions.skill: Long division with a zero in the quotient
questions.stem: What is $2{,}436 \div 6$?
questions.solution: $24 \div 6 = 4$ (hundreds). The 3 tens cannot be shared by 6, so the tens digit is 0. Then $36 \div 6 = 6$ (ones). The quotient is 406. Check: $406 \times 6 = 2{,}436$.

questions.skill: Multiply a three-digit number by a two-digit number
questions.stem: Dev multiplies 308 by 46. What product should he get?

questions.skill: Multiply a three-digit number by a two-digit number
questions.stem: A warehouse stacks boxes in 27 rows. Each row has 342 boxes. How many boxes are in the warehouse?

questions.skill: Multiply a three-digit number by a two-digit number
questions.stem: Ana says that $256 \times 34 = 1{,}792$. Which sentence explains what she most likely did?
choices: She multiplied 256 by the tens digit 3 only.
She added $256 \times 4$ and $256 \times 3$, but she should have added $256 \times 4$ and $256 \times 30$.
She multiplied 256 by the ones digit 4 only.
She added 256 and 34 instead of multiplying.
questions.answer: She added $256 \times 4$ and $256 \times 3$, but she should have added $256 \times 4$ and $256 \times 30$.
questions.solution: $256 \times 4 = 1{,}024$ and $256 \times 3 = 768$, and $1{,}024 + 768 = 1{,}792$. Ana forgot that the 3 in 34 means 30. The correct product is $1{,}024 + 7{,}680 = 8{,}704$.

solve.answer: She added $256 \times 4$ and $256 \times 3$, but she should have added $256 \times 4$ and $256 \times 30$.
solve.work: Correct: 256 x 34 = 8,704. 256 x 4 = 1,024 and 256 x 3 = 768; 1,024 + 768 = 1,792, which is her answer. So she used 3 instead of 30. 256 x 3 = 768, 256 x 4 = 1,024, 256 + 34 = 290 all differ from 1,792.

questions.skill: Multiply a three-digit number by a two-digit number
questions.stem: A rectangular parking lot is 215 feet long and 48 feet wide. What is its area in square feet?
questions.solution: Area = length $\times$ width. $215 \times 8 = 1{,}720$ and $215 \times 40 = 8{,}600$. Add: $1{,}720 + 8{,}600 = 10{,}320$ square feet.

questions.skill: Multiply a three-digit number by a two-digit number
questions.stem: A printer prints 156 pages each minute. How many pages does it print in 35 minutes?

questions.skill: Multiply a three-digit number by a two-digit number
questions.stem: Each tablet costs 438 dollars. A school buys 26 tablets. How many dollars does the school pay?

questions.skill: Multiply by multiples of ten and one hundred
questions.stem: A shipping center sends out 450 packages every hour. How many packages does it send out in 60 hours?
questions.solution: $45 \times 6 = 270$. Then add the 2 zeros that end $450$ and $60$ (one each): $450 \times 60 = 27{,}000$ packages.

questions.skill: Multiply by multiples of ten and one hundred
questions.stem: Find $85 \times 300$.
questions.solution: $85 \times 3 = 255$. Then multiplying by 100 adds two zeros: $85 \times 300 = 25{,}500$.

questions.skill: Divide a four-digit number by a one-digit number
questions.stem: A factory made $7{,}128$ toy cars and packed them 8 to a box. How many boxes did it fill?

questions.skill: Divide a four-digit number by a one-digit number
questions.stem: A school has $6{,}534$ pencils to share equally among 9 classes. How many pencils does each class get?

questions.skill: Divide a four-digit number by a one-digit number
questions.stem: A bakery uses $4{,}536$ grams of flour for 6 identical batches of bread. How many grams of flour are in each batch?

questions.skill: Divide a four-digit number by a one-digit number
questions.stem: How many groups of 7 are in $8{,}232$?

questions.skill: Divide a four-digit number by a one-digit number
questions.stem: Ruth uses all $3{,}185$ beads to make 5 equal strings. How many beads are on each string?

questions.skill: Long division with a zero in the quotient
