solve.answer: Each number in A is 3 more than the matching number in B
solve.work: A: 0, 6, 12, 18; B: 0, 3, 6, 9. '3 more' fails (0 vs 0, 12 vs 6). 2 times, half, and the adding rules are all true. So the NOT-true statement is the '3 more' one.

questions.skill: Describe the relationship between matching terms of two patterns
questions.stem: Pattern A is 6, 12, 18, 24. Pattern B is 2, 4, 6, 8. Each number in A is how many times the matching number in B?
questions.solution: Match them up: $6 \to 2$, $12 \to 4$, $18 \to 6$, $24 \to 8$. Each number in A is $6 \div 2 = 3$ times the matching number in B.

questions.skill: Describe the relationship between matching terms of two patterns
questions.stem: Pattern C is 1, 2, 3, 4. Pattern D is 5, 10, 15, 20. Maya says each number in D is 4 more than the matching number in C, because 5 is 4 more than 1. Why is she wrong?
choices: 10 is not 4 more than 2; each number in D is 5 times the one in C
Each number in C is 5 times the matching number in D
The numbers in D are smaller than the numbers in C
questions.answer: 10 is not 4 more than 2; each number in D is 5 times the one in C
questions.solution: Check the next pair: 10 is 8 more than 2, not 4 more. The difference keeps changing. What stays the same is the multiplier: $1 \to 5$, $2 \to 10$, $3 \to 15$, $4 \to 20$, so each number in D is 5 times the number in C.

solve.answer: 10 is not 4 more than 2; each number in D is 5 times the one in C
solve.work: 10 - 2 = 8, not 4, so 'always 4 more' fails. 5 = 5 x 1, 10 = 5 x 2, ...: D is 5 times C.

questions.skill: Use the relationship between two patterns to find a term
questions.stem: Pattern A is 4, 7, 10, 13, ... Pattern B is 9, 12, 15, 18, ... The 15th number in Pattern A is 46. What is the 15th number in Pattern B?
questions.solution: Match them up: $4 \to 9$, $7 \to 12$, $10 \to 15$. Each number in B is 5 more than the matching number in A. So the 15th number in B is $46 + 5 = 51$.

solve.work: Both add 3; B is always 5 more (9 - 4). 15th in B = 46 + 5 = 51. Check: 9 + 3 x 14 = 51.

questions.skill: Use the relationship between two patterns to find a term
questions.stem: Pattern M is 2, 4, 6, 8, ... Pattern N is 12, 14, 16, 18, ... A number in Pattern N is 86. What is the matching number in Pattern M?
questions.solution: Each number in N is 10 more than the matching number in M ($2 \to 12$, $4 \to 14$). So the matching number in M is $86 - 10 = 76$.

solve.work: Both add 2; N is always 10 more than M. Matching M number = 86 - 10 = 76. Check: 86 is position 38 of N (12 + 2 x 37), and M's 38th is 76.

questions.skill: Use the relationship between two patterns to find a term
questions.stem: Both patterns start at 0. Pattern M adds 3 each time. Each number in Pattern N is 5 times the matching number in Pattern M. What number does Pattern N add each time?
questions.solution: Pattern M is 0, 3, 6, 9, ... Multiplying each by 5 gives Pattern N: 0, 15, 30, 45, ... So Pattern N adds 15 each time.

questions.skill: Patterns with two quantities in real situations
questions.stem: Pool A and Pool B each gain 15 liters of water every minute. After 8 minutes, Pool A has 160 liters. Pool A started with 40 liters and Pool B started with 10 liters. How many liters does Pool B have after 8 minutes?
questions.solution: Both pools gain the same amount, so Pool B always has $40 - 10 = 30$ liters less than Pool A. After 8 minutes Pool B has $160 - 30 = 130$ liters. (Check: $10 + 8 \times 15 = 130$.)

solve.work: Both gain the same, so B is always 40 - 10 = 30 less than A. 160 - 30 = 130. Check: 10 + 15 x 8 = 130.

questions.skill: Patterns with two quantities in real situations
questions.stem: Maya runs 2 laps each day. Her coach runs 6 laps each day. They both start on day 1. By the end of day 5, how many more laps has the coach run than Maya?
questions.solution: The coach has run $5 \times 6 = 30$ laps and Maya has run $5 \times 2 = 10$ laps. The coach has run $30 - 10 = 20$ more laps.

solve.work: By end of day 5: coach 6 x 5 = 30, Maya 2 x 5 = 10. 30 - 10 = 20.

questions.skill: Patterns with two quantities in real situations
questions.stem: One plant is 5 centimeters tall and grows 3 centimeters each week. A second plant is 10 centimeters tall and also grows 3 centimeters each week. Which statement is true after any number of weeks?
choices: The second plant is always twice as tall as the first plant
The second plant is always 3 centimeters taller than the first plant
The second plant is always 5 centimeters taller than the first plant
The second plant grows faster than the first plant
questions.answer: The second plant is always 5 centimeters taller than the first plant
questions.solution: Both plants grow the same amount each week, so the gap stays the same: $10 - 5 = 5$ centimeters. It is not "twice as tall": after 1 week the plants are 8 and 13 centimeters.

solve.answer: The second plant is always 5 centimeters taller than the first plant
solve.work: Heights after w weeks: 5 + 3w and 10 + 3w. The difference is always 5 cm. (Twice as tall only at week 0; same growth rate.)

questions.skill: Compare two patterns
questions.stem: Each of four patterns starts at 2. Which pattern has the greatest 4th number?
questions.solution: 4th numbers: add 20 gives 2, 22, 42, 62 (62); multiply by 3 gives 2, 6, 18, 54 (54); multiply by 2 gives 2, 4, 8, 16 (16); add 10 gives 2, 12, 22, 32 (32). The greatest is 62. (Multiplying grows faster later on, but not by the 4th number here.)

questions.skill: Compare two patterns
questions.stem: Pattern A starts at 2 and multiplies by 2 each time. Pattern B starts at 40 and adds 10 each time. In which position is Pattern A's number first greater than Pattern B's number in the same position?
questions.solution: Pattern A: 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128. Pattern B: 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, 100. In position 6 the numbers are 64 and 90, so A is still smaller. In position 7 the numbers are 128 and 100, so A is greater for the first time.

questions.skill: Compare two patterns
questions.stem: Pattern A starts at 12 and adds 6 each time. Pattern B starts at 36 and adds 2 each time. In which position is Pattern A's number first greater than Pattern B's number in the same position?
questions.solution: Pattern A: 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 54. Pattern B: 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48, 50. In position 7 the numbers are equal (48 and 48). In position 8, A has 54 and B has 50, so A is greater for the first time.

solve.work: A: 12, 18, 24, 30, 36, 42, 48, 54. B: 36, 38, 40, 42, 44, 46, 48, 50. Position 7: both 48 (equal, not greater). Position 8: 54 > 50. First greater at position 8.

questions.skill: Name a quadrilateral from its properties
questions.stem: A quadrilateral has 4 sides of equal length and 4 right angles. Which name describes it most specifically?
questions.solution: A rectangle, a rhombus and a parallelogram all describe it, but a square is the most specific name: it has equal sides and right angles.

solve.work: 4 equal sides and 4 right angles -> square, the most specific name.

questions.skill: Hierarchy: which category fits inside another
questions.stem: Which statement is true?
questions.solution: A square has 4 right angles, which is what makes a rectangle. But a rectangle can have sides of different lengths, so it is not always a square.

solve.work: A square has 4 right angles and opposite sides parallel, so it is a rectangle. The others are false (a rhombus need not have right angles, etc.).

questions.skill: Parallel sides of a rectangle
questions.stem: How many pairs of parallel sides does a rectangle have?
questions.solution: The two long sides are parallel to each other and the two short sides are parallel to each other. That makes 2 pairs.

solve.work: A rectangle is a parallelogram: 2 pairs of parallel sides.

questions.skill: Name a quadrilateral from its properties
questions.stem: Ben draws a four-sided shape that has exactly one pair of parallel sides. What is the name of the shape?
questions.solution: A four-sided shape with exactly one pair of parallel sides is a trapezoid. Parallelograms, rectangles and rhombuses all have two pairs of parallel sides.

solve.work: Exactly one pair of parallel sides is the defining attribute of a trapezoid. Rectangle, rhombus and parallelogram all have two pairs of parallel sides.

questions.skill: Name a quadrilateral from its properties
questions.stem: A four-sided shape has 4 right angles. Its opposite sides are equal, but its sides are not all the same length. What is the most specific name for it?
questions.solution: Four right angles with opposite sides equal makes a rectangle. A square would need all four sides equal, and a rhombus is defined by four equal sides.

solve.work: 4 right angles and opposite sides equal: rectangle. Sides not all equal, so not a square. Most specific: rectangle.

questions.skill: Name a quadrilateral from its properties
questions.stem: Which name always fits a four-sided shape when both pairs of its opposite sides are parallel?
questions.solution: Two pairs of parallel sides is what makes a parallelogram. A square, rectangle or rhombus also needs equal sides or right angles, which this shape does not have to have.

solve.work: Both pairs of opposite sides parallel is the definition of a parallelogram; rhombus, square, rectangle need more and do not always fit.

questions.skill: Name a quadrilateral from its properties
questions.stem: Which kind of shape has four sides that are all equal in length, but does not have to have any right angles?
questions.solution: A rhombus has four equal sides and can be slanted, with no right angles. A square must have right angles. A rectangle or trapezoid does not have to have equal sides.

solve.work: Four equal sides, right angles not required: rhombus. A square must have right angles; trapezoid and rectangle need not have 4 equal sides.

questions.skill: Which category fits inside another
questions.stem: Which of these shapes is always a rectangle?
questions.solution: Every square has four right angles and opposite sides equal, so every square is a rectangle. A rhombus, parallelogram or trapezoid may have no right angles.

solve.work: A square has 4 right angles and opposite sides parallel and equal, so it is always a rectangle. Parallelograms, trapezoids and rhombuses need not have right angles.

questions.skill: Which category fits inside another
questions.stem: Look at two sentences. (1) Every square is a rectangle. (2) Every rectangle is a square. How many of the sentences are true?
questions.solution: Sentence 1 is true: a square has four right angles. Sentence 2 is false: a rectangle with sides of 5 cm and 3 cm is not a square. One sentence is true.

solve.work: (1) True: a square has 4 right angles. (2) False: a 6 by 2 rectangle is not a square. 1 true.

questions.skill: Which category fits inside another
questions.stem: Which statement about rhombuses is true?
choices: A rhombus is not a quadrilateral.
questions.solution: A rhombus has two pairs of parallel sides, so it is a parallelogram. It does not have to have right angles, so it is not always a rectangle or a square.

solve.work: A rhombus has 4 equal sides and both pairs of opposite sides parallel, so it is always a parallelogram. It need not have right angles, so not always a rectangle or square; it is a quadrilateral.

questions.skill: Which category fits inside another
questions.stem: Every rectangle belongs to which larger group of shapes?
questions.solution: A rectangle has two pairs of parallel sides, so it is a parallelogram. Not every rectangle is a rhombus or a square, and a rectangle has four sides, so it is not a triangle.

solve.work: Every rectangle has two pairs of parallel sides, so it is in the parallelograms. Not every rectangle is a rhombus or square; none is a triangle.

questions.skill: Attributes carry down to subcategories
questions.stem: All parallelograms have opposite sides that are equal in length. A rectangle is a kind of parallelogram. What must be true of a rectangle?
choices: All four of its sides are equal.
Its opposite sides are equal in length.
Its sides are all different lengths.
questions.answer: Its opposite sides are equal in length.
questions.solution: What is true of every parallelogram is true of every rectangle, because a rectangle is a parallelogram. So a rectangle has opposite sides equal.

solve.answer: Its opposite sides are equal in length.
solve.work: Attribute of the parent group carries to the subgroup: a rectangle's opposite sides are equal. It has right angles, and need not have 4 equal sides.

questions.skill: Attributes carry down to subcategories
questions.stem: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal in length. A rectangle is a parallelogram. One side of a rectangle is 9 cm long. How long is the side directly across from it, in centimeters?
questions.solution: A rectangle is a parallelogram, so its opposite sides are equal. The side across from the 9 cm side is also 9 cm.

solve.work: Rectangle is a parallelogram, so opposite sides are equal: 9 cm.

questions.skill: Attributes carry down to subcategories
questions.stem: A rhombus has four equal sides, and a square is a kind of rhombus. What is true of every square?
choices: Only two of its sides are equal.
None of its sides are equal.
Its sides are all different lengths.
All four of its sides are equal.
questions.answer: All four of its sides are equal.
questions.solution: Every attribute of rhombuses carries down to squares. So every square has four equal sides.

solve.answer: All four of its sides are equal.
solve.work: A square is a rhombus, so it has four equal sides.

questions.skill: Attributes carry down to subcategories
questions.stem: Every rectangle has 4 right angles. A square is a kind of rectangle. How many right angles does a square have?
questions.solution: A square is a rectangle, so it has every attribute of a rectangle, including 4 right angles.

solve.work: A square is a rectangle, so it has 4 right angles.

questions.skill: Always, sometimes or never true
questions.stem: A rectangle is sometimes a square. Which of these rectangles is a square?
choices: A rectangle with sides of 8 cm, 4 cm, 8 cm and 4 cm
A rectangle with sides of 5 cm, 3 cm, 5 cm and 3 cm
A rectangle with sides of 6 cm, 6 cm, 6 cm and 6 cm
A rectangle with sides of 9 cm, 2 cm, 9 cm and 2 cm
questions.answer: A rectangle with sides of 6 cm, 6 cm, 6 cm and 6 cm
questions.solution: A rectangle is a square when all four sides are equal. Only the first rectangle has four equal sides.

solve.answer: A rectangle with sides of 6 cm, 6 cm, 6 cm and 6 cm
solve.work: A rectangle with all 4 sides equal (6, 6, 6, 6) is a square. The others have two different side lengths.

questions.skill: Always, sometimes or never true
questions.stem: Which statement is NEVER true?
choices: A square has four equal sides.
A rhombus has four equal sides.
A parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides.
A rectangle has exactly one right angle.
questions.answer: A rectangle has exactly one right angle.
questions.solution: Every rectangle has four right angles, so it can never have exactly one. The other three statements are always true.

solve.answer: A rectangle has exactly one right angle.
solve.work: Every rectangle has 4 right angles, so exactly one right angle never happens. A, C, D are always true.

questions.skill: Always, sometimes or never true
questions.stem: Read three sentences. (1) A square has 4 right angles. (2) A rectangle has 4 equal sides. (3) A rhombus has 4 equal sides. How many of the sentences are true for EVERY shape of that kind?
questions.solution: Sentences 1 and 3 are true for every square and every rhombus. Sentence 2 is false: a rectangle with sides of 5 cm and 3 cm does not have 4 equal sides. The answer is 2.

solve.work: (1) true for every square. (2) false (6 by 2 rectangle). (3) true for every rhombus. Count 2.

questions.skill: Always, sometimes or never true
questions.stem: Which shape is ALWAYS a parallelogram?
choices: A trapezoid with exactly one pair of parallel sides
A four-sided shape with one right angle
questions.solution: Every rectangle has two pairs of parallel sides, so it is always a parallelogram. The other shapes can have fewer parallel sides.

solve.work: A rectangle has two pairs of parallel sides, so always a parallelogram. Trapezoid with one pair: never. Any quadrilateral or one with one right angle: not always.

questions.skill: Count shapes that have an attribute
questions.stem: Zoe has three shape cards: Rectangle, Rhombus and Square. She keeps only the cards for shapes that ALWAYS have four right angles. How many cards does she keep?
questions.solution: Every rectangle and every square has four right angles. A rhombus can be slanted with no right angles. She keeps 2 cards.

solve.work: Rectangle: always 4 right angles. Square: always. Rhombus: not always. Keep 2.

questions.skill: Count shapes that have an attribute
questions.stem: A class makes a poster of four shapes: square, rectangle, parallelogram and rhombus. Under the heading "Both pairs of opposite sides are equal in length" the teacher writes every shape that ALWAYS fits. How many shapes does she write under the heading?
questions.solution: Every parallelogram has opposite sides equal, and rectangles, rhombuses and squares are all parallelograms. So all 4 shapes fit.

solve.work: All four are parallelograms, so all have both pairs of opposite sides equal: 4.

questions.skill: Count shapes that have an attribute
questions.stem: A shape bin holds four shapes: a square, a rectangle, a parallelogram and a trapezoid with exactly one pair of parallel sides. How many of the shapes have two pairs of parallel sides?
questions.solution: The square, the rectangle and the parallelogram each have two pairs of parallel sides. The trapezoid has only one pair. The answer is 3.

solve.work: Square, rectangle, parallelogram have two pairs of parallel sides; the trapezoid has one. 3.

questions.skill: Tell two categories apart
questions.stem: Lin has two quadrilaterals. Both have two pairs of parallel sides. One is a rectangle. The other is a parallelogram that is not a rectangle. How can Lin tell them apart?
choices: Check whether opposite sides are parallel.
Check whether all four angles are right angles.
Check whether opposite sides are equal in length.
questions.answer: Check whether all four angles are right angles.
questions.solution: Both shapes have four sides, parallel opposite sides and equal opposite sides. Only the rectangle must have four right angles.

solve.answer: Check whether all four angles are right angles.
solve.work: Both are parallelograms, so both have 4 sides, parallel and equal opposite sides. Only the rectangle has 4 right angles.

questions.skill: Tell two categories apart
questions.stem: Which is true of a parallelogram but NOT true of a trapezoid that has exactly one pair of parallel sides?
choices: It has at least one pair of parallel sides.
Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
questions.answer: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
questions.solution: Both shapes have four sides, are quadrilaterals and have at least one pair of parallel sides. Only the parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides.

solve.answer: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel.
solve.work: Both have four sides, are quadrilaterals, and have at least one pair of parallel sides. Only the parallelogram has both pairs parallel.

questions.skill: Tell two categories apart
questions.stem: A rectangle that is not a square has 2 different side lengths. How many different side lengths does a square have?
questions.solution: All four sides of a square are equal, so a square has just 1 side length.

solve.work: All four sides of a square are equal: 1 side length.

questions.skill: Tell two categories apart
questions.stem: Which shape has all the attributes of a parallelogram and also has four equal sides?
questions.solution: A rhombus is a parallelogram with four equal sides. A rectangle does not have to have equal sides, and a trapezoid or a general quadrilateral is not a parallelogram.

solve.work: A parallelogram with four equal sides is a rhombus. A rectangle need not have 4 equal sides; trapezoid and quadrilateral need not be parallelograms.

questions.skill: Combine clues to identify a shape
questions.stem: A mystery shape is both a rectangle and a rhombus. One of its sides is 5 cm long. How long is the side next to it, in centimeters?
questions.solution: A shape that is both a rectangle and a rhombus is a square, because it has four right angles and four equal sides. So the side next to the 5 cm side is also 5 cm.

solve.work: Both rectangle and rhombus = square: all sides equal, 5 cm.

questions.skill: Combine clues to identify a shape
questions.stem: Pia says her shape is a square. Which statement about her shape must be true?
choices: Only its opposite sides are equal.
All its sides are equal and it has four right angles.
Exactly one pair of its sides is parallel.
questions.answer: All its sides are equal and it has four right angles.
questions.solution: A square has both attributes together: four equal sides and four right angles.

solve.answer: All its sides are equal and it has four right angles.
solve.work: A square has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles. Other options contradict that.

questions.skill: Classify by attributes
questions.stem: A quadrilateral has 4 right angles. Which name must fit it?
choices: Trapezoid, with one pair of parallel sides
questions.solution: A quadrilateral with 4 right angles is a rectangle. It might also be a square, but it does not have to be. It is not always a square or a rhombus, because its sides do not have to be equal. A trapezoid with one pair of parallel sides cannot have 4 right angles, because then both pairs of its sides would be parallel.

solve.work: Four right angles means a rectangle by definition; it need not have equal sides (so not necessarily square or rhombus), and a trapezoid with exactly one pair of parallel sides cannot have 4 right angles.

questions.skill: Attributes carry down the hierarchy
questions.stem: Every parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides. A rectangle is a parallelogram, and a square is a rectangle. How many pairs of parallel sides does a square have?
questions.solution: A square is a rectangle, and a rectangle is a parallelogram. Each group passes its attributes down to the shapes inside it, so a square has the 2 pairs of parallel sides that every parallelogram has.

solve.work: A square is a rectangle, which is a parallelogram, so it inherits two pairs of parallel sides.

questions.skill: Place a shape in the hierarchy
questions.stem: The group of rectangles sits inside the group of parallelograms. Which of these shapes sits inside the group of rectangles?
choices: Trapezoid, with one pair of parallel sides
questions.solution: A square has 4 right angles and opposite sides that are equal, so every square is a rectangle and sits inside that group. A rhombus, a parallelogram or a trapezoid can have angles that are not right angles, so they are not always rectangles.

solve.work: Squares are rectangles with four equal sides; rhombuses and parallelograms are not always rectangles; a trapezoid with one pair of parallel sides is never one.

questions.skill: Attributes carry down the hierarchy
questions.stem: Every parallelogram has opposite angles that are equal in size. A rectangle is a kind of parallelogram. One angle of a rectangle measures 90 degrees. How many degrees does the angle opposite it (across the shape from it) measure?
questions.solution: A rectangle is a parallelogram, so its opposite angles are equal. The angle opposite a 90 degree angle is also 90 degrees.

solve.work: Rectangle is a parallelogram, opposite angles equal, so the opposite angle is 90.

questions.skill: Attributes carry down the hierarchy
questions.stem: A rhombus has one side that is 5 centimeters long. How many of its four sides are 5 centimeters long, counting that side?
questions.solution: Every rhombus has four sides of equal length. If one side is 5 centimeters, all four sides are 5 centimeters.

solve.work: A rhombus has four equal sides, so all 4 are 5 cm.

questions.skill: Attributes that every rhombus has
questions.stem: Which attribute do ALL rhombuses have?
choices: Opposite sides that are different lengths
Exactly one pair of parallel sides
questions.solution: A rhombus is defined by four sides of equal length. Only some rhombuses (squares) have right angles. A rhombus has 2 pairs of parallel sides, and all its sides are equal.

solve.work: A rhombus is defined by four equal sides. Right angles not required; it has 2 pairs of parallel sides; opposite sides are equal.

questions.skill: Shapes that always have four right angles
questions.stem: Which list contains only shapes that ALWAYS have four right angles?
questions.solution: Squares and rectangles always have four right angles. Rhombuses and parallelograms can lean over, so their angles are not always right angles.

solve.work: Squares and rectangles always have four right angles; rhombuses and parallelograms need not.

questions.skill: Use an attribute of a category to find a measurement
questions.stem: A rhombus has four sides of equal length. One side is 7 centimeters long. What is the perimeter of the rhombus, in centimeters?
questions.solution: All 4 sides are 7 centimeters long, so the perimeter is $4 \times 7 = 28$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Name a quadrilateral from its properties
questions.stem: A quadrilateral has two pairs of parallel sides, and its opposite sides are equal in length. It has no right angles, and its sides are not all equal. What is the most specific name for it?
questions.solution: Two pairs of parallel sides makes it a parallelogram. It is not a rectangle (no right angles) or a rhombus (sides not all equal), so parallelogram is the most specific name.

solve.work: Two pairs of parallel sides: parallelogram. No right angles: not rectangle/square. Sides not all equal: not rhombus. Most specific: parallelogram.

questions.skill: Name a quadrilateral from its properties
questions.stem: Which description fits a rhombus that is not a square?
choices: Four equal sides and four right angles
Four equal sides and no right angles
Opposite sides equal and four right angles
Exactly one pair of parallel sides and no right angles
questions.answer: Four equal sides and no right angles
questions.solution: A rhombus has four equal sides. If it also had four right angles it would be a square, so a rhombus that is not a square has no right angles.

solve.answer: Four equal sides and no right angles
solve.work: A rhombus has 4 equal sides. If it is not a square it has no right angles (one right angle in a parallelogram forces all four). Option A is a trapezoid, C a rectangle, D a square.

questions.skill: Name a quadrilateral from its properties
questions.stem: A game card says: "I have 4 sides. Both pairs of my opposite sides are parallel. All 4 of my sides are equal. I have no right angles." What is the most specific name of the shape on the card?
questions.solution: Four equal sides and two pairs of parallel sides make a rhombus. With no right angles it cannot be a square.

solve.work: Two pairs of parallel sides, 4 equal sides, no right angles: rhombus, not square.

questions.skill: Name a quadrilateral from its properties
questions.stem: Four quadrilaterals are described. Shape 1 has 4 right angles. Shape 2 has 4 equal sides. Shape 3 has two pairs of parallel sides. Shape 4 has exactly one pair of parallel sides. How many of the four shapes are certain to be parallelograms?
questions.solution: Shape 1 is a rectangle, Shape 2 is a rhombus and Shape 3 has two pairs of parallel sides, so all three are parallelograms. Shape 4 has only one pair of parallel sides, so it is not. The answer is 3.

solve.work: Shape 1: 4 right angles = rectangle, a parallelogram. Shape 2: 4 equal sides = rhombus, a parallelogram. Shape 3: two pairs parallel = parallelogram. Shape 4: exactly one pair = trapezoid, not a parallelogram. Total 3.

questions.skill: Which category fits inside another
questions.stem: A teacher draws a chart. At the top is the group of quadrilaterals. Inside it is the group of parallelograms. Inside parallelograms are rectangles and rhombuses. Inside both of those groups are squares. A square belongs to how many of these four groups: quadrilaterals, parallelograms, rectangles, rhombuses?
questions.solution: A square is a rectangle and a rhombus. Both of those are parallelograms, and every parallelogram is a quadrilateral. So a square belongs to all 4 groups.

solve.work: Squares are inside rectangles and rhombuses, both inside parallelograms, inside quadrilaterals. A square is in all 4 groups.

questions.skill: Which category fits inside another
questions.stem: Which list puts the groups in order from the biggest group to the smallest, so that each group fits inside the one before it?
questions.solution: All quadrilaterals is the biggest group. Parallelograms fit inside it, rectangles fit inside parallelograms, and squares fit inside rectangles.

solve.work: Quadrilaterals contain parallelograms, which contain rectangles, which contain squares. Option A.

questions.skill: Which category fits inside another
questions.stem: Which statement about rectangles and rhombuses is true?
choices: Some shapes are both a rectangle and a rhombus.
No shape is both a rectangle and a rhombus.
questions.answer: Some shapes are both a rectangle and a rhombus.
questions.solution: A square has four right angles and four equal sides, so it is both a rectangle and a rhombus. But a 5 by 3 rectangle is not a rhombus, and a slanted rhombus is not a rectangle.

solve.answer: Some shapes are both a rectangle and a rhombus.
solve.work: A square is both a rectangle and a rhombus, so C is true and D false. A 6 by 2 rectangle is not a rhombus; a rhombus with no right angles is not a rectangle, so A and B are false.

questions.skill: Which category fits inside another
questions.stem: Pam writes four sentences about a rhombus. (1) A rhombus is a parallelogram. (2) A rhombus is a rectangle. (3) A rhombus is a quadrilateral. (4) A rhombus is a square. How many of the sentences are always true?
questions.solution: Every rhombus is a parallelogram and a quadrilateral, so sentences 1 and 3 are always true. A rhombus does not have to have right angles, so 2 and 4 are not always true. The answer is 2.

solve.work: (1) always true. (2) not always (rhombus without right angles). (3) always true. (4) not always. Count 2.

questions.skill: Attributes carry down to subcategories
questions.stem: Which attribute is shared by parallelograms, rectangles, rhombuses AND squares?
choices: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel
All four angles are right angles
Exactly one pair of sides is parallel
questions.answer: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel
questions.solution: Rectangles, rhombuses and squares are all kinds of parallelograms, so they all have two pairs of parallel sides. Right angles belong only to rectangles and squares, and equal sides only to rhombuses and squares.

solve.answer: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel
solve.work: All four are parallelograms, so all have both pairs of opposite sides parallel. Not all have 4 equal sides or 4 right angles; none has exactly one pair parallel.

questions.skill: Attributes carry down to subcategories
questions.stem: Which attribute do squares get from rectangles that rhombuses do not need to have?
questions.solution: Rhombuses already have four equal sides, parallel opposite sides and four sides. Only rectangles are required to have four right angles, and squares are rectangles.

solve.work: Rectangles give four right angles; rhombuses need not have them. Four equal sides comes from rhombuses; four sides and parallel sides are shared by both.

questions.skill: Attributes carry down to subcategories
questions.stem: A rhombus has these three attributes: it has 4 sides, it has 4 equal sides, and it has 2 pairs of parallel sides. A square is a kind of rhombus. How many of these three attributes does every square have?
questions.solution: All the attributes of a rhombus carry down to a square. So a square has all 3 of them.

solve.work: Every attribute of a rhombus carries to a square, which is a kind of rhombus: all 3.

questions.skill: Attributes carry down to subcategories
questions.stem: Rina knows that every rhombus has four equal sides and that every square is a rhombus. A square has a perimeter of 20 cm. What can Rina say about its sides?
choices: The side length cannot be found.
questions.solution: A square is a rhombus, so its four sides are equal. Each side is 20 divided by 4, which is 5 cm.

solve.work: Square is a rhombus, so 4 equal sides: 20 / 4 = 5 cm each.

questions.skill: Always, sometimes or never true
questions.stem: Jo says: "Every parallelogram has four right angles." Which shape shows that Jo is wrong?
choices: A rectangle with sides of 7 cm and 4 cm
A parallelogram with sides of 7 cm and 4 cm and no right angles
A square with sides of 4 cm
A rectangle with sides of 5 cm and 3 cm
questions.answer: A parallelogram with sides of 7 cm and 4 cm and no right angles
questions.solution: To show a claim is false you need a shape that is a parallelogram but does not have four right angles. The rectangles and the square all have four right angles, so they cannot show Jo is wrong.

solve.answer: A parallelogram with sides of 7 cm and 4 cm and no right angles
solve.work: A counterexample needs a parallelogram without four right angles: the 7 by 4 parallelogram with no right angles. Squares and rectangles have right angles.

questions.skill: Always, sometimes or never true
questions.stem: Which of these statements is true only SOMETIMES?
choices: A rhombus has four equal sides.
A rectangle has four right angles.
A square has four right angles.
questions.solution: Some parallelograms have four equal sides and some do not, so "A parallelogram is a rhombus" is only sometimes true. The other three are always true.

solve.work: A, C, D are always true. A parallelogram is a rhombus only when its sides are all equal: sometimes.

questions.skill: Always, sometimes or never true
questions.stem: Amir tests the claim "Every rectangle is a square" with these rectangles, with side lengths in cm: 5 and 5, 8 and 3, 4 and 4, 10 and 2, 6 and 9. How many of these rectangles show that the claim is false?
questions.solution: A rectangle shows the claim is false when its sides are not all equal. The rectangles 8 by 3, 10 by 2 and 6 by 9 do that. The 5 by 5 and 4 by 4 rectangles are squares. The answer is 3.

solve.work: Non-squares: 8 by 3, 10 by 2, 6 by 9. 5 by 5 and 4 by 4 are squares. Count 3.

questions.skill: Always, sometimes or never true
questions.stem: Which statement is NOT always true of a rectangle?
choices: It has two pairs of parallel sides.
questions.solution: A rectangle with sides of 5 cm and 3 cm has four right angles, equal opposite sides and two pairs of parallel sides, but its four sides are not all equal.

solve.work: Rectangles always have two pairs of parallel sides, 4 right angles and opposite sides equal; four equal sides only if it is a square.

questions.skill: Use attributes to find a measurement
questions.stem: A rhombus-shaped tile has a perimeter of 26 cm. How long is each side of the tile, in centimeters?
questions.solution: A rhombus has four equal sides, so each side is 26 divided by 4 = 6.5 cm.

solve.issues: Borderline alignment: mostly perimeter arithmetic, though it does require recalling that a rhombus has four equal sides.
solve.work: A rhombus has 4 equal sides: 26 / 4 = 6.5 cm.

questions.skill: Count shapes that have an attribute
questions.stem: How many of these five shapes ALWAYS have at least one right angle: square, rectangle, rhombus, parallelogram, trapezoid with exactly one pair of parallel sides?
questions.solution: Squares and rectangles always have four right angles. A rhombus, a parallelogram and a trapezoid can all be drawn with no right angles. The answer is 2.

solve.work: Square and rectangle always have right angles. Rhombus, parallelogram and trapezoid may have none. 2.

questions.skill: Count shapes that have an attribute
questions.stem: A teacher has shape cards. 4 cards show squares, 3 show rectangles that are not squares, 2 show rhombuses that are not squares, and 5 show parallelograms that are neither rectangles nor rhombuses. How many cards show a shape with four equal sides?
questions.solution: Squares and rhombuses have four equal sides. That is 4 + 2 = 6 cards. Rectangles that are not squares and the other parallelograms do not have four equal sides.

solve.work: Four equal sides: squares (4) and rhombuses that are not squares (2). 4 + 2 = 6.

questions.skill: Count shapes that have an attribute
questions.stem: Kim sorts cards for these shapes: square, rectangle, rhombus, trapezoid with exactly one pair of parallel sides, and quadrilateral. She puts a card in the "parallelogram" pile only if the shape is ALWAYS a parallelogram. How many cards go in that pile?
questions.solution: Squares, rectangles and rhombuses are always parallelograms. A trapezoid with exactly one pair of parallel sides and a general quadrilateral are not. The answer is 3.

solve.work: Square, rectangle, rhombus are always parallelograms. Trapezoid with one pair: never. Quadrilateral: not always. 3.

questions.skill: Count shapes that have an attribute
questions.stem: Six quadrilaterals are described. A: sides 6, 6, 6, 6 cm; four right angles. B: sides 8, 3, 8, 3 cm; four right angles. C: sides 5, 5, 5, 5 cm; no right angles. D: sides 9, 4, 9, 4 cm; no right angles. E: sides 2, 2, 2, 2 cm; four right angles. F: exactly one pair of parallel sides. How many of the six are rectangles?
questions.solution: A rectangle has four right angles. A, B and E have four right angles, so they are rectangles (A and E are squares). C and D have no right angles, and F has only one pair of parallel sides. The answer is 3.

solve.work: Rectangles need 4 right angles: A (square), B, E (square). C, D have no right angles; F is a trapezoid. 3.

questions.skill: Tell two categories apart
questions.stem: Two quadrilaterals each have four right angles. Shape A has four equal sides. Shape B has sides of 5 cm, 3 cm, 5 cm and 3 cm. What are the most specific names for Shape A and Shape B?
choices: A is a rectangle and B is a square.
A is a square and B is a rectangle.
A is a rhombus and B is a square.
A is a rectangle and B is a rhombus.
questions.answer: A is a square and B is a rectangle.
questions.solution: Four right angles and four equal sides is a square. Four right angles with sides 5, 3, 5, 3 is a rectangle that is not a square.

solve.answer: A is a square and B is a rectangle.
solve.work: A: 4 right angles and 4 equal sides = square. B: 4 right angles, sides 5, 3, 5, 3 = rectangle (not square).

questions.skill: Tell two categories apart
questions.stem: Sana's mystery quadrilateral is either a rectangle with sides of 6 cm and 4 cm or a rhombus with no right angles. Which measurement would tell her it is the rhombus?
choices: Two opposite sides are equal in length.
One of its angles is not a right angle.
questions.answer: One of its angles is not a right angle.
questions.solution: Both shapes have four sides, parallel opposite sides and equal opposite sides. A rectangle has only right angles, so an angle that is not a right angle shows the shape is the rhombus.

solve.answer: One of its angles is not a right angle.
solve.work: The rectangle has all right angles; the rhombus has none. Both have 4 sides, parallel and equal opposite sides. A non-right angle identifies the rhombus.

questions.skill: Tell two categories apart
questions.stem: A quadrilateral has four right angles. Its perimeter is 24 cm and one of its sides is 6 cm long. How long is a side next to the 6 cm side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: Half the perimeter is 24 divided by 2 = 12 cm, which is two side lengths added. The side next to the 6 cm side is 12 - 6 = 6 cm. So all four sides are 6 cm and the shape is a square.

solve.work: Four right angles = rectangle, opposite sides equal. Adjacent sides sum to 12; 12 - 6 = 6 cm (it is a square).

questions.skill: Combine clues to identify a shape
questions.stem: Which shape fits all three clues? Clue 1: Both pairs of opposite sides are parallel. Clue 2: Opposite sides are equal, but sides next to each other have different lengths. Clue 3: Not every angle is a right angle.
choices: A parallelogram that is not a rectangle
questions.answer: A parallelogram that is not a rectangle
questions.solution: Clue 2 rules out a rhombus and a square (their sides are all equal). Clue 3 rules out a rectangle. A parallelogram with no right angles and unequal neighboring sides fits all three clues.

solve.answer: A parallelogram that is not a rectangle
solve.issues: Minor: option B also includes non-square rhombuses, which fail clue 2; 'neither a rectangle nor a rhombus' would be exact. Still the only defensible choice.
solve.work: Clue 1: parallelogram. Clue 2: adjacent sides differ, so not a rhombus/square. Clue 3: not a rectangle. Only B can fit.

questions.skill: Combine clues to identify a shape
questions.stem: Shape A has 4 right angles and sides of 7 cm and 3 cm. Shape B has 4 equal sides, each the same length as the longer side of Shape A. How many centimeters longer is the perimeter of Shape B than the perimeter of Shape A?
questions.solution: Shape A is a rectangle with perimeter 2 x (7 + 3) = 20 cm. Shape B has four sides of 7 cm, so its perimeter is 4 x 7 = 28 cm. The difference is 28 - 20 = 8 cm.

solve.work: A: rectangle 7 by 3, perimeter 20. B: 4 sides of 7, perimeter 28. 28 - 20 = 8 cm.

questions.skill: Combine clues to identify a shape
questions.stem: Priya says her mystery quadrilateral is a rhombus and also a rectangle. What else can she be sure of?
choices: It has exactly one pair of parallel sides.
Its sides are not all equal.
questions.solution: Being a rhombus means four equal sides. Being a rectangle means four right angles. Together those describe a square.

solve.work: Rhombus (4 equal sides) and rectangle (4 right angles) together = square.

questions.skill: Count the names that fit a shape
questions.stem: Here are six names: quadrilateral, trapezoid with exactly one pair of parallel sides, parallelogram, rectangle, rhombus and square. How many of these six names always fit a square?
questions.solution: A square is a quadrilateral, a parallelogram, a rectangle, a rhombus and a square, which is 5 names. It is not a trapezoid with exactly one pair of parallel sides, because a square has two pairs of parallel sides.

solve.work: A square is a quadrilateral, parallelogram, rectangle, rhombus and square (5). It has two pairs of parallel sides, so 'trapezoid with exactly one pair' does not fit.

questions.skill: Sort shapes by an attribute
questions.stem: Mia describes six quadrilaterals: a square; a rectangle that is not a square; a rhombus that is not a square; a parallelogram with no right angles and sides that are not all equal; a trapezoid with exactly one pair of parallel sides; and a quadrilateral with no parallel sides. How many of the six are parallelograms?
questions.solution: A parallelogram has two pairs of parallel sides. The square, the rectangle, the rhombus and the parallelogram all have them, so that is 4. The trapezoid has only one pair and the last shape has none.

solve.work: Parallelograms: square, rectangle, rhombus, the general parallelogram = 4. The trapezoid (exactly one pair) and the quadrilateral with no parallel sides are not.

questions.skill: Reason from the hierarchy
questions.stem: Every rhombus has opposite sides that are parallel. Every square is a rhombus. Which conclusion must be true?
choices: Every square has opposite sides that are parallel
Every rhombus has four right angles
Every shape with parallel opposite sides is a square
questions.answer: Every square has opposite sides that are parallel
questions.solution: A square is inside the group of rhombuses, so it has every attribute of a rhombus, including parallel opposite sides. The other statements go the wrong way: rhombuses are not all squares, and many shapes with parallel opposite sides are not squares.

solve.answer: Every square has opposite sides that are parallel
solve.work: Squares are rhombuses, rhombuses have parallel opposite sides, so every square does. The others reverse the inclusion.

questions.skill: Attributes carry down to subcategories
questions.stem: Which statement about the attributes of quadrilaterals is true?
choices: Every attribute of a square is also an attribute of a rectangle.
Every attribute of a rhombus is also an attribute of a rectangle.
Every attribute of a square is also an attribute of a rhombus.
Every attribute of a rectangle is also an attribute of a square.
questions.answer: Every attribute of a rectangle is also an attribute of a square.
questions.solution: A square is a kind of rectangle, so it has every attribute that rectangles have. The other statements fail: a square has four equal sides, which a rectangle does not always have, and a square has right angles, which a rhombus does not always have.

solve.answer: Every attribute of a rectangle is also an attribute of a square.
solve.work: A square is a special rectangle, so every property all rectangles have (4 right angles, opposite sides parallel and equal) holds for squares. Square->rectangle fails (equal sides), square->rhombus fails (right angles), rhombus->rectangle fails (right angles).

questions.skill: Use a counterexample to test a claim
questions.stem: Sam says: "This shape has four sides of equal length, so it must be a square." Which shape shows that Sam is wrong?
choices: A rhombus with angles of 60 degrees and 120 degrees
A rectangle with sides 4 centimeters and 6 centimeters
A square with sides of 4 centimeters
A parallelogram with sides 3 centimeters and 5 centimeters
questions.answer: A rhombus with angles of 60 degrees and 120 degrees
questions.solution: We need a shape with four equal sides that is not a square. A rhombus with no right angles is one. The other shapes either do not have four equal sides, or are squares.

solve.answer: A rhombus with angles of 60 degrees and 120 degrees
solve.work: A rhombus with 60 and 120 degree angles has four equal sides but no right angles, so it is not a square. Rectangle 4x6 and parallelogram 3x5 do not have equal sides; a square agrees with Sam.

questions.skill: Count shapes that always have an attribute
questions.stem: Look at these four shapes: square, rectangle, rhombus, parallelogram. How many of them ALWAYS have four sides of equal length?
questions.solution: A square and a rhombus always have four equal sides. A rectangle and a parallelogram only have equal opposite sides, so they do not always have four equal sides. The answer is 2.

solve.work: Always four equal sides: square and rhombus. Rectangle and parallelogram not always. Count = 2.

questions.skill: Name a quadrilateral from its properties
questions.stem: Which of these four-sided shapes could NOT be called a parallelogram?
choices: A rectangle with sides of 6 cm and 3 cm
A rhombus with 5 cm sides and no right angles
A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides
questions.answer: A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides
questions.solution: A parallelogram needs two pairs of parallel sides. Rectangles, rhombuses and squares all have them. A shape with exactly one pair of parallel sides does not.

solve.answer: A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides
solve.work: Rectangles, squares and rhombuses all have two pairs of parallel sides, so all are parallelograms. A quadrilateral with exactly one pair of parallel sides is not.

questions.skill: Name a quadrilateral from its properties
questions.stem: Which pair of clues is enough to be sure that a quadrilateral is a square?
choices: It has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles
It has 4 equal sides and opposite sides parallel
It has 4 right angles and opposite sides equal
It has opposite sides parallel and opposite sides equal
questions.answer: It has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles
questions.solution: Four equal sides and four right angles together describe a square. The other pairs also fit shapes that are not squares: a rhombus, a rectangle and a parallelogram.

solve.answer: It has 4 equal sides and 4 right angles
solve.work: A: 4 equal sides + parallel = rhombus, maybe not square. B: 4 equal sides and 4 right angles = square. C: any parallelogram. D: rectangle, maybe not square. Answer B.

questions.skill: Name a quadrilateral from its properties
questions.stem: A quadrilateral has 4 equal sides. Which extra clue would make it a square?
choices: It has two pairs of equal sides
questions.solution: Every shape with four equal sides is a rhombus, and a rhombus already has parallel opposite sides, equal opposite sides and two pairs of equal sides. Only four right angles make it a square.

solve.work: 4 equal sides = rhombus. Opposite sides parallel/equal and two pairs of equal sides are already true of every rhombus. Adding 4 right angles makes it a square.

questions.skill: Name a quadrilateral from its properties
questions.stem: Five quadrilaterals are described. A has 4 right angles and sides of 5, 5, 5 and 5 cm. B has 4 right angles and sides of 6, 2, 6 and 2 cm. C has sides of 4, 4, 4 and 4 cm and no right angles. D has opposite sides parallel, sides of 7, 3, 7 and 3 cm, and no right angles. E has exactly one pair of parallel sides. How many of A, B, C, D and E are parallelograms?
questions.solution: A is a square, B is a rectangle, C is a rhombus (four equal sides) and D has two pairs of parallel sides, so all four are parallelograms. E has only one pair of parallel sides. The answer is 4.

solve.work: A: square, parallelogram. B: rectangle, parallelogram. C: 4 equal sides = rhombus, parallelogram. D: opposite sides parallel = parallelogram. E: exactly one pair = trapezoid, not. Count 4.

questions.skill: Which category fits inside another
questions.stem: In a chart of quadrilaterals, the group of rhombuses and the group of rectangles overlap. Which kind of shape belongs to BOTH groups?
questions.solution: Only a shape with four equal sides and four right angles is in both groups, and that is a square. Parallelograms and quadrilaterals are bigger groups, and a trapezoid is neither a rectangle nor a rhombus.

solve.work: A shape that is both a rhombus (4 equal sides) and a rectangle (4 right angles) is a square. Parallelograms/quadrilaterals are larger groups, not all of which are in both.

questions.skill: Which category fits inside another
questions.stem: Which of these statements is NOT true?
questions.solution: A parallelogram with sides of 7 cm and 4 cm and no right angles is not a rectangle, so "Every parallelogram is a rectangle" is false. The other three are true: squares are rectangles, some parallelograms have four equal sides, and squares are rhombuses that are rectangles.

solve.work: A parallelogram with no right angles is not a rectangle, so A is not true. B (squares), C (rhombuses), D (squares) are true.

questions.skill: Which category fits inside another
questions.stem: Think about four kinds of shapes: squares, rectangles that are not squares, rhombuses that are not squares, and parallelograms that are neither rectangles nor rhombuses. How many of these four kinds are rectangles?
questions.solution: Squares are rectangles, and so are the rectangles that are not squares. Rhombuses that are not squares have no right angles, and the last kind has none either. So 2 of the kinds are rectangles.

solve.work: Squares: rectangles (yes). Rectangles that are not squares: yes. Rhombuses that are not squares: no right angles, not rectangles. Other parallelograms: not rectangles. Count 2.

questions.skill: Which category fits inside another
questions.stem: Rhombuses and rectangles are both groups inside the group of parallelograms. Which shape is a parallelogram but is in NEITHER the group of rhombuses nor the group of rectangles?
choices: A square with sides of 4 cm
A parallelogram with sides of 8 cm and 5 cm and no right angles
A rectangle with sides of 9 cm and 2 cm
A rhombus with 6 cm sides and no right angles
questions.answer: A parallelogram with sides of 8 cm and 5 cm and no right angles
questions.solution: The first shape has sides that are not all equal (so it is not a rhombus) and no right angles (so it is not a rectangle). The other three are squares, rectangles or rhombuses.

solve.answer: A parallelogram with sides of 8 cm and 5 cm and no right angles
solve.work: 9 by 2 rectangle: rectangle. Rhombus: rhombus. Square: both. 8 by 5 with no right angles: parallelogram, sides not all equal (not rhombus), no right angles (not rectangle).

questions.skill: Attributes carry down to subcategories
questions.stem: Tom says: "A square has four equal sides, and a square is a parallelogram, so every parallelogram has four equal sides." Which sentence explains his mistake?
choices: A square is not a kind of parallelogram.
A square does not have four equal sides.
No parallelogram has any equal sides.
What is true of a smaller group is not always true of the bigger group around it.
questions.answer: What is true of a smaller group is not always true of the bigger group around it.
questions.solution: Attributes carry down from a bigger group to a smaller group, not up. A parallelogram with sides of 7 cm and 4 cm shows that parallelograms do not all have four equal sides.

solve.answer: What is true of a smaller group is not always true of the bigger group around it.
solve.work: Attributes pass down to subgroups, not up. Squares are a smaller group inside parallelograms, so a square's four equal sides need not hold for all parallelograms. Option C.

questions.skill: Attributes carry down to subcategories
questions.stem: A hierarchy chart lists each attribute only once, at the biggest group that has it. Parallelograms have 2 listed attributes: two pairs of parallel sides, and opposite sides equal. Rectangles have 1 more listed attribute: four right angles. Rhombuses have 1 more listed attribute: four equal sides. A square is a kind of rectangle and a kind of rhombus. How many attributes does a square have in all?
questions.solution: A square gets the 2 attributes of parallelograms, the extra attribute of rectangles and the extra attribute of rhombuses. That is 2 + 1 + 1 = 4.

solve.issues: Minor: 'how many attributes in all' would be tighter as 'how many of the listed attributes', since a square has other attributes (4 sides) not in the chart described.
solve.work: Square inherits parallelogram's 2 listed attributes, plus rectangle's 1 (right angles) and rhombus's 1 (equal sides): 2 + 1 + 1 = 4.

questions.skill: Attributes carry down to subcategories
questions.stem: Every rhombus has opposite sides that are equal in length. This is because every rhombus is a kind of ____, and every ____ has opposite sides equal in length. Which word fills both blanks?
questions.solution: Every rhombus is a parallelogram, and every parallelogram has opposite sides equal, so the attribute carries down to rhombuses. Not every rhombus is a rectangle or a square, and a trapezoid does not have to have opposite sides equal.

solve.work: Every rhombus is a parallelogram, and every parallelogram has opposite sides equal. Rhombus is not always a rectangle or square; trapezoid is wrong.

questions.skill: Attributes carry down to subcategories
questions.stem: Which list has only attributes that EVERY rhombus has?
choices: Four equal sides; four right angles
Four equal sides; opposite sides parallel
Opposite sides parallel; four right angles
Four right angles; exactly one pair of parallel sides
questions.answer: Four equal sides; opposite sides parallel
questions.solution: Every rhombus has four equal sides and two pairs of parallel sides. A rhombus does not have to have right angles, and it never has exactly one pair of parallel sides.

solve.answer: Four equal sides; opposite sides parallel
solve.work: Every rhombus has 4 equal sides and opposite sides parallel. Right angles not required; exactly one pair parallel is false.

questions.skill: Always, sometimes or never true
questions.stem: Which of these claims can be proven false by finding just ONE shape that breaks it?
choices: All rhombuses have four right angles.
questions.answer: All rhombuses have four right angles.
questions.solution: A slanted rhombus with no right angles is a shape that breaks the first claim. The other claims are true, so no shape can break them.

solve.answer: All rhombuses have four right angles.
solve.work: Only a false 'all' claim is disproved by one counterexample. D is false: a rhombus with no right angles breaks it. A, B, C are true, so nothing breaks them.

questions.skill: Always, sometimes or never true
questions.stem: Tess draws a quadrilateral with 4 equal sides. Tess says it must have four right angles. Dev says it cannot have four right angles. Who is right?
choices: Neither: it might or might not have four right angles.
questions.answer: Neither: it might or might not have four right angles.
questions.solution: A shape with four equal sides is a rhombus. It is a square if it has four right angles, and a slanted rhombus if it does not, so both are possible.

solve.answer: Neither: it might or might not have four right angles.
solve.work: 4 equal sides = rhombus; it may be a square (4 right angles) or not. So neither must nor cannot holds.

questions.skill: Always, sometimes or never true
questions.stem: Read six sentences. (1) A rhombus has opposite sides parallel. (2) A rhombus has 4 right angles. (3) A rectangle has 4 equal sides. (4) A parallelogram has opposite sides equal. (5) A square has 4 equal sides. (6) A rectangle has 4 right angles. How many of the sentences are true for EVERY shape of that kind?
questions.solution: Sentences 1, 4, 5 and 6 are always true. Sentence 2 is false for a slanted rhombus, and sentence 3 is false for a 5 by 3 rectangle. The answer is 4.

solve.work: (1) true. (2) false. (3) false. (4) true. (5) true. (6) true. Count 4.

questions.skill: Always, sometimes or never true
questions.stem: Maria draws every rectangle whose sides are whole numbers of centimeters and whose perimeter is 16 cm. A 1 cm by 7 cm rectangle counts, and a 7 cm by 1 cm rectangle is the same rectangle. How many of her rectangles are NOT squares?
questions.solution: The side pairs that add to 8 are 1 and 7, 2 and 6, 3 and 5, and 4 and 4. That is 4 rectangles. Only the 4 by 4 rectangle is a square, so 3 are not squares.

solve.work: Perimeter 16: length + width = 8. Whole-number pairs: 1x7, 2x6, 3x5, 4x4. Squares: 4x4. Not squares: 3.

questions.skill: Use attributes to find a measurement
questions.stem: A quadrilateral is both a rectangle and a rhombus. Its perimeter is 52 cm. How long is each side, in centimeters?
questions.solution: A shape that is both a rectangle and a rhombus has four right angles and four equal sides, so it is a square. Each side is 52 divided by 4 = 13 cm.

solve.work: Both rectangle and rhombus = square, 4 equal sides: 52 / 4 = 13 cm.

questions.skill: Use attributes to find a measurement
questions.stem: A parallelogram has a perimeter of 64 cm. One pair of opposite sides is 3 times as long as the other pair. How long is each of the longer sides, in centimeters?
questions.solution: If a shorter side is s, a longer side is 3s, and the perimeter is 2 x (s + 3s) = 8s. So 8s = 64 and s = 8. A longer side is 3 x 8 = 24 cm.

solve.work: Opposite sides equal: short + long = 32, long = 3 x short, so 4 x short = 32, short = 8, long = 24 cm.

questions.skill: Count shapes that have an attribute
questions.stem: A box holds 12 cutouts: 3 squares, 2 rectangles that are not squares, 4 rhombuses that are not squares, and 3 parallelograms that are neither rectangles nor rhombuses. How many of the cutouts are parallelograms that are NOT rectangles?
questions.solution: Every cutout is a parallelogram. The squares and the other rectangles (3 + 2 = 5) are rectangles. The rest are not: 4 rhombuses and 3 other parallelograms, which is 4 + 3 = 7.

solve.work: Parallelograms that are not rectangles: rhombuses that are not squares (4) + other parallelograms (3) = 7. Squares and rectangles are rectangles.

questions.skill: Count shapes that have an attribute
questions.stem: Dara draws six quadrilaterals: a square, a rectangle with sides of 9 cm and 5 cm, a rhombus with 7 cm sides and no right angles, a parallelogram with sides of 8 cm and 3 cm and no right angles, a rectangle with sides of 6 cm and 6 cm, and a trapezoid with exactly one pair of parallel sides. How many of the six shapes are squares?
questions.solution: A square has four equal sides and four right angles. The first shape is a square, and the rectangle with sides of 6 cm and 6 cm also has four equal sides and four right angles. The other four are not squares. The answer is 2.

solve.work: Squares: the square, and the 6 by 6 rectangle (4 right angles, 4 equal sides). The 9 by 5 rectangle, rhombus with no right angles, parallelogram and trapezoid are not. 2.

questions.skill: Count shapes that have an attribute
questions.stem: A mosaic has 20 tiles: 5 squares, 7 rectangles that are not squares, 3 rhombuses that are not squares, and the rest are parallelograms that are neither rectangles nor rhombuses. How many tiles do NOT have four equal sides?
questions.solution: The rest are 20 - 5 - 7 - 3 = 5 tiles. Tiles without four equal sides are the 7 rectangles that are not squares and those 5 parallelograms. That is 7 + 5 = 12 tiles.

solve.work: Other parallelograms: 20 - 5 - 7 - 3 = 5. Four equal sides: squares 5 + rhombuses 3 = 8. Not: 20 - 8 = 12 (7 rectangles + 5 parallelograms).

questions.skill: Tell two categories apart
questions.stem: Which single question separates squares from all other rectangles?
choices: Does it have four right angles?
Are opposite sides equal in length?
Are all four sides equal in length?
questions.answer: Are all four sides equal in length?
questions.solution: Every rectangle has four right angles, parallel opposite sides and equal opposite sides. Only a square also has all four sides equal.

solve.answer: Are all four sides equal in length?
solve.work: All rectangles have right angles, equal and parallel opposite sides. Only squares have all four sides equal.

questions.skill: Tell two categories apart
questions.stem: Rectangles and rhombuses have some attributes in common. Which attribute do BOTH always have?
choices: Exactly one pair of parallel sides
questions.solution: Rectangles and rhombuses are both parallelograms, so both always have two pairs of parallel sides. Rectangles need not have equal sides, and rhombuses need not have right angles.

solve.work: Both are parallelograms: two pairs of parallel sides. Right angles only rectangles; equal sides only rhombuses.

questions.skill: Combine clues to identify a shape
questions.stem: Which shape fits all three clues? Clue 1: It is a rectangle. Clue 2: Its perimeter is 20 cm. Clue 3: Its length is 5 cm.
choices: A square with sides of 5 cm
A rectangle with sides of 7 cm and 3 cm
A rectangle with sides of 5 cm and 3 cm
A rhombus with no right angles
questions.answer: A square with sides of 5 cm
questions.solution: A rectangle with perimeter 20 cm has length plus width equal to 10 cm. With length 5 cm the width is 5 cm too, so it is a square. The 7 by 3 rectangle has no 5 cm side, the 5 by 3 rectangle has perimeter 16 cm, and a rhombus with no right angles is not a rectangle.

solve.answer: A square with sides of 5 cm
solve.work: Perimeter 20, length 5: width 10 - 5 = 5, so it is a 5 by 5 square, which is a rectangle. A: perimeter 16. C: length 7. D: not a rectangle.

questions.skill: Combine clues to identify a shape
questions.stem: A mystery shape is a rhombus. Its perimeter is 3 times the perimeter of a square with sides of 4 cm. How long is each side of the rhombus, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The square's perimeter is 4 x 4 = 16 cm. The rhombus's perimeter is 3 x 16 = 48 cm. A rhombus has four equal sides, so each side is 48 divided by 4 = 12 cm.

solve.work: Square perimeter 16; 3 x 16 = 48; rhombus 4 equal sides: 48 / 4 = 12 cm.

questions.skill: Combine clues to identify a shape
questions.stem: A parallelogram has a perimeter of 36 cm, and its sides are not all equal. Which could be its side lengths?
choices: Two sides of 11 cm and two sides of 7 cm
Two sides of 11 cm and two sides of 8 cm
Three sides of 11 cm and one side of 3 cm
questions.answer: Two sides of 11 cm and two sides of 7 cm
questions.solution: Two sides of 11 cm and two of 7 cm have opposite sides equal and total 22 + 14 = 36 cm. Four sides of 9 cm are all equal. Two of 11 and two of 8 total 38 cm. Three sides of 11 and one of 3 total 36 cm but opposite sides are not equal.

solve.answer: Two sides of 11 cm and two sides of 7 cm
solve.work: Opposite sides equal. A: not a parallelogram (three equal, one different). B: 38. C: all equal (excluded). D: 11 + 11 + 7 + 7 = 36.

questions.skill: Combine clues to identify a shape
questions.stem: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are equal in length. A parallelogram-shaped garden bed has two neighboring sides that are each 12 feet long. What is the distance around the garden bed, in feet?
questions.solution: The other two sides are equal to these, so all four sides are 12 feet. The distance around is 4 x 12 = 48 feet. (The bed is a rhombus.)

solve.work: Opposite sides equal and neighbouring sides 12 and 12, so all four sides are 12. Perimeter 4 x 12 = 48.

questions.skill: Reason from the hierarchy
questions.stem: Ravi says: "If a quadrilateral has four equal sides, its opposite sides must be parallel." Which response is correct?
choices: Ravi is wrong, because only squares and rectangles have parallel opposite sides
Ravi is right, because a quadrilateral with four equal sides is always a square
Ravi is right, because a quadrilateral with four equal sides is a rhombus, and every rhombus is a parallelogram
Ravi is wrong, because a rhombus does not have any pair of parallel sides
questions.answer: Ravi is right, because a quadrilateral with four equal sides is a rhombus, and every rhombus is a parallelogram
questions.solution: A quadrilateral with four equal sides is a rhombus, and a rhombus is a kind of parallelogram, so its opposite sides are parallel. It is not always a square, because its angles do not have to be right angles.

solve.answer: Ravi is right, because a quadrilateral with four equal sides is a rhombus, and every rhombus is a parallelogram
solve.work: Four equal sides is a rhombus; a rhombus is a parallelogram, so opposite sides are parallel. Option 1 is wrong reasoning (not always a square).

questions.skill: Count with overlapping groups
questions.stem: A box holds 20 shape cards. Every card shows a rectangle, a rhombus, or both. Squares count as rectangles and as rhombuses. 14 cards show rectangles and 11 cards show rhombuses. How many cards show squares?
questions.solution: A shape that is both a rectangle and a rhombus has 4 right angles and 4 equal sides, so it is a square, and every square is both. Adding 14 + 11 = 25 counts each square twice. There are only 20 cards, so 25 - 20 = 5 cards were counted twice. Those 5 cards show squares.

solve.issues: Mostly an overlapping-sets count (14+11-20); the quadrilateral idea (square = rectangle and rhombus) is used but the main skill is inclusion-exclusion, which may be tricky for Grade 5.
solve.work: Every card is rectangle, rhombus or both; both = square. 14 + 11 - 20 = 5 cards counted twice, i.e. squares.

questions.skill: Combine clues to identify a shape
questions.stem: A quadrilateral is a parallelogram. Which extra clue is enough to be sure that it is a rectangle?
choices: Two sides next to each other are equal in length
One of its angles is a right angle
Its opposite sides are equal in length
questions.answer: One of its angles is a right angle
questions.solution: In a parallelogram, the angle next to a right angle is also a right angle, and then the other two angles must match them. So one right angle makes all four right angles, which is a rectangle. Two equal neighboring sides would make a rhombus. Every parallelogram already has equal opposite sides, and a perimeter alone says nothing about the angles.

solve.answer: One of its angles is a right angle
solve.work: A parallelogram with one right angle has all angles right (opposite equal, consecutive supplementary), so it is a rectangle. Equal neighbours gives a rhombus; opposite sides equal is already true; perimeter tells nothing.

questions.skill: Read a coordinate
questions.stem: The point $(5, 2)$ is plotted on a coordinate plane. How many units above the x-axis is the point?
questions.solution: In $(5, 2)$ the first number says how far right and the second number says how far up. The point is 2 units above the x-axis.

solve.work: y-coordinate is 2, so 2 units above the x-axis.

questions.skill: Name a point reached by moving from the origin
questions.stem: Starting at the origin $(0, 0)$, you move 3 units right and 6 units up. Which ordered pair names where you are?
questions.solution: The first number is the move right (3) and the second is the move up (6), so you are at $(3, 6)$.

solve.work: Right 3 gives x = 3, up 6 gives y = 6: (3, 6).

questions.skill: Points on an axis
questions.stem: Which point is on the y-axis?
questions.solution: A point on the y-axis is 0 units right of it, so its first number is 0. That is $(0, 5)$. The point $(5, 0)$ is on the x-axis.

solve.work: Points on the y-axis have x = 0: (0, 5).

questions.skill: Read the coordinates of a point
questions.stem: The park on a map is at $(3, 8)$. The first number tells how many blocks to move right from the origin, and the second tells how many to move up. How many blocks right of the origin is the park?
questions.solution: In an ordered pair the first number is the x-coordinate, which tells how far right to move. The park is 3 blocks right of the origin.

solve.work: The first number, 3, is the blocks to the right.

questions.skill: Read the coordinates of a point
questions.stem: Mia says the point $(2, 7)$ is 2 units up and 7 units right of the origin. Which statement is correct?
choices: She is correct: it is 2 units up and 7 units right.
It is 2 units right and 7 units up.
It is 7 units right and 7 units up.
It is 2 units right and 2 units up.
questions.answer: It is 2 units right and 7 units up.
questions.solution: The first number, 2, is the x-coordinate, so the point is 2 units right. The second number, 7, is the y-coordinate, so it is 7 units up. Mia mixed up the order.

solve.answer: It is 2 units right and 7 units up.
solve.work: In (2, 7) the x-coordinate 2 means right 2 and the y-coordinate 7 means up 7. Mia has them reversed.

questions.skill: Read the coordinates of a point
questions.stem: Which ordered pair has an x-coordinate of 5 and a y-coordinate of 8?
questions.solution: An ordered pair is written (x-coordinate, y-coordinate). The x-coordinate 5 comes first and the y-coordinate 8 comes second, so the pair is $(5, 8)$.

questions.skill: Plot a point by moving from the origin
questions.stem: A ladybug starts at the origin $(0, 0)$ and crawls 8 units to the right along the x-axis. What is the y-coordinate of the ladybug's new position?
questions.solution: Moving right changes only the x-coordinate. The ladybug is at $(8, 0)$, so its y-coordinate is 0.

solve.work: Moving along the x-axis keeps y = 0; new position (8, 0).

questions.skill: Plot a point by moving from the origin
questions.stem: A drone starts at the origin. It flies 4 units right and then 7 units up. Which ordered pair names where it lands?
questions.solution: Right 4 gives an x-coordinate of 4. Up 7 gives a y-coordinate of 7. The drone lands at $(4, 7)$.

solve.work: Right 4 gives x = 4, up 7 gives y = 7: (4, 7).

questions.skill: Plot a point by moving from the origin
questions.stem: To plot the point $(6, 2)$, you start at the origin. Which directions are correct?
questions.solution: The x-coordinate 6 tells you to move 6 units right. The y-coordinate 2 tells you to move 2 units up.

questions.skill: Points on an axis or on the same line
questions.stem: What is the y-coordinate of every point that is on the x-axis?
questions.solution: A point on the x-axis is not above or below it, so it is 0 units up. Every point on the x-axis has a y-coordinate of 0.

solve.work: Points on the x-axis have y = 0.

questions.skill: Points on an axis or on the same line
questions.stem: Which ordered pair names the origin?
questions.solution: The origin is where the two axes meet. It is 0 units right and 0 units up, so it is $(0, 0)$.

questions.skill: Points on an axis or on the same line
questions.stem: Which point is on the same horizontal line as $(2, 5)$ and is to the right of it?
questions.solution: Points on one horizontal line have the same y-coordinate, 5. Moving right makes the x-coordinate larger, so $(7, 5)$ fits.

solve.work: Same horizontal line means y = 5; to the right means x > 2. Only (7, 5).

questions.skill: Distance along a horizontal or vertical line
questions.stem: Two towns are at $(1, 4)$ and $(7, 4)$ on a map where each unit is 1 mile. How many miles apart are the towns?
questions.solution: The towns have the same y-coordinate, so they are on a horizontal line. The distance is 7 - 1 = 6 miles.

questions.skill: Distance along a horizontal or vertical line
questions.stem: A ladder stands straight up. Its foot is at $(3, 0)$ and its top is at $(3, 9)$ on a plane where each unit is 1 foot. How many feet long is the ladder?
questions.solution: Both points have x-coordinate 3, so they are on a vertical line. The length is 9 - 0 = 9 feet.

questions.skill: Distance along a horizontal or vertical line
questions.stem: The point $(2, 5)$ and a second point are on the same horizontal line. The second point is to the right and 4 units away. Which is the second point?
questions.solution: Staying on a horizontal line keeps the y-coordinate 5. Moving 4 units right makes the x-coordinate 2 + 4 = 6.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter of rectangles on the plane
questions.stem: A square has corners at $(0, 0)$, $(4, 0)$, $(4, 4)$ and $(0, 4)$. What is its area, in square units?
questions.solution: Each side is 4 units long. The area is 4 x 4 = 16 square units.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter of rectangles on the plane
questions.stem: A rectangle has corners at $(2, 1)$, $(8, 1)$, $(8, 3)$ and $(2, 3)$. How long is its longer side, in units?
questions.solution: The bottom side runs from x = 2 to x = 8, which is 6 units. The side that goes up is only 3 - 1 = 2 units. The longer side is 6 units.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter of rectangles on the plane
questions.stem: A rectangle has corners at $(0, 0)$, $(7, 0)$, $(7, 2)$ and $(0, 2)$. What is its area, in square units?
questions.solution: The rectangle is 7 units long and 2 units tall. The area is 7 x 2 = 14 square units.

questions.skill: Find a missing corner of a shape
questions.stem: Three corners of a square are $(2, 2)$, $(6, 2)$ and $(6, 6)$. What is the x-coordinate of the fourth corner?
questions.solution: The fourth corner is above $(2, 2)$ and level with $(6, 6)$, so it is $(2, 6)$. Its x-coordinate is 2.

solve.work: Square of side 4 with corners (2,2), (6,2), (6,6); fourth is (2, 6). x = 2.

questions.skill: Find a missing corner of a shape
questions.stem: The bottom-left corner of a rectangle is at $(3, 4)$ and the rectangle is 5 units wide. What is the x-coordinate of its bottom-right corner?
questions.solution: The bottom-right corner is 5 units to the right of the bottom-left corner, on the same horizontal line. Its x-coordinate is 3 + 5 = 8.

questions.skill: Find a missing corner of a shape
questions.stem: The bottom side of a rectangle runs from $(1, 2)$ to $(6, 2)$. The rectangle is 3 units tall. What is its top-left corner?
questions.solution: The top-left corner is directly above the bottom-left corner $(1, 2)$. Going up 3 gives a y-coordinate of 2 + 3 = 5, so it is $(1, 5)$.

solve.work: Top-left is above the bottom-left (1, 2) by 3: (1, 5).

questions.skill: Move a point and measure a path
questions.stem: A robot is at $(4, 2)$. It moves 3 units up. What is its y-coordinate now?
questions.solution: Moving up adds to the y-coordinate: 2 + 3 = 5.

questions.skill: Move a point and measure a path
questions.stem: A ball is at $(2, 6)$. It rolls 4 units to the right. Where is the ball now?
questions.solution: Moving right adds to the x-coordinate, and the y-coordinate stays the same. 2 + 4 = 6, so the ball is at $(6, 6)$.

questions.skill: Move a point and measure a path
questions.stem: A bee is at $(8, 7)$. It flies 5 units to the left. What is its x-coordinate now?
questions.solution: Moving left subtracts from the x-coordinate: 8 - 5 = 3. The bee is at $(3, 7)$.

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from two number patterns
questions.stem: The ordered pairs $(0, 0)$, $(1, 5)$ and $(2, 10)$ follow a pattern. The next pair has an x-coordinate of 3. What is its y-coordinate?
questions.solution: The y-coordinate goes up by 5 each time: 0, 5, 10, and then 15. The next pair is $(3, 15)$.

solve.work: y goes up 5 when x goes up 1 (y = 5x). x = 3 gives 15.

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from two number patterns
questions.stem: The first pattern is 0, 2, 4, 6. The second pattern is 0, 5, 10, 15. Matching numbers make ordered pairs (first, second). Which ordered pair comes from the third number in each pattern?
questions.solution: The third number in the first pattern is 4 and the third number in the second pattern is 10. The ordered pair is $(4, 10)$.

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from two number patterns
questions.stem: Which ordered pair comes next in the list $(0, 0)$, $(1, 3)$, $(2, 6)$, $(3, 9)$?
questions.solution: The x-coordinates go up by 1 and the y-coordinates go up by 3. The next pair is $(4, 12)$.

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from two number patterns
questions.stem: Pattern A starts at 0 and adds 1 each time. Pattern B starts at 0 and adds 7 each time. Matching numbers make the ordered pairs (A, B). What is the y-coordinate of the pair whose x-coordinate is 4?
questions.solution: Pattern A reaches 4 after 4 steps. Pattern B has added 7 four times, so it is 4 x 7 = 28. The pair is $(4, 28)$.

solve.work: x = 4 is after 4 steps; B = 4 x 7 = 28.

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from a real situation
questions.stem: A baker puts 6 muffins in each box. Let x be the number of boxes and y the number of muffins. Which ordered pair $(x, y)$ matches 3 boxes?
questions.solution: 3 boxes with 6 muffins each is 3 x 6 = 18 muffins. With x first and y second, the pair is $(3, 18)$.

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from a real situation
questions.stem: Raj reads 5 pages each day. A point (day, pages read so far) is plotted for each day. The point for day 4 is $(4, 20)$. What is the y-coordinate of the point for day 6?
questions.solution: Each day adds 5 pages, so after 6 days he has read 6 x 5 = 30 pages. The point is $(6, 30)$.

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from a real situation
questions.stem: A rule says that y is 2 more than x. Which ordered pair follows the rule?
questions.solution: For the pair $(5, 7)$, y = 7 is 2 more than x = 5. The others do not follow the rule.

solve.work: y = x + 2: (5, 7). (5,3) and (7,5) have y 2 less; (5,10) is double.
