questions.skill: Ordered pairs from a real situation
questions.stem: In the point $(7, 21)$, x is the number of bags and y is the number of apples. Each bag holds 3 apples. What does the 21 tell you?
choices: There are 21 apples in each bag.
There are 21 more apples than bags.
questions.solution: The y-coordinate is the number of apples. 7 bags of 3 apples is 7 x 3 = 21 apples in all.

solve.work: y is the number of apples: 7 bags x 3 = 21 apples in all.

questions.skill: Compare the locations of points
questions.stem: Which point is farthest to the right: $(2, 9)$, $(8, 1)$, $(5, 5)$ or $(7, 7)$?
questions.solution: The farther right a point is, the greater its x-coordinate. The x-coordinates are 2, 8, 5 and 7, and 8 is the greatest.

questions.skill: Distance between two points on a vertical line
questions.stem: On a coordinate plane, Point A is at $(2, 3)$ and Point B is at $(2, 9)$. How many units apart are A and B?
questions.solution: Both points have x-coordinate 2, so they are on a vertical line. The distance is $9 - 3 = 6$ units.

questions.skill: Move a point on the coordinate plane
questions.stem: Point P is at $(3, 4)$. Dana moves it 5 units right and 2 units up. What are the new coordinates?
questions.solution: Moving right adds to the first number: $3 + 5 = 8$. Moving up adds to the second number: $4 + 2 = 6$. The new point is $(8, 6)$.

questions.skill: Perimeter of a rectangle from its corners
questions.stem: A rectangle on a coordinate plane has corners at $(1, 1)$, $(6, 1)$, $(6, 4)$ and $(1, 4)$. What is its perimeter, in units?
questions.solution: The width is $6 - 1 = 5$ units and the height is $4 - 1 = 3$ units. The perimeter is $2 \times (5 + 3) = 16$ units.

questions.skill: Read the coordinates of a point
questions.stem: Point A is at $(4, 6)$ and point B is at $(9, 2)$. How many units farther from the y-axis is B than A?
questions.solution: The distance from the y-axis is the x-coordinate. B is 9 units from it and A is 4 units, so B is 9 - 4 = 5 units farther.

solve.work: Distance from the y-axis is the x-coordinate: B 9, A 4. 9 - 4 = 5.

questions.skill: Read the coordinates of a point
questions.stem: A point is 6 units from the y-axis and 10 units from the x-axis. What are its coordinates?
questions.solution: The distance from the y-axis is the x-coordinate, which is 6. The distance from the x-axis is the y-coordinate, which is 10. The point is $(6, 10)$.

solve.work: 6 from the y-axis means x = 6; 10 from the x-axis means y = 10. (6, 10).

questions.skill: Read the coordinates of a point
questions.stem: A point is 7 units from the y-axis and 3 units from the x-axis. What is the sum of its x-coordinate and its y-coordinate?
questions.solution: The point is $(7, 3)$ because the distance from the y-axis is the x-coordinate. The sum is 7 + 3 = 10.

solve.work: x = 7 (distance from y-axis), y = 3 (distance from x-axis). 7 + 3 = 10.

questions.skill: Plot a point by moving from the origin
questions.stem: A robot starts at the origin. It moves 2 units right, 3 units up, 5 units right, and then 1 unit up. Which ordered pair names where it stops?
questions.solution: Right moves add to the x-coordinate: 2 + 5 = 7. Up moves add to the y-coordinate: 3 + 1 = 4. The robot stops at $(7, 4)$.

questions.skill: Plot a point by moving from the origin
questions.stem: Zoe plots a point by starting at the origin, moving up 7 units, and then moving right 4 units. She writes $(7, 4)$. Which statement is correct?
questions.solution: Moving right 4 makes the x-coordinate 4, and moving up 7 makes the y-coordinate 7. The ordered pair is (x, y), so the point is $(4, 7)$.

solve.work: Up 7 and right 4 means x = 4, y = 7: (4, 7). Zoe reversed them.

questions.skill: Plot a point by moving from the origin
questions.stem: A game piece starts at $(1, 1)$. Each move takes it 2 units right and 3 units up. After 4 moves, what is the y-coordinate of the piece?
questions.solution: Each move adds 3 to the y-coordinate. After 4 moves it has gone up 4 x 3 = 12 units, so the y-coordinate is 1 + 12 = 13.

solve.work: y starts at 1 and gains 3 per move: 1 + 4 x 3 = 13. (Position (9, 13).)

questions.skill: Points on an axis or on the same line
questions.stem: A horizontal line passes through the points $(3, 8)$ and $(11, y)$. What is the value of y?
questions.solution: Every point on a horizontal line has the same y-coordinate. The first point has y-coordinate 8, so y = 8.

solve.work: Points on a horizontal line share their y-coordinate, so y = 8.

questions.skill: Points on an axis or on the same line
questions.stem: Which point is on the same vertical line as $(6, 1)$?
questions.solution: Points on one vertical line have the same x-coordinate. The x-coordinate of $(6, 1)$ is 6, and $(6, 9)$ also has x-coordinate 6.

solve.work: Same vertical line means x = 6. Only (6, 9).

questions.skill: Points on an axis or on the same line
questions.stem: Lena says the point $(0, 6)$ is on the x-axis. Which statement is correct?
choices: She is right, because the point has a 0 in it.
It is on the y-axis, because its x-coordinate is 0.
It is on the x-axis, 6 units from the origin.
questions.answer: It is on the y-axis, because its x-coordinate is 0.
questions.solution: A point with x-coordinate 0 has not moved right at all, so it is on the y-axis, 6 units above the origin. Points on the x-axis have y-coordinate 0.

solve.answer: It is on the y-axis, because its x-coordinate is 0.
solve.work: (0, 6) has x = 0, so it lies on the y-axis, 6 up from the origin.

questions.skill: Distance along a horizontal or vertical line
questions.stem: A sprinter runs along a straight horizontal line from $(3, 6)$ to $(15, 6)$ on a plane where each unit is 1 meter. How many meters does she run?
questions.solution: The y-coordinates match, so find the difference of the x-coordinates: 15 - 3 = 12 meters.

questions.skill: Distance along a horizontal or vertical line
questions.stem: Which pair of points is the farthest apart?
questions.solution: Each pair is on a horizontal or vertical line. The distances are 8, 7, 6 and 5 units. The pair $(1, 5)$ and $(9, 5)$ is 9 - 1 = 8 units apart, the farthest.

questions.skill: Distance along a horizontal or vertical line
questions.stem: Two points are on the same vertical line. One is $(5, 4)$. The other is 9 units above it. What is the y-coordinate of the other point?
questions.solution: Moving up 9 units adds 9 to the y-coordinate: 4 + 9 = 13. The other point is $(5, 13)$.

questions.skill: Distance along a horizontal or vertical line
questions.stem: Point P is at $(11, 4)$. Point Q is on the same horizontal line as P and is 7 units to the left of P. What is the x-coordinate of Q?
questions.solution: Moving 7 units left subtracts 7 from the x-coordinate: 11 - 7 = 4. Q is at $(4, 4)$.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter of rectangles on the plane
questions.stem: A square has corners at $(3, 2)$, $(9, 2)$, $(9, 8)$ and $(3, 8)$. What is its perimeter, in units?
questions.solution: Each side is 9 - 3 = 6 units long. The perimeter is 4 x 6 = 24 units.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter of rectangles on the plane
questions.stem: A rectangular pool has corners at $(2, 1)$, $(12, 1)$, $(12, 6)$ and $(2, 6)$ on a plane where each unit is 1 meter. What is the area of the pool, in square meters?
questions.solution: The pool is 12 - 2 = 10 meters long and 6 - 1 = 5 meters wide. The area is 10 x 5 = 50 square meters.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter of rectangles on the plane
questions.stem: A rectangle has corners at $(2, 2)$, $(9, 2)$, $(9, 5)$ and $(2, 5)$. Which pair of numbers gives its length and width, in units?
questions.solution: The length is 9 - 2 = 7 units and the width is 5 - 2 = 3 units.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter of rectangles on the plane
questions.stem: Which rectangle has a perimeter of 14 units?
questions.solution: The first rectangle is 5 by 2, so its perimeter is 2 x (5 + 2) = 14. The others are 4 by 4 (16), 6 by 3 (18) and 7 by 1 (16).

questions.skill: Find a missing corner of a shape
questions.stem: Three corners of a rectangle are $(2, 1)$, $(7, 1)$ and $(2, 6)$. What is the sum of the coordinates of the fourth corner?
questions.solution: The fourth corner is level with $(2, 6)$ and above $(7, 1)$, so it is $(7, 6)$. The sum of its coordinates is 7 + 6 = 13.

solve.work: Right angle at (2,1) (sides along x and y). Fourth corner (7, 6). 7 + 6 = 13. No other right angle among the three points, so it is unique.

questions.skill: Find a missing corner of a shape
questions.stem: A square has its top-left corner at $(3, 9)$ and each side is 5 units long. What is its bottom-left corner?
questions.solution: The bottom-left corner is directly below the top-left corner. Going down 5 gives a y-coordinate of 9 - 5 = 4, so it is $(3, 4)$.

questions.skill: Find a missing corner of a shape
questions.stem: A rectangle has horizontal and vertical sides. Two opposite corners are $(1, 1)$ and $(7, 5)$. How many units is the top-left corner above the x-axis?
questions.solution: The other two corners are $(1, 5)$ and $(7, 1)$. The top-left corner is $(1, 5)$, which is 5 units above the x-axis.

solve.work: Corners (1,1), (7,1), (7,5), (1,5). Top-left (1, 5), 5 units above the x-axis.

questions.skill: Move a point and measure a path
questions.stem: A game piece moves from $(3, 3)$ to $(3, 10)$. Which describes the move?
questions.solution: The x-coordinate stays 3, so the piece did not move sideways. The y-coordinate went from 3 to 10, which is 7 units up.

solve.work: x unchanged, y from 3 to 10: 7 units up.

questions.skill: Move a point and measure a path
questions.stem: A frog is at $(1, 2)$. It hops 4 units right, then 3 units up, then 2 units left. What is the sum of its x-coordinate and its y-coordinate now?
questions.solution: The x-coordinate is 1 + 4 - 2 = 3. The y-coordinate is 2 + 3 = 5. The frog is at $(3, 5)$, and 3 + 5 = 8.

questions.skill: Move a point and measure a path
questions.stem: A snail crawls from $(1, 1)$ up to $(1, 5)$ and then right to $(6, 5)$. How many more units does it crawl on the second part than on the first part?
questions.solution: The first part is 5 - 1 = 4 units. The second part is 6 - 1 = 5 units. The second part is 5 - 4 = 1 unit longer.

questions.skill: Move a point and measure a path
questions.stem: Pat moves a point from $(5, 9)$ to $(8, 4)$. Which describes the move?
questions.solution: The x-coordinate went from 5 to 8, which is 3 units right. The y-coordinate went from 9 to 4, which is 5 units down.

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from two number patterns
questions.stem: A pattern of ordered pairs is $(1, 4)$, $(2, 5)$, $(3, 6)$, $(4, 7)$. Which rule describes how each y-coordinate is related to its x-coordinate?
questions.solution: In every pair the y-coordinate is 3 greater than the x-coordinate: 1 + 3 = 4, 2 + 3 = 5, and so on.

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from two number patterns
questions.stem: Rule 1 starts at 2 and adds 3 each time: 2, 5, 8, 11. Rule 2 starts at 4 and adds 6 each time: 4, 10, 16, 22. Matching numbers make ordered pairs (Rule 1, Rule 2). What is the y-coordinate of the pair whose x-coordinate is 14?
questions.solution: Continue both rules. Rule 1: 2, 5, 8, 11, 14. Rule 2: 4, 10, 16, 22, 28. The pair is $(14, 28)$, so the y-coordinate is 28. (Each y-coordinate is twice its x-coordinate.)

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from two number patterns
questions.stem: Pattern A starts at 0 and adds 4 each time. Pattern B starts at 0 and adds 10 each time. Matching numbers make ordered pairs (A, B). What is the sum of the x-coordinate and the y-coordinate of the 6th pair, counting $(0, 0)$ as the first pair?
questions.solution: The 6th pair comes after 5 steps. Pattern A is 5 x 4 = 20 and Pattern B is 5 x 10 = 50, so the pair is $(20, 50)$. The sum is 70.

solve.work: 6th pair is after 5 steps: A = 20, B = 50. 20 + 50 = 70.

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from a real situation
questions.stem: A car travels 40 miles each hour. A point (hours, miles) is plotted for each whole number of hours. Which point is on the graph?
questions.solution: In 3 hours the car travels 3 x 40 = 120 miles. With hours first, the point is $(3, 120)$.

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from a real situation
questions.stem: A tank has 10 gallons of water at time 0, and 4 more gallons are added each minute. A point (minutes, gallons) is plotted for each minute. What is the x-coordinate of the point whose y-coordinate is 30?
questions.solution: The tank gained 30 - 10 = 20 gallons. At 4 gallons a minute, that takes 20 / 4 = 5 minutes. The point is $(5, 30)$.

questions.skill: Compare the locations of points
questions.stem: Four points are plotted: $(4, 6)$, $(9, 3)$, $(2, 8)$ and $(7, 5)$. Which point is the second closest to the x-axis?
questions.solution: The distance from the x-axis is the y-coordinate. In order from closest, the y-coordinates are 3, 5, 6 and 8. The second closest is the point with y-coordinate 5, which is $(7, 5)$.

solve.work: Distance from x-axis is y: 6, 3, 8, 5. Closest (9,3), second closest (7,5).

questions.skill: Distance along a path on the coordinate plane
questions.stem: On a coordinate plane, a bug crawls in a straight line from $(2, 3)$ to $(7, 3)$ and then in a straight line to $(7, 9)$. How many units does it crawl in all?
questions.solution: First part: the y-coordinate stays 3, so the distance is $7 - 2 = 5$ units. Second part: the x-coordinate stays 7, so the distance is $9 - 3 = 6$ units. Total: $5 + 6 = 11$ units.

questions.skill: Ordered pairs made from two patterns
questions.stem: Pattern 1 starts at 0 and adds 2. Pattern 2 starts at 0 and adds 6. Matching numbers form ordered pairs (Pattern 1 number, Pattern 2 number), such as $(0, 0)$ and $(2, 6)$. Which ordered pair is also one of these pairs?
questions.solution: Pattern 1: 0, 2, 4, 6. Pattern 2: 0, 6, 12, 18. The third numbers make the pair $(4, 12)$. The pair $(6, 12)$ is wrong because the pair for 6 is $(6, 18)$.

questions.skill: Find the missing corner of a rectangle
questions.stem: Three corners of a rectangle on a coordinate plane are $(2, 2)$, $(8, 2)$ and $(8, 5)$. What are the coordinates of the fourth corner?
questions.solution: The fourth corner is above $(2, 2)$ and left of $(8, 5)$. So it has x-coordinate 2 and y-coordinate 5: $(2, 5)$.

solve.work: Sides are horizontal/vertical. Corners use x in {2,8}, y in {2,5}: missing (2, 5).

questions.skill: Read the coordinates of a point
questions.stem: Point P is at $(12, 4)$ and point Q is at $(4, 12)$. Which statement is true?
choices: P is farther from the y-axis than Q, and Q is farther from the x-axis than P.
P is farther from both axes than Q is.
P and Q are the same distance from the x-axis.
P and Q are the same point.
questions.answer: P is farther from the y-axis than Q, and Q is farther from the x-axis than P.
questions.solution: P has x-coordinate 12 and Q has 4, so P is farther from the y-axis. Q has y-coordinate 12 and P has 4, so Q is farther from the x-axis. They are different points because the order of the numbers matters.

solve.answer: P is farther from the y-axis than Q, and Q is farther from the x-axis than P.
solve.work: P: 12 from y-axis, 4 from x-axis. Q: 4 from y-axis, 12 from x-axis. So P is farther from the y-axis and Q farther from the x-axis. Others false.

questions.skill: Read the coordinates of a point
questions.stem: Point R is plotted so that its x-coordinate is 3 more than its y-coordinate, and the two coordinates add up to 15. What is the x-coordinate of R?
questions.solution: If y is the y-coordinate, x = y + 3, so y + y + 3 = 15. Then 2y = 12 and y = 6, so x = 9. Check: 9 is 3 more than 6, and 9 + 6 = 15.

questions.skill: Plot a point by moving from the origin
questions.stem: A marker starts at $(4, 1)$. It moves right 3 units, then up 5 units, then right 2 units, and then down 4 units. What is the sum of the x-coordinate and the y-coordinate of its final position?
questions.solution: The x-coordinate is 4 + 3 + 2 = 9. The y-coordinate is 1 + 5 - 4 = 2. The final position is $(9, 2)$, and 9 + 2 = 11.

questions.skill: Plot a point by moving from the origin
questions.stem: A frog starts at the origin and makes two jumps. Each jump goes some units right and some units up. Which pair of jumps lands the frog at $(5, 8)$?
choices: Right 3 and up 4, then right 4 and up 2
Right 3 and up 4, then right 2 and up 4
Right 5 and up 4, then right 3 and up 4
Right 4 and up 8, then right 1 and up 1
questions.answer: Right 3 and up 4, then right 2 and up 4
questions.solution: Add the right moves and the up moves separately. 3 + 2 = 5 and 4 + 4 = 8 gives $(5, 8)$. The other pairs of jumps land at $(7, 6)$, $(8, 8)$ and $(5, 9)$.

solve.answer: Right 3 and up 4, then right 2 and up 4
solve.work: Need total right 5 and up 8. A: 3+2 = 5, 4+4 = 8. B: 8, 8. C: 5, 9. D: 7, 6. Only A.

questions.skill: Points on an axis or on the same line
questions.stem: Point A is on the x-axis and point B is on the y-axis. A is 7 units from the origin and B is 4 units from the origin. What is the sum of the x-coordinate of A and the y-coordinate of B?
questions.solution: A is on the x-axis, so it is $(7, 0)$ and its x-coordinate is 7. B is on the y-axis, so it is $(0, 4)$ and its y-coordinate is 4. The sum is 7 + 4 = 11.

solve.work: In the first quadrant A = (7, 0), B = (0, 4). 7 + 4 = 11.

questions.skill: Points on an axis or on the same line
questions.stem: Here are five points: $(0, 7)$, $(7, 0)$, $(0, 0)$, $(5, 5)$ and $(9, 0)$. How many of them are on the x-axis? The origin counts.
questions.solution: A point is on the x-axis when its y-coordinate is 0. That is true for $(7, 0)$, $(0, 0)$ and $(9, 0)$. The answer is 3.

solve.work: On the x-axis means y = 0: (7, 0), (0, 0), (9, 0). That is 3.

questions.skill: Distance along a horizontal or vertical line
questions.stem: Mina walks along a straight vertical path from $(6, 3)$ up to $(6, 15)$. She stops halfway. What is the y-coordinate of the place where she stops?
questions.solution: The path is 15 - 3 = 12 units long, so halfway is 6 units up from the start. The y-coordinate is 3 + 6 = 9.

questions.skill: Distance along a horizontal or vertical line
questions.stem: On a plane where each unit is 1 mile, a runner goes from $(2, 4)$ right to $(10, 4)$. Then she turns around and runs 3 miles back to the left. How many miles from her starting point is she now?
questions.solution: She first goes 10 - 2 = 8 miles right of the start. Then she runs 3 miles back, so she is 8 - 3 = 5 miles from the start.

solve.work: From x = 2 to x = 10 is 8 miles; back 3 to x = 7. Distance from start (2, 4) is 7 - 2 = 5.

questions.skill: Distance along a horizontal or vertical line
questions.stem: Point M is on the same vertical line as $(4, 5)$ and is 9 units from it. M is in the first quadrant (no negative coordinates). Which point is M?
questions.solution: A point on the same vertical line has x-coordinate 4. Moving down 9 from y = 5 would go below the x-axis, so M is 9 units up: 5 + 9 = 14. M is $(4, 14)$.

solve.work: Same vertical line means x = 4; 9 units away gives y = 14 (or -4, excluded). (4, 14).

questions.skill: Area and perimeter of rectangles on the plane
questions.stem: A rectangle has horizontal and vertical sides. One corner is at $(1, 2)$ and the corner opposite it is at $(9, 7)$. What is the perimeter of the rectangle, in units?
questions.solution: The rectangle is 9 - 1 = 8 units wide and 7 - 2 = 5 units tall. The perimeter is 2 x (8 + 5) = 26 units.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter of rectangles on the plane
questions.stem: Rectangle A has corners $(1, 1)$, $(5, 1)$, $(5, 4)$ and $(1, 4)$. Rectangle B has corners $(6, 1)$, $(11, 1)$, $(11, 3)$ and $(6, 3)$. Which statement is true?
choices: Rectangle B has the greater area, by 2 square units.
The two rectangles have the same area.
Rectangle A has the greater area, by 2 square units.
Rectangle A has the greater area, by 4 square units.
questions.answer: Rectangle A has the greater area, by 2 square units.
questions.solution: Rectangle A is 4 by 3, so its area is 12 square units. Rectangle B is 5 by 2, so its area is 10 square units. A is greater by 2. (Both have perimeter 14, but that does not make the areas equal.)

solve.answer: Rectangle A has the greater area, by 2 square units.
solve.work: A: 4 x 3 = 12. B: 5 x 2 = 10. A greater by 2.

questions.skill: Area and perimeter of rectangles on the plane
questions.stem: The bottom side of a rectangle runs from $(2, 2)$ to $(8, 2)$. The area of the rectangle is 24 square units, and the rectangle extends upward from the bottom side. What is the y-coordinate of its top side?
questions.solution: The bottom side is 8 - 2 = 6 units long. The height is 24 divided by 6 = 4 units. The top side is 4 units above y = 2, so its y-coordinate is 6.

questions.skill: Find a missing corner of a shape
questions.stem: Two corners of a square are $(3, 2)$ and $(3, 8)$. They are the ends of one side, and the square lies to the right of that side. What is the x-coordinate of the other two corners?
questions.solution: The side from $(3, 2)$ to $(3, 8)$ is 8 - 2 = 6 units long, so every side is 6 units. The other corners are 6 units to the right, at x = 3 + 6 = 9.

solve.work: Side length 8 - 2 = 6; to the right, x = 3 + 6 = 9.

questions.skill: Find a missing corner of a shape
questions.stem: Which set of points are the four corners of a rectangle whose sides are horizontal and vertical?
questions.solution: The corners of such a rectangle share x-coordinates in pairs and y-coordinates in pairs. Only the first set has two points with y = 1, two with y = 4, two with x = 1 and two with x = 5.

solve.work: Need two x values and two y values each used twice. Only (1,1), (5,1), (5,4), (1,4) works; others have a stray 2 or 4.

questions.skill: Move a point and measure a path
questions.stem: A truck drives from $(0, 2)$ right to $(6, 2)$, then up to $(6, 7)$, then left to $(1, 7)$. On a plane where each unit is 1 mile, how many miles does it drive in all?
questions.solution: The first part is 6 - 0 = 6 miles, the second is 7 - 2 = 5 miles, and the third is 6 - 1 = 5 miles. The total is 6 + 5 + 5 = 16 miles.

questions.skill: Move a point and measure a path
questions.stem: A game character starts at $(2, 8)$. Each turn it moves 2 units right and 1 unit down. After how many turns is it at $(10, 4)$?
questions.solution: The x-coordinate goes from 2 to 10, which is 8 units, at 2 units a turn: 4 turns. Check the y-coordinate: 4 turns down 1 each is 4 units, so 8 - 4 = 4.

solve.work: x: 2 to 10 is 8, at 2 per turn = 4 turns; y: 8 to 4 is 4 down at 1 per turn = 4 turns. Consistent: 4.

questions.skill: Move a point and measure a path
questions.stem: A hiker starts at $(2, 2)$. She walks 5 units right, 4 units up, 5 units left, and 4 units down. On a plane where each unit is 1 kilometer, how many kilometers does she walk in all?
questions.solution: She walks every part, even though she ends where she started. The total is 5 + 4 + 5 + 4 = 18 kilometers.

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from two number patterns
questions.stem: Pattern A starts at 0 and adds 1: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4. Pattern B starts at 1 and adds 2: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. Matching numbers make ordered pairs (A, B). Which ordered pair is NOT one of them?
questions.solution: Matching the numbers gives $(0, 1)$, $(1, 3)$, $(2, 5)$, $(3, 7)$ and $(4, 9)$. The pair $(4, 8)$ is not on the list.

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from two number patterns
questions.stem: Pattern A starts at 0 and adds 3 each time. Pattern B starts at 0 and adds 12 each time. In every ordered pair (A, B) other than $(0, 0)$, how many times as large as the x-coordinate is the y-coordinate?
questions.solution: The pairs are $(3, 12)$, $(6, 24)$, $(9, 36)$ and so on. Each y-coordinate is 12 / 3 = 4 times the x-coordinate.

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from two number patterns
questions.stem: Pattern A starts at 0 and adds 5 each time. Pattern B starts at 0 and adds 15 each time. Matching numbers make ordered pairs (A, B). One of the pairs has a y-coordinate of 90. What is its x-coordinate?
questions.solution: Pattern B reaches 90 after 90 / 15 = 6 steps. In 6 steps Pattern A is 6 x 5 = 30. The pair is $(30, 90)$.

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from two number patterns
questions.stem: Which two rules make the ordered pairs $(0, 0)$, $(2, 10)$, $(4, 20)$, $(6, 30)$?
choices: x starts at 0 and adds 2; y starts at 0 and adds 5
x starts at 0 and adds 10; y starts at 0 and adds 2
x starts at 0 and adds 2; y starts at 0 and adds 10
x starts at 0 and adds 2; y starts at 0 and adds 8
questions.answer: x starts at 0 and adds 2; y starts at 0 and adds 10
questions.solution: The x-coordinates go 0, 2, 4, 6, so x adds 2. The y-coordinates go 0, 10, 20, 30, so y adds 10.

solve.answer: x starts at 0 and adds 2; y starts at 0 and adds 10

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from two number patterns
questions.stem: Pattern A starts at 0 and adds 6 each time. Pattern B starts at 0 and adds 4 each time. Matching numbers make ordered pairs (A, B). What is the y-coordinate of the pair whose x-coordinate is 36?
questions.solution: Pattern A reaches 36 after 36 / 6 = 6 steps. In 6 steps Pattern B is 6 x 4 = 24. The pair is $(36, 24)$.

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from a real situation
questions.stem: Points (week, dollars saved) are plotted: $(1, 6)$, $(2, 12)$, $(3, 18)$. If the pattern continues, in which week do the savings first reach 96 dollars?
questions.solution: The savings grow by 6 dollars each week, so the amount is 6 times the week number. 96 / 6 = 16, so it is week 16.

solve.work: Savings = 6 x week; 96 / 6 = 16. Week 15 is 90, so 16 is first.

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from a real situation
questions.stem: Ava saves 4 dollars each week and Ben saves 7 dollars each week. Both started with nothing. A point (week, dollars) is plotted for each of them each week. In week 6, how many more dollars does Ben have than Ava?
questions.solution: In week 6 Ben has 6 x 7 = 42 dollars and Ava has 6 x 4 = 24 dollars. The difference is 42 - 24 = 18 dollars.

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from a real situation
questions.stem: Points (minutes, gallons) for a filling pool are $(0, 5)$, $(1, 8)$, $(2, 11)$. Which point will also be on the graph if the pattern continues?
questions.solution: The pool starts with 5 gallons and gains 3 gallons each minute. After 5 minutes it holds 5 + 5 x 3 = 20 gallons, so $(5, 20)$ is on the graph. After 4 minutes it would be 17, not 14.

solve.work: y = 5 + 3x. x = 4 gives 17 (not 14); x = 5 gives 20. So (5, 20).

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from a real situation
questions.stem: A taxi charges a flat fee of 3 dollars plus 2 dollars for each mile. A point (miles, cost in dollars) is plotted for each trip. What is the y-coordinate of the point for a 9-mile trip?
questions.solution: The trip costs 2 x 9 = 18 dollars for the miles plus the flat fee of 3 dollars, which is 21 dollars. The point is $(9, 21)$.

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from a real situation
questions.stem: Which situation matches the ordered pairs $(1, 4)$, $(2, 8)$, $(3, 12)$?
choices: x is the number of bags and y is the number of apples, with 4 apples in each bag
x is the number of apples and y is the number of bags, with 4 apples in each bag
x is the number of bags and y is the number of apples, with 3 apples in each bag
x is the number of bags and y is the number of apples, with 4 more apples than bags
questions.answer: x is the number of bags and y is the number of apples, with 4 apples in each bag
questions.solution: Each y-coordinate is 4 times its x-coordinate. That fits x bags holding 4 apples each. The other situations would give pairs such as $(4, 1)$, $(1, 3)$ or $(1, 5)$.

solve.answer: x is the number of bags and y is the number of apples, with 4 apples in each bag
solve.work: y = 4x with x first: x bags, y apples, 4 per bag. 'Apples, bags' reversed would give (4, 1) etc.

questions.skill: Ordered pairs from a real situation
questions.stem: A group buys tickets that cost 4 dollars each. They pay with a 50-dollar bill and get 6 dollars back in change. On a graph of (tickets, cost), what is the x-coordinate of the point for this group?
questions.solution: The group spent 50 - 6 = 44 dollars. At 4 dollars each, they bought 44 / 4 = 11 tickets, so the x-coordinate is 11.

questions.skill: Compare the locations of points
questions.stem: Here are four points: $(3, 8)$, $(6, 2)$, $(9, 5)$ and $(4, 4)$. How many of these points are farther from the x-axis than from the y-axis?
questions.solution: The distance from the x-axis is the y-coordinate, and the distance from the y-axis is the x-coordinate. A point is farther from the x-axis when y is greater than x. That is true only for $(3, 8)$, because 8 is greater than 3. The answer is 1.

solve.work: Need y > x. (3,8) yes; (6,2) no; (9,5) no; (4,4) equal, no. Count 1.

questions.skill: Compare the locations of points
questions.stem: Which point is twice as far from the y-axis as it is from the x-axis?
questions.solution: The distance from the y-axis is x and the distance from the x-axis is y, so we need x to be twice y. Only $(8, 4)$ works: 8 = 2 x 4. The other points have y twice x.

solve.work: Need x = 2y. (8, 4) works; the others have y = 2x.

questions.skill: Convert meters to centimeters
questions.stem: How many centimeters are in 4 meters?
questions.solution: There are 100 centimeters in 1 meter, so in 4 meters there are $4 \times 100 = 400$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Convert feet to inches
questions.stem: How many inches are in 3 feet? (1 foot = 12 inches)
questions.solution: Each foot is 12 inches, so 3 feet is $3 \times 12 = 36$ inches.

questions.skill: Convert gallons to quarts
questions.stem: A bucket holds 5 gallons of water. How many quarts is that? (1 gallon = 4 quarts)
questions.solution: Each gallon is 4 quarts, so 5 gallons is $5 \times 4 = 20$ quarts.

questions.skill: Convert a larger customary unit to a smaller one
questions.stem: A rope is 5 yards long. How many feet long is it? (1 yard = 3 feet)
questions.solution: A yard is 3 feet, so 5 yards is $5 \times 3 = 15$ feet.

questions.skill: Convert a larger customary unit to a smaller one
questions.stem: Sam's dog drinks 3 quarts of water in a day. How many pints is that? (1 quart = 2 pints)
questions.solution: Pints are smaller than quarts, so there are more of them: $3 \times 2 = 6$ pints. Dividing gives 1.5, adding gives 5, and using 4 pints for every quart gives 12.

solve.work: 3 qt x 2 pt/qt = 6 pt. Only option 6 matches.

questions.skill: Convert a larger customary unit to a smaller one
questions.stem: A recipe uses 3 cups of milk. How many fluid ounces of milk is that? (1 cup = 8 fluid ounces)
questions.solution: Each cup is 8 fluid ounces, so 3 cups is $3 \times 8 = 24$ fluid ounces.

solve.work: 3 c x 8 fl oz/c = 24 fl oz.

questions.skill: Convert a larger customary unit to a smaller one
questions.stem: A small truck carries 3 tons of sand. How many pounds of sand is that? (1 ton = 2,000 pounds)
questions.solution: Each ton is 2,000 pounds, so $3 \times 2{,}000 = 6{,}000$ pounds. Adding gives 2,003, and 600 and 60,000 come from slipping on the zeros.

questions.skill: Convert a smaller customary unit to a larger one
questions.stem: A ribbon is 24 inches long. How many feet long is it? (1 foot = 12 inches)
questions.solution: Every 12 inches make 1 foot, so $24 \div 12 = 2$ feet.

questions.skill: Convert a smaller customary unit to a larger one
questions.stem: A box of books weighs 48 ounces. How many pounds is that? (1 pound = 16 ounces)
questions.solution: Every 16 ounces make 1 pound, so $48 \div 16 = 3$ pounds. Subtracting gives 32, adding gives 64, and multiplying gives 768.

questions.skill: Convert a smaller customary unit to a larger one
questions.stem: A farm stand sells 10 pints of berries. How many quarts of berries is that? (1 quart = 2 pints)
questions.solution: Every 2 pints make 1 quart, so $10 \div 2 = 5$ quarts.

questions.skill: Convert a smaller customary unit to a larger one
questions.stem: A rope is 18 feet long. How many yards long is it? (1 yard = 3 feet)
questions.solution: Every 3 feet make 1 yard, so $18 \div 3 = 6$ yards. Subtracting gives 15, adding gives 21, and multiplying gives 54.

questions.skill: Convert metric units of length
questions.stem: A pencil is 15 centimeters long. How many millimeters long is it? (1 centimeter = 10 millimeters)
questions.solution: $15 \times 10 = 150$ millimeters.

questions.skill: Convert metric units of length
questions.stem: Rosa walks 5 kilometers to her grandmother's house. How many meters does she walk? (1 kilometer = 1,000 meters)
questions.solution: $5 \times 1{,}000 = 5{,}000$ meters. The other choices slip on the number of zeros.

questions.skill: Convert metric units of length
questions.stem: A ribbon is 700 centimeters long. How many meters long is it? (1 meter = 100 centimeters)
questions.solution: Every 100 centimeters make 1 meter, so $700 \div 100 = 7$ meters.

questions.skill: Convert metric units of length
questions.stem: A lizard is 90 millimeters long. How many centimeters long is it? (1 centimeter = 10 millimeters)
questions.solution: $90 \div 10 = 9$ centimeters. Multiplying gives 900, subtracting gives 80, and adding gives 100.

questions.skill: Convert metric units of mass and capacity
questions.stem: A bag of rice has a mass of 3 kilograms. What is its mass in grams? (1 kilogram = 1,000 grams)

questions.skill: Convert metric units of mass and capacity
questions.stem: A bottle holds 2 liters of juice. How many milliliters of juice is that? (1 liter = 1,000 milliliters)
questions.solution: $2 \times 1{,}000 = 2{,}000$ milliliters. Adding gives 2,002, and 20 and 200 slip on the zeros.

questions.skill: Convert metric units of mass and capacity
questions.stem: A box of sand has a mass of 4,000 grams. What is its mass in kilograms? (1 kilogram = 1,000 grams)
questions.solution: Every 1,000 grams make 1 kilogram, so $4{,}000 \div 1{,}000 = 4$ kilograms.

questions.skill: Convert metric units of mass and capacity
questions.stem: A tank holds 9,000 milliliters of water. How many liters of water is that? (1 liter = 1,000 milliliters)
questions.solution: $9{,}000 \div 1{,}000 = 9$ liters. The other choices divide by too small or too large a number.

questions.skill: Check that a conversion is reasonable
questions.stem: Sam changes 4 feet to inches. Will the number of inches be greater than 4 or less than 4?
choices: Less than 4, because an inch is shorter than a foot
Greater than 4, because an inch is longer than a foot
Equal to 4, because both units measure length
Greater than 4, because an inch is shorter than a foot
questions.answer: Greater than 4, because an inch is shorter than a foot
questions.solution: An inch is shorter than a foot, so it takes more inches than feet to cover the same length. There will be more than 4 inches (in fact 48).

solve.answer: Greater than 4, because an inch is shorter than a foot
solve.work: Inches are smaller than feet, so it takes more of them: 4 ft = 48 in > 4. Only option 3 has the right result and the right reason.

questions.skill: Check that a conversion is reasonable
questions.stem: Which answer is reasonable for changing 5 meters to centimeters?
questions.solution: A centimeter is much shorter than a meter (100 of them make a meter), so 5 meters is about $5 \times 100 = 500$ centimeters. The other answers are far too small.

solve.work: 5 m x 100 cm/m = 500 cm. "About 500" is the reasonable one.

questions.skill: Check that a conversion is reasonable
questions.stem: Ivy changes 2 liters to milliliters and gets 0.002 milliliters. Why is her answer NOT reasonable?
choices: A milliliter is much smaller than a liter, so there should be many more milliliters than liters
A liter is much smaller than a milliliter, so the answer should be even smaller
Liters cannot be changed to milliliters
Changing units never changes the number
questions.answer: A milliliter is much smaller than a liter, so there should be many more milliliters than liters
questions.solution: A milliliter is a tiny amount, so 2 liters must be a big number of milliliters (2,000). Ivy divided when she should have multiplied.

solve.answer: A milliliter is much smaller than a liter, so there should be many more milliliters than liters
solve.work: 2 L = 2,000 mL. A milliliter is smaller, so the number of mL must be larger than 2, not 0.002.

questions.skill: Compare measurements in different units
questions.stem: Which comparison is true? (1 foot = 12 inches)
questions.solution: 3 feet is $3 \times 12 = 36$ inches, and 36 is greater than 30.

questions.skill: Compare measurements in different units
questions.stem: Which measurement is the greatest? (1 kilogram = 1,000 grams)
questions.solution: 4 kilograms is 4,000 grams. That is more than 3,500, 2,000 and 900 grams. The number 4 looks small only because the unit is large.

solve.work: 4 kg = 4,000 g; compare 4,000, 2,000, 3,500, 900. Greatest is 4 kg.

questions.skill: Compare measurements in different units
questions.stem: Which pair of measurements is equal? (1 foot = 12 inches, 1 yard = 36 inches, 1 gallon = 4 quarts, 1 pound = 16 ounces)
questions.solution: 3 feet is $3 \times 12 = 36$ inches. The others are not equal: 2 yards is 72 inches, 4 quarts is 1 gallon, and 5 pounds is 80 ounces.

solve.work: 4 qt = 1 gal, not 2 gal; 2 yd = 72 in, not 6 in; 5 lb = 80 oz, not 50; 3 ft = 36 in (equal).

questions.skill: Convert measurements given as decimals or fractions
questions.stem: A cord is 2.5 meters long. How many centimeters long is it? (1 meter = 100 centimeters)
questions.solution: $2.5 \times 100 = 250$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Convert measurements given as decimals or fractions
questions.stem: A bottle holds 0.5 liter of water. How many milliliters of water is that? (1 liter = 1,000 milliliters)
questions.solution: Half a liter is half of 1,000 milliliters: $0.5 \times 1{,}000 = 500$ milliliters.

questions.skill: Convert measurements given as decimals or fractions
questions.stem: A board is $\frac{1}{2}$ foot long. How many inches long is it? (1 foot = 12 inches)
questions.solution: Half a foot is half of 12 inches: $\frac{1}{2} \times 12 = 6$ inches.

questions.skill: Convert measurements given as decimals or fractions
questions.stem: A bag of oats has a mass of 1.5 kilograms. What is its mass in grams? (1 kilogram = 1,000 grams)
questions.solution: $1.5 \times 1{,}000 = 1{,}500$ grams: 1,000 grams for the first kilogram and 500 for the half.

questions.skill: Complete a conversion statement
questions.stem: Fill in the blank: 5 feet = ___ inches. (1 foot = 12 inches)
questions.solution: $5 \times 12 = 60$, so 5 feet = 60 inches.

questions.skill: Complete a conversion statement
questions.stem: Which number goes in the blank? 4 meters = ___ centimeters
questions.solution: There are 100 centimeters in each meter, so $4 \times 100 = 400$.

questions.skill: Complete a conversion statement
questions.stem: Fill in the blank: 6 quarts = ___ pints. (1 quart = 2 pints)
questions.solution: $6 \times 2 = 12$, so 6 quarts = 12 pints.

questions.skill: Complete a conversion statement
questions.stem: Which number goes in the blank? 8 kilograms = ___ grams
questions.solution: There are 1,000 grams in each kilogram, so $8 \times 1{,}000 = 8{,}000$.

questions.skill: Convert meters to kilometers
questions.stem: A hiking path is $2{,}400$ meters long. How many kilometers long is it?
questions.solution: There are 1,000 meters in 1 kilometer, so $2{,}400 \div 1{,}000 = 2.4$ kilometers.

questions.skill: Check that a conversion is reasonable
questions.stem: Lena changes 24 inches to feet and gets 288 feet. Why can you tell that her answer is not reasonable?
choices: A foot is shorter than an inch, so there should be more feet than inches.
A foot is longer than an inch, so there should be more feet than inches.
A foot is longer than an inch, so there should be fewer feet than inches.
Feet cannot be changed into inches or the other way around.
questions.answer: A foot is longer than an inch, so there should be fewer feet than inches.
questions.solution: A foot is a longer unit, so it takes fewer feet than inches to measure the same length. 24 inches is $24 \div 12 = 2$ feet, not 288 feet.

solve.answer: A foot is longer than an inch, so there should be fewer feet than inches.
solve.work: 24 inches = 2 feet. A foot is longer than an inch, so the number of feet must be smaller than 24; 288 is what you get by multiplying by 12 instead of dividing.

questions.skill: Convert pounds to ounces
questions.stem: A puppy weighs 7 pounds. How many ounces does the puppy weigh? (1 pound = 16 ounces)
questions.solution: Each pound is 16 ounces, so 7 pounds is $7 \times 16 = 112$ ounces.

questions.skill: Convert a larger customary unit to a smaller one
questions.stem: Marcus ran 3 miles. How many feet did he run? (1 mile = 5,280 feet)
questions.solution: Each mile is 5,280 feet, so $3 \times 5{,}280 = 15{,}840$ feet.

questions.skill: Convert a larger customary unit to a smaller one
questions.stem: A water cooler holds 7 gallons of water. How many cups of water is that? (1 gallon = 16 cups)
questions.solution: $7 \times 16 = 112$ cups. Adding 7 and 16 gives 23, $7 \times 4 = 28$ counts quarts, and $7 \times 8 = 56$ counts pints, not cups.

questions.skill: Convert a larger customary unit to a smaller one
questions.stem: A banner is 6 yards long. How many inches long is it? (1 yard = 36 inches)
questions.solution: Each yard is 36 inches, so $6 \times 36 = 216$ inches.

questions.skill: Convert a smaller customary unit to a larger one
questions.stem: A truck is loaded with 8,000 pounds of gravel. How many tons of gravel is that? (1 ton = 2,000 pounds)
questions.solution: Every 2,000 pounds make 1 ton, so $8{,}000 \div 2{,}000 = 4$ tons.

questions.skill: Convert a smaller customary unit to a larger one
questions.stem: Kai ran 15,840 feet. How many miles is that? (1 mile = 5,280 feet)
questions.solution: $15{,}840 \div 5{,}280 = 3$ miles. Check: $3 \times 5{,}280 = 15{,}840$. Subtracting gives 10,560, adding gives 21,120, and 1,584 divides by 10.

questions.skill: Convert a smaller customary unit to a larger one
questions.stem: A bottle holds 72 fluid ounces of juice. How many cups of juice is that? (1 cup = 8 fluid ounces)
questions.solution: Every 8 fluid ounces make 1 cup, so $72 \div 8 = 9$ cups.

questions.skill: Convert metric units of length
questions.stem: A snail crawls 1,350 millimeters across a garden path. How many centimeters is that?
questions.solution: There are 10 millimeters in each centimeter, so $1{,}350 \div 10 = 135$ centimeters.

solve.work: 1,350 mm / 10 mm/cm = 135 cm (metric fact assumed known).

questions.skill: Convert metric units of length
questions.stem: The school hallway is 45 meters long. How many centimeters long is it?
questions.solution: There are 100 centimeters in each meter, so $45 \times 100 = 4{,}500$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Convert metric units of length
questions.stem: A bike trail is 14 kilometers long. How many meters long is it?
questions.solution: There are 1,000 meters in each kilometer, so $14 \times 1{,}000 = 14{,}000$ meters.

questions.skill: Convert metric units of mass and capacity
questions.stem: A sack of potatoes has a mass of 25 kilograms. What is the mass of the sack in grams?
questions.solution: There are 1,000 grams in each kilogram, so $25 \times 1{,}000 = 25{,}000$ grams.

questions.skill: Convert metric units of mass and capacity
questions.stem: Which amount is equal to 8 liters?
questions.solution: There are 1,000 milliliters in each liter, so 8 liters is $8 \times 1{,}000 = 8{,}000$ milliliters.

questions.skill: Convert metric units of mass and capacity
questions.stem: A large bathtub holds 72,000 milliliters of water. How many liters is that?
questions.solution: There are 1,000 milliliters in each liter, so $72{,}000 \div 1{,}000 = 72$ liters.

questions.skill: Check that a conversion is reasonable
questions.stem: Zoe changes 120 inches to feet. She multiplies 120 by 12 and gets 1,440 feet. What should Zoe do instead? (1 foot = 12 inches)
choices: Multiply 120 by 12, because there are 12 inches in a foot
Add 120 and 12, because she is combining the units
Subtract 12 from 120, because feet are smaller than inches
Divide 120 by 12, because a foot is longer than an inch, so there are fewer feet than inches
questions.answer: Divide 120 by 12, because a foot is longer than an inch, so there are fewer feet than inches
questions.solution: A foot is longer than an inch, so the number of feet must be smaller than 120. $120 \div 12 = 10$ feet.

solve.answer: Divide 120 by 12, because a foot is longer than an inch, so there are fewer feet than inches
solve.work: Going to a larger unit means fewer of them: 120 / 12 = 10 ft. Option 2 says divide, with the right reason.

questions.skill: Check that a conversion is reasonable
questions.stem: Which statement does NOT make sense?
questions.solution: A pound is much heavier than an ounce (16 ounces make a pound), so 3 pounds must be more than 3 ounces: it is 48 ounces. The other three statements are correct.

solve.work: 4 L = 4,000 mL true; 3 lb = 48 oz, not 3 oz (false); 2 yd = 6 ft true; 5 km = 5,000 m true. The one that does not make sense is 3 lb = 3 oz.

questions.skill: Check that a conversion is reasonable
questions.stem: Nora changes 36 inches to feet and gets 432 feet. To check, she changes 432 feet back to inches. How many inches does she get? (1 foot = 12 inches)
questions.solution: $432 \times 12 = 5{,}184$ inches. That is not 36, so 432 feet is wrong. (The right answer is $36 \div 12 = 3$ feet.)

solve.work: 432 ft x 12 in/ft = 5,184 in, which is not 36, showing her answer was wrong.

questions.skill: Check that a conversion is reasonable
questions.stem: A bottle of water holds 500 milliliters. Kim estimates that it holds about 5 liters. Her estimate is how many times as large as the real amount? (1 liter = 1,000 milliliters)
questions.solution: 5 liters is $5 \times 1{,}000 = 5{,}000$ milliliters. Compare with 500 milliliters: $5{,}000 \div 500 = 10$, so her estimate is 10 times too large.

questions.skill: Compare measurements in different units
questions.stem: Three ropes are 2 meters, 150 centimeters and 1,000 millimeters long. Which list puts them in order from shortest to longest?
questions.solution: In centimeters the ropes are 200, 150 and 100. From shortest to longest: 100 (1,000 millimeters), 150, 200 (2 meters).

solve.work: 2 m = 200 cm; 150 cm; 1,000 mm = 100 cm. Shortest to longest: 100, 150, 200 cm = 1,000 mm, 150 cm, 2 m.

questions.skill: Compare measurements in different units
questions.stem: Kai's pencil is 12 centimeters long. Lia's pencil is 100 millimeters long. How many millimeters longer is Kai's pencil? (1 centimeter = 10 millimeters)
questions.solution: Kai's pencil is $12 \times 10 = 120$ millimeters long. Then $120 - 100 = 20$ millimeters longer.

questions.skill: Compare measurements in different units
questions.stem: A soup recipe needs 2 quarts of milk. Ana has 7 cups of milk. (1 quart = 4 cups) Does Ana have enough milk?
questions.solution: 2 quarts is $2 \times 4 = 8$ cups. Ana has only 7 cups, so she needs $8 - 7 = 1$ more cup.

solve.work: 2 qt x 4 = 8 cups needed; 8 - 7 = 1 more cup.

questions.skill: Two-step conversion problem
questions.stem: Mr. Lee buys 3 boards that are each 8 feet long. How many inches of board does he buy in all? (1 foot = 12 inches)
questions.solution: The boards are $3 \times 8 = 24$ feet in all. Then $24 \times 12 = 288$ inches.

questions.skill: Two-step conversion problem
questions.stem: A recipe uses 2 cups of oil. Sam has 24 fluid ounces of oil. How many fluid ounces of oil will Sam have left after making the recipe? (1 cup = 8 fluid ounces)
questions.solution: 2 cups is $2 \times 8 = 16$ fluid ounces. Sam has $24 - 16 = 8$ fluid ounces left.

solve.work: 2 c = 16 fl oz; 24 - 16 = 8 fl oz left.

questions.skill: Two-step conversion problem
questions.stem: A baker has 4 kilograms of flour and uses 1,500 grams of it. How many grams of flour are left? (1 kilogram = 1,000 grams)
questions.solution: 4 kilograms is 4,000 grams. Then $4{,}000 - 1{,}500 = 2{,}500$ grams. Adding gives 5,500, and 2.5 is the answer in kilograms, not grams.

questions.skill: Two-step conversion problem
questions.stem: Eli walked 2 kilometers in the morning and 850 meters in the afternoon. How many meters did he walk in all? (1 kilometer = 1,000 meters)
questions.solution: 2 kilometers is 2,000 meters. Then $2{,}000 + 850 = 2{,}850$ meters.

questions.skill: Two-step conversion problem
questions.stem: A pitcher holds 3 quarts of lemonade. Each glass holds 1 cup. How many glasses can be filled from a full pitcher? (1 quart = 4 cups)
questions.solution: 3 quarts is $3 \times 4 = 12$ cups, so 12 glasses can be filled. Adding gives 7, dividing gives 0.75, and 4 is just the number of cups in one quart.

questions.skill: Convert measurements given as decimals or fractions
questions.stem: A pot holds $2\frac{1}{2}$ gallons of soup. How many quarts of soup is that? (1 gallon = 4 quarts)
questions.solution: $2\frac{1}{2} \times 4 = 2 \times 4 + \frac{1}{2} \times 4 = 8 + 2 = 10$ quarts.

questions.skill: Convert measurements given as decimals or fractions
questions.stem: A hiking trail is 3.6 kilometers long. How many meters long is it?
questions.solution: There are 1,000 meters in each kilometer, so $3.6 \times 1{,}000 = 3{,}600$ meters.

questions.skill: Convert measurements given as decimals or fractions
questions.stem: A strip of tape is 45 centimeters long. How many meters long is it? (1 meter = 100 centimeters)

questions.skill: Complete a conversion statement
questions.stem: Fill in the blank: ___ feet = 108 inches. (1 foot = 12 inches)
questions.solution: Every 12 inches make 1 foot, so $108 \div 12 = 9$ feet.

questions.skill: Complete a conversion statement
questions.stem: Which number goes in the blank? ___ pints = 9 quarts (1 quart = 2 pints)
questions.solution: Each quart is 2 pints, so 9 quarts is $9 \times 2 = 18$ pints. Dividing gives 4.5, adding gives 11, and using 4 pints per quart gives 36.

questions.skill: Complete a conversion statement
questions.stem: Fill in the blank: 4,500 meters = ___ kilometers
questions.solution: Every 1,000 meters make 1 kilometer, so $4{,}500 \div 1{,}000 = 4.5$ kilometers.

questions.skill: Two-step problem with metric units
questions.stem: A bucket holds 5 liters of water. Jo pours out 1,200 milliliters. How many milliliters of water are left in the bucket?
questions.solution: 5 liters is $5 \times 1{,}000 = 5{,}000$ milliliters. Then $5{,}000 - 1{,}200 = 3{,}800$ milliliters are left.

questions.skill: Compare lengths in different metric units
questions.stem: Which length is the greatest?
questions.solution: Change each to centimeters: 1.5 meters is 150 cm, 190 cm stays 190 cm, 1,800 millimeters is 180 cm, and 0.002 kilometers is 2 meters, which is 200 cm. The greatest is 0.002 kilometers.

solve.work: In meters: 1,800 mm = 1.8 m; 1.5 m; 190 cm = 1.9 m; 0.002 km = 2 m. Greatest is 0.002 km.

questions.skill: Two-step conversion with customary units
questions.stem: A ribbon is 3 yards long. Mia cuts it into pieces that are each 9 inches long. How many pieces does she get? (1 yard = 3 feet and 1 foot = 12 inches)
questions.solution: 3 yards is $3 \times 3 = 9$ feet, which is $9 \times 12 = 108$ inches. Then $108 \div 9 = 12$ pieces.

questions.skill: Convert a larger customary unit to a smaller one
questions.stem: A parcel weighs 4 pounds 6 ounces. What is its weight in ounces? (1 pound = 16 ounces)
questions.solution: The 4 pounds are $4 \times 16 = 64$ ounces. Add the 6 extra ounces: $64 + 6 = 70$ ounces.

questions.skill: Convert a larger customary unit to a smaller one
questions.stem: A road is 7 miles long. How many yards long is it? (1 mile = 1,760 yards)
questions.solution: $7 \times 1{,}760 = 12{,}320$ yards. Adding gives 1,767; using the 5,280 feet in a mile gives 36,960; and 1,232 drops a zero.

questions.skill: Convert a larger customary unit to a smaller one
questions.stem: Which measurement is equal to 9 feet? (1 foot = 12 inches)
questions.solution: Each foot is 12 inches, so 9 feet is $9 \times 12 = 108$ inches. Adding gives 21, multiplying by 3 gives 27, and 1,080 is ten times too large.

questions.skill: Convert a smaller customary unit to a larger one
questions.stem: A strip of cloth is 90 inches long. How many yards long is it? (1 yard = 36 inches)
questions.solution: $90 \div 36 = 2.5$, so the cloth is 2.5 yards long. Check: $2.5 \times 36 = 90$.

solve.work: 90 in / 36 in/yd = 2.5 yd (36 x 2 = 72, remainder 18 = half a yard).

questions.skill: Convert a smaller customary unit to a larger one
questions.stem: A tank holds 28 pints of water. How many gallons of water is that? (1 gallon = 8 pints)
questions.solution: $28 \div 8 = 3.5$ gallons. Ignoring the leftover half gives 3, subtracting gives 20, and multiplying gives 224.

questions.skill: Convert a smaller customary unit to a larger one
questions.stem: Which measurement is equal to 108 inches? (1 foot = 12 inches and 1 yard = 3 feet)
questions.solution: $108 \div 12 = 9$ feet, and $9 \div 3 = 3$ yards. 9 is the number of FEET, so 9 yards stops one step early. 36 and 324 come from dividing or multiplying 108 by 3 only.

questions.skill: Convert metric units of length
questions.stem: A ribbon is 12 meters long. How many millimeters long is it?
questions.solution: There are 1,000 millimeters in a meter (100 centimeters, with 10 millimeters in each), so $12 \times 1{,}000 = 12{,}000$ millimeters.

questions.skill: Convert metric units of length
questions.stem: Which length is equal to 4,000 centimeters?
questions.solution: There are 100 centimeters in a meter, so $4{,}000 \div 100 = 40$ meters. 4 meters and 400 meters slip on the zeros, and 4 kilometers is 4,000 meters.

questions.skill: Convert metric units of length
questions.stem: A metal rod is 6 meters 40 centimeters long. How long is the rod in centimeters?
questions.solution: 6 meters is $6 \times 100 = 600$ centimeters. Add the 40 centimeters: $600 + 40 = 640$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Convert metric units of mass and capacity
questions.stem: A drum holds 45 liters of paint. How many milliliters of paint is that?
questions.solution: $45 \times 1{,}000 = 45{,}000$ milliliters.

questions.skill: Convert metric units of mass and capacity
questions.stem: Which mass is equal to 7,000 grams?
questions.solution: There are 1,000 grams in a kilogram, so $7{,}000 \div 1{,}000 = 7$ kilograms.

questions.skill: Convert metric units of mass and capacity
questions.stem: A parcel has a mass of 3 kilograms 200 grams. What is its mass in grams?
questions.solution: 3 kilograms is 3,000 grams. Add the 200 grams: $3{,}000 + 200 = 3{,}200$ grams.

questions.skill: Check that a conversion is reasonable
questions.stem: Which statement is true?
choices: The number of cups in a jug is greater than the number of fluid ounces in the same jug
The number of feet in a road is greater than the number of inches in the same road
The number of pints in a tank is greater than the number of gallons in the same tank
The number of grams in a bag is less than the number of kilograms in the same bag
questions.answer: The number of pints in a tank is greater than the number of gallons in the same tank
questions.solution: The smaller the unit, the greater the number of them. A pint is smaller than a gallon, so there are more pints. A cup is bigger than a fluid ounce, a foot is bigger than an inch, and a gram is smaller than a kilogram, so the other three statements are backwards.

solve.answer: The number of pints in a tank is greater than the number of gallons in the same tank
solve.work: Grams are smaller than kilograms, so more grams (A false); cups are larger than fl oz, so fewer cups (B false); feet are larger than inches, so fewer feet (C false); pints are smaller than gallons, so more pints (D true).

questions.skill: Check that a conversion is reasonable
questions.stem: Ruth changes 8 kilograms to grams and gets 800 grams. By what number should she multiply her answer to correct it? (1 kilogram = 1,000 grams)
questions.solution: The correct answer is $8 \times 1{,}000 = 8{,}000$ grams. Since $8{,}000 \div 800 = 10$, her answer must be multiplied by 10.

solve.work: Correct: 8 x 1,000 = 8,000 g. 8,000 / 800 = 10, so multiply by 10.

questions.skill: Check that a conversion is reasonable
questions.stem: Dana changes 2 miles to feet and gets 10,560 feet. Marc changes 2 miles to feet and gets 2,640 feet. (1 mile = 5,280 feet) Whose answer is reasonable?
choices: Marc's, because 2 miles should be less than 5,280 feet
Both, because they used the same units
Neither, because miles cannot be changed to feet
Dana's, because 2 miles should be more than 5,280 feet
questions.answer: Dana's, because 2 miles should be more than 5,280 feet
questions.solution: One mile is 5,280 feet, so 2 miles must be more than 5,280 feet. Dana's 10,560 feet is $2 \times 5{,}280$. Marc divided instead of multiplying.

solve.answer: Dana's, because 2 miles should be more than 5,280 feet
solve.work: 2 mi = 2 x 5,280 = 10,560 ft. Dana is right; 2 miles must be more than 1 mile = 5,280 ft, so 2,640 is too small.

questions.skill: Compare measurements in different units
questions.stem: Three boards are 2 yards, 5 feet and 70 inches long. Which list puts them in order from longest to shortest? (1 yard = 3 feet, 1 foot = 12 inches)
questions.solution: In inches the boards are $2 \times 36 = 72$, $5 \times 12 = 60$ and 70. From longest to shortest: 72 (2 yards), 70, 60 (5 feet).

solve.work: 2 yd = 6 ft = 72 in; 5 ft = 60 in; 70 in. Longest to shortest: 72, 70, 60 = 2 yd, 70 in, 5 ft.

questions.skill: Compare measurements in different units
questions.stem: Three ribbons are 1.2 meters, 130 centimeters and 1,050 millimeters long. How long is the longest ribbon, in centimeters?
questions.solution: In centimeters the ribbons are 120 (1.2 meters), 130 and 105 (1,050 millimeters). The longest is 130 centimeters.

solve.work: 1.2 m = 120 cm; 130 cm; 1,050 mm = 105 cm. Longest is 130 cm.

questions.skill: Compare measurements in different units
questions.stem: Jules has 3 pounds of flour and 40 ounces of sugar. How many more ounces of flour than sugar does he have? (1 pound = 16 ounces)
questions.solution: 3 pounds of flour is $3 \times 16 = 48$ ounces. Then $48 - 40 = 8$ more ounces of flour.

questions.skill: Compare measurements in different units
questions.stem: Mia says 5 liters is less than 4,500 milliliters because 5 is less than 4,500. (1 liter = 1,000 milliliters) Which statement is true?
choices: Mia is right, because 5 is less than 4,500
Mia is right, because 5 liters is 500 milliliters
The two amounts are equal, because 5 liters is 4,500 milliliters
Mia is wrong, because 5 liters is 5,000 milliliters, which is more than 4,500 milliliters
questions.answer: Mia is wrong, because 5 liters is 5,000 milliliters, which is more than 4,500 milliliters
questions.solution: The numbers cannot be compared until the units match. 5 liters is $5 \times 1{,}000 = 5{,}000$ milliliters, and 5,000 is more than 4,500.

solve.answer: Mia is wrong, because 5 liters is 5,000 milliliters, which is more than 4,500 milliliters
solve.work: 5 L = 5,000 mL > 4,500 mL, so Mia is wrong.

questions.skill: Two-step conversion problem
questions.stem: A rope is 5 meters long. It is cut into pieces that are each 25 centimeters long. How many pieces are there? (1 meter = 100 centimeters)
questions.solution: 5 meters is $5 \times 100 = 500$ centimeters. Then $500 \div 25 = 20$ pieces.

questions.skill: Two-step conversion problem
questions.stem: A tank holds 5 gallons of water. How many 1-pint bottles can be filled from a full tank? (1 gallon = 4 quarts and 1 quart = 2 pints)
questions.solution: 5 gallons is $5 \times 4 = 20$ quarts, and 20 quarts is $20 \times 2 = 40$ pints, so 40 bottles can be filled.

solve.work: 5 gal x 4 = 20 qt; 20 x 2 = 40 pt = 40 bottles.

questions.skill: Two-step conversion problem
questions.stem: A recipe needs 3 cups of milk and 8 fluid ounces of cream. How many fluid ounces of liquid does it need in all? (1 cup = 8 fluid ounces)
questions.solution: 3 cups is $3 \times 8 = 24$ fluid ounces. Add the cream: $24 + 8 = 32$. Adding 3 and 8 gives 11, and 24 forgets the cream.

solve.work: 3 c x 8 = 24 fl oz; 24 + 8 = 32 fl oz.

questions.skill: Two-step conversion problem
questions.stem: Dina swims 8 laps of a 50-meter pool. How many kilometers does she swim? (1 kilometer = 1,000 meters)
questions.solution: 8 laps is $8 \times 50 = 400$ meters. Then $400 \div 1{,}000 = 0.4$ kilometer.

questions.skill: Two-step conversion problem
questions.stem: Nick pours a 2-liter bottle of juice into cups that each hold 250 milliliters. How many cups can he fill? (1 liter = 1,000 milliliters)
questions.solution: 2 liters is 2,000 milliliters. Then $2{,}000 \div 250 = 8$ cups. Multiplying 2 by 250 gives 500, and adding gives 252.

questions.skill: Convert measurements given as decimals or fractions
questions.stem: A curtain is $2\frac{3}{4}$ feet long. How many inches long is it? (1 foot = 12 inches)
questions.solution: $2 \times 12 = 24$ and $\frac{3}{4} \times 12 = 9$, so the curtain is $24 + 9 = 33$ inches long.

questions.skill: Convert measurements given as decimals or fractions
questions.stem: Which mass is equal to 0.35 kilogram?
questions.solution: There are 1,000 grams in a kilogram, so $0.35 \times 1{,}000 = 350$ grams.

questions.skill: Convert measurements given as decimals or fractions
questions.stem: A string is 0.065 kilometer long. How many meters long is it?
questions.solution: There are 1,000 meters in each kilometer, so $0.065 \times 1{,}000 = 65$ meters.

questions.skill: Complete a conversion statement
questions.stem: Fill in the blank: 3 yards = ___ inches. (1 yard = 3 feet and 1 foot = 12 inches)
questions.solution: 3 yards is $3 \times 3 = 9$ feet, and 9 feet is $9 \times 12 = 108$ inches.

questions.skill: Complete a conversion statement
questions.stem: Which statement is NOT true?
questions.solution: There are 4 quarts in a gallon, not 8. The other three statements are correct.

solve.work: 1 m = 1,000 mm true; 1 lb = 16 oz true; 1 gal = 4 qt, so 1 gal = 8 qt is NOT true; 1 km = 1,000 m true.

questions.skill: Complete a conversion statement
questions.stem: There are 2,000 pounds in 1 ton and 16 ounces in 1 pound. How many ounces are in 1 ton?
questions.solution: Each of the 2,000 pounds is 16 ounces, so 1 ton is $2{,}000 \times 16 = 32{,}000$ ounces.

questions.skill: Count unit cubes in a rectangular prism
questions.stem: A rectangular prism is built from unit cubes. It is 4 cubes long, 3 cubes wide and 2 cubes tall. How many unit cubes make the prism?
questions.solution: One layer has $4 \times 3 = 12$ cubes. There are 2 layers, so $12 \times 2 = 24$ cubes.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism from its dimensions
questions.stem: A box is 5 centimeters long, 2 centimeters wide and 3 centimeters tall. What is its volume, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: Volume = length $\times$ width $\times$ height $= 5 \times 2 \times 3 = 30$ cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume of a cube
questions.stem: A cube has edges that are each 4 inches long. What is its volume, in cubic inches?
questions.solution: All three dimensions are 4 inches: $4 \times 4 \times 4 = 64$ cubic inches.

questions.skill: Understand volume and cubic units
questions.stem: Each unit cube has a volume of 1 cubic unit. A solid is made from 18 unit cubes with no gaps. What is the volume of the solid, in cubic units?
questions.solution: Each cube is 1 cubic unit, so 18 cubes make 18 cubic units.

solve.work: 18 unit cubes, each 1 cubic unit, no gaps: 18 cubic units.

questions.skill: Understand volume and cubic units
questions.stem: Mia wants to know how much space is inside a box. Which unit should she use?
questions.solution: The space inside a solid is its volume, and volume is counted in cubic units, such as cubic centimeters. Centimeters measure length and square centimeters measure area.

solve.work: Space inside a box is volume, measured in cubic units: cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Understand volume and cubic units
questions.stem: Which problem is about volume?
choices: Finding how much fence goes around a garden
Finding how much carpet covers a floor
Finding how far it is to school
Finding how much sand fills a sandbox
questions.answer: Finding how much sand fills a sandbox
questions.solution: Volume tells how much space a solid takes up. The fence is a perimeter, the carpet is an area and the distance to school is a length.

solve.answer: Finding how much sand fills a sandbox
solve.work: Carpet = area, fence = perimeter, distance = length; sand filling a sandbox = volume.

questions.skill: Understand volume and cubic units
questions.stem: Jo stacks unit cubes to make a solid that is 5 cubes long, 2 cubes wide and 1 cube tall. What is its volume, in cubic units?
questions.solution: There is one layer of $5 \times 2 = 10$ cubes, so the volume is 10 cubic units.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism from length, width and height
questions.stem: A box is 3 inches long, 2 inches wide and 4 inches tall. What is its volume, in cubic inches?
questions.solution: $V = 3 \times 2 \times 4 = 24$ cubic inches.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism from length, width and height
questions.stem: A wooden block is 6 centimeters long, 3 centimeters wide and 2 centimeters tall. What is its volume, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: $V = 6 \times 3 \times 2 = 36$ cubic centimeters. Adding the three numbers gives 11, leaving out the height gives 18, and leaving out the width gives 12.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism from length, width and height
questions.stem: A rectangular prism has a length of 8 meters, a width of 2 meters and a height of 1 meter. What is its volume, in cubic meters?
questions.solution: $V = 8 \times 2 \times 1 = 16$ cubic meters.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism from length, width and height
questions.stem: A rectangular prism has a length of 7, a width of 3 and a height of 2. Which expression gives its volume?
questions.solution: The volume is length times width times height: $7 \times 3 \times 2 = 42$.

solve.work: V = l x w x h = 7 x 3 x 2.

questions.skill: Volume from the area of the base and the height
questions.stem: The base of a prism has an area of 10 square centimeters. The prism is 4 centimeters tall. What is its volume, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: $V = B \times h = 10 \times 4 = 40$ cubic centimeters.

solve.work: V = B x h = 10 x 4 = 40 cubic cm.

questions.skill: Volume from the area of the base and the height
questions.stem: The base of a prism has an area of $B$ square units, and the prism has a height of $h$ units. Which expression gives its volume?
questions.solution: The base area tells how many unit cubes make one layer, and the height tells how many layers there are, so the volume is $B \times h$.

questions.skill: Volume from the area of the base and the height
questions.stem: A closet has a floor with an area of 6 square meters. The closet is 3 meters tall. What is the volume of the closet, in cubic meters?
questions.solution: $V = 6 \times 3 = 18$ cubic meters.

questions.skill: Volume from the area of the base and the height
questions.stem: A cereal box stands on a base with an area of 30 square inches. The box is 10 inches tall. What is its volume, in cubic inches?
questions.solution: $V = 30 \times 10 = 300$ cubic inches. Adding gives 40, and dividing gives 3.

questions.skill: Find a missing dimension from the volume
questions.stem: A box has a volume of 30 cubic centimeters. Its base has an area of 10 square centimeters. How tall is the box, in centimeters?
questions.solution: $V = B \times h$, so $h = 30 \div 10 = 3$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Find a missing dimension from the volume
questions.stem: A prism has a volume of 48 cubic inches. It is 6 inches long and 4 inches wide. How tall is it, in inches?
questions.solution: The base area is $6 \times 4 = 24$ square inches, so the height is $48 \div 24 = 2$ inches. Dividing by only one side gives 8 or 12.

questions.skill: Find a missing dimension from the volume
questions.stem: A prism is filled with 40 unit cubes. It is 5 cubes long and 4 cubes wide. How many cubes tall is it?
questions.solution: One layer has $5 \times 4 = 20$ cubes, so there are $40 \div 20 = 2$ layers. The prism is 2 cubes tall.

questions.skill: Find a missing dimension from the volume
questions.stem: A prism has a volume of 18 cubic inches. Its base is 3 inches long and 3 inches wide. How tall is the prism, in inches?
questions.solution: The base area is $3 \times 3 = 9$ square inches, so the height is $18 \div 9 = 2$ inches. Dividing by 3 only gives 6, and 9 is the base area.

questions.skill: Volume of a composite solid
questions.stem: A solid is made of two parts. One part has a volume of 12 cubic centimeters and the other part has a volume of 9 cubic centimeters. What is the volume of the whole solid, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: Add the volumes of the parts: $12 + 9 = 21$ cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume of a composite solid
questions.stem: A toy is made by joining two blocks. One block is 2 cm by 2 cm by 2 cm. The other block is 3 cm by 2 cm by 1 cm. What is the volume of the whole toy, in cubic centimeters?
questions.solution: The first block is $2 \times 2 \times 2 = 8$ and the second is $3 \times 2 \times 1 = 6$. Together: $8 + 6 = 14$. Multiplying the two volumes gives 48.

questions.skill: Volume of a composite solid
questions.stem: A step is made of two blocks. The bottom block is 4 feet long, 3 feet wide and 1 foot tall. The top block is 2 feet long, 3 feet wide and 1 foot tall. What is the volume of the step, in cubic feet?
questions.solution: The bottom block is $4 \times 3 \times 1 = 12$ and the top block is $2 \times 3 \times 1 = 6$. Together: $12 + 6 = 18$ cubic feet.

questions.skill: Volume of a composite solid
questions.stem: One block holds 20 unit cubes and another block holds 14 unit cubes. They are joined with no gaps and no overlap. How many unit cubes make the whole solid?
questions.solution: The cubes of the two blocks add up: $20 + 14 = 34$ unit cubes.

questions.skill: Pack a box with unit cubes in layers
questions.stem: A box is 4 inches long and 3 inches wide. One layer of 1-inch cubes covers the bottom of the box exactly. How many cubes are in the layer?
questions.solution: The layer is 4 cubes long and 3 cubes wide: $4 \times 3 = 12$ cubes.

questions.skill: Pack a box with unit cubes in layers
questions.stem: The bottom layer of a box holds 15 unit cubes. The box is filled with 2 layers of cubes. How many unit cubes fill the box?
questions.solution: Two layers of 15 cubes: $15 \times 2 = 30$ cubes. Adding gives 17 and subtracting gives 13.

questions.skill: Pack a box with unit cubes in layers
questions.stem: Ravi builds a prism from unit cubes. It has 4 layers. Each layer is 2 cubes by 3 cubes. How many unit cubes does he use?
questions.solution: Each layer has $2 \times 3 = 6$ cubes. Four layers have $4 \times 6 = 24$ cubes.

questions.skill: Volume in a real-world problem
questions.stem: A fish tank is 20 inches long, 10 inches wide and 10 inches tall. How many cubic inches of water does it hold when it is full to the top?
questions.solution: $20 \times 10 \times 10 = 2{,}000$ cubic inches.

questions.skill: Volume in a real-world problem
questions.stem: A rectangular pool is 5 meters long, 4 meters wide and 2 meters deep. How much water does it hold when it is full, in cubic meters?
questions.solution: $5 \times 4 \times 2 = 40$ cubic meters. Adding gives 11, and leaving out the depth gives 20.

questions.skill: Volume in a real-world problem
questions.stem: A bin for storing dirt is 3 feet long, 2 feet wide and 2 feet deep. How many cubic feet of dirt fill the bin?
questions.solution: $3 \times 2 \times 2 = 12$ cubic feet.

questions.skill: Volume in a real-world problem
questions.stem: A lunch box is 8 inches long, 5 inches wide and 2 inches tall. How many cubic inches of space are inside it?
questions.solution: $8 \times 5 \times 2 = 80$ cubic inches. Adding gives 15, and 40 and 10 leave out one measurement.

questions.skill: Compare volumes and see how volume changes
questions.stem: Box A is 5 cm long, 2 cm wide and 2 cm tall. Box B is 3 cm long, 3 cm wide and 2 cm tall. Which box has the greater volume?
questions.solution: Box A: $5 \times 2 \times 2 = 20$ cubic centimeters. Box B: $3 \times 3 \times 2 = 18$. Box A is greater.

questions.skill: Compare volumes and see how volume changes
questions.stem: A prism has a volume of 12 cubic units. A second prism holds exactly twice as many unit cubes as the first. What is the volume of the second prism, in cubic units?
questions.solution: Twice as many unit cubes means twice the volume: $12 \times 2 = 24$ cubic units.

solve.work: Twice as many unit cubes: 2 x 12 = 24 cubic units.

questions.skill: Compare volumes and see how volume changes
questions.stem: Prism P is 4 cm long, 3 cm wide and 2 cm tall. Prism Q has a volume of 20 cubic centimeters. How many more cubic centimeters is the volume of Prism P than the volume of Prism Q?
questions.solution: Prism P has volume $4 \times 3 \times 2 = 24$ cubic centimeters. Then $24 - 20 = 4$ more cubic centimeters.

questions.skill: Volume from the area of the base and the height
questions.stem: The base of a rectangular prism has an area of 18 square meters. The prism is 6 meters tall. What is its volume, in cubic meters?
questions.solution: Volume = area of the base $\times$ height $= 18 \times 6 = 108$ cubic meters.

solve.work: V = B x h = 18 x 6 = 108 cubic m.

questions.skill: Find a missing dimension from the volume
questions.stem: A rectangular prism has a volume of 240 cubic centimeters. Its length is 8 centimeters and its width is 5 centimeters. How tall is it, in centimeters?
questions.solution: The base area is $8 \times 5 = 40$ square centimeters. Since volume = base area $\times$ height, the height is $240 \div 40 = 6$ centimeters.

questions.skill: Pack a box with unit cubes in layers
questions.stem: Mia covers the bottom of a box with one layer of 1-inch cubes. The layer has 5 rows with 8 cubes in each row. The box is 4 inches tall. How many 1-inch cubes does it take to fill the box?
questions.solution: One layer has $5 \times 8 = 40$ cubes. The box is 4 inches tall, so it holds 4 layers: $40 \times 4 = 160$ cubes.

solve.work: One layer: 5 x 8 = 40 cubes. 4 inches tall -> 4 layers: 40 x 4 = 160.

questions.skill: Understand volume and cubic units
questions.stem: A solid made of unit cubes has a volume of 40 cubic units. It has 5 layers that are all the same size. How many cubes are in each layer?
questions.solution: The 40 cubes are shared equally among 5 layers: $40 \div 5 = 8$ cubes in each layer.

questions.skill: Understand volume and cubic units
questions.stem: A rectangular prism is built from 1-inch cubes. Its volume is 36 cubic inches. Which could be the number of cubes along its length, width and height?
questions.solution: $4 \times 3 \times 3 = 36$. The others give 48, 54 and 27 cubes.

questions.skill: Understand volume and cubic units
questions.stem: Dana finds that a box measuring 3 meters by 4 meters by 5 meters has a volume of 60 square meters. What should she change?
choices: Write cubic meters instead of square meters
questions.answer: Write cubic meters instead of square meters
questions.solution: $3 \times 4 \times 5 = 60$ is right, but volume is measured in cubic units, so the volume is 60 cubic meters.

solve.answer: Write cubic meters instead of square meters
solve.work: 3 x 4 x 5 = 60 is right; volume is in cubic units, so the unit should be cubic meters.

questions.skill: Understand volume and cubic units
questions.stem: Which statement correctly tells the difference between area and volume?
choices: Area counts the unit cubes that fill a solid, and volume counts the unit squares that cover a flat shape
Area and volume both count unit squares
Area is measured in cubic units, and volume is measured in square units
Area counts the unit squares that cover a flat shape, and volume counts the unit cubes that fill a solid
questions.answer: Area counts the unit squares that cover a flat shape, and volume counts the unit cubes that fill a solid
questions.solution: Area is the number of unit squares that cover a flat shape (square units). Volume is the number of unit cubes that fill a solid (cubic units).

solve.answer: Area counts the unit squares that cover a flat shape, and volume counts the unit cubes that fill a solid
solve.work: Area counts unit squares covering a flat shape; volume counts unit cubes filling a solid. Option D; option C swaps them.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism from length, width and height
questions.stem: A moving box is 12 inches long, 10 inches wide and 8 inches tall. What is its volume, in cubic inches?
questions.solution: $12 \times 10 = 120$, and $120 \times 8 = 960$ cubic inches.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism from length, width and height
questions.stem: A planter box is 9 feet long, 2 feet wide and 3 feet deep. What is its volume, in cubic feet?
questions.solution: $9 \times 2 \times 3 = 54$ cubic feet. Adding gives 14, and leaving out one measurement gives 27 or 18.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism from length, width and height
questions.stem: A cube-shaped storage room has edges that are each 7 meters long. What is its volume, in cubic meters?
questions.solution: All three measurements are 7, so $V = 7 \times 7 \times 7 = 343$ cubic meters.

questions.skill: Volume of a rectangular prism from length, width and height
questions.stem: A cereal box is 8 inches long, 3 inches wide and 12 inches tall. What is its volume, in cubic inches?
questions.solution: $8 \times 3 = 24$, and $24 \times 12 = 288$ cubic inches. The other choices add the numbers (23) or leave one measurement out (96 and 36).

questions.skill: Volume from the area of the base and the height
questions.stem: A prism has a base area of 8 square feet and a height of 5 feet. What is its volume, in cubic feet?
questions.solution: $V = 8 \times 5 = 40$ cubic feet. Adding gives 13, subtracting gives 3, and dividing gives 1.6.

questions.skill: Volume from the area of the base and the height
questions.stem: A tank has a base area of 16 square feet and holds water that is 7 feet deep. How many cubic feet of water does it hold?
questions.solution: The water forms a prism with base area 16 and height 7: $16 \times 7 = 112$ cubic feet.

questions.skill: Volume from the area of the base and the height
questions.stem: A storage tank has a square base that measures 6 meters on each side. The tank is 4 meters tall. What is its volume, in cubic meters?
questions.solution: The base area is $6 \times 6 = 36$ square meters. Then $V = 36 \times 4 = 144$ cubic meters.

solve.work: Base 6 x 6 = 36 sq m; 36 x 4 = 144 cubic m.

questions.skill: Find a missing dimension from the volume
questions.stem: A box has a volume of 24 cubic feet and is 2 feet tall. Which could be its length and its width?
questions.solution: The base area must be $24 \div 2 = 12$ square feet. Only $4 \times 3 = 12$ works; the other pairs give base areas 24, 24 and 9.

solve.work: Base area must be 24 / 2 = 12. 12x2 = 24, 6x4 = 24, 4x3 = 12, 3x3 = 9. Only 4 ft and 3 ft.

questions.skill: Find a missing dimension from the volume
